title: Iliad, Book 2
author: Homer
source_notes: Greek text: Monro & Allen, Oxford Classical Text, via Perseus Digital Library. English: Samuel Butler 1898, via Perseus Digital Library.
reading_notes: Book 2 of the Iliad. 877 lines. Per-line greek with per-line gloss; Samuel Butler's prose translation provided as parallel panel for context.

lines.original: ἄλλοι μέν ῥα θεοί τε καὶ ἀνέρες ἱπποκορυσταὶ
lines.english: Now the other gods and the chariot-fighting warriors
lines.gloss:
**ἄλλοι** (ἄλλος): nominative plural masculine, "the other" or "the rest of"
**θεοί** (θεός): nominative plural masculine, "gods"
**ἀνέρες** (ἀνήρ): nominative plural masculine, "men"
**ἱπποκορυσταί** (ἱπποκορυστής): nominative plural masculine, "horse-taming" or "helmeted warriors"

The line contrasts "the other gods and men" (who slept through the night, per the following verse) with Zeus, establishing the narrative focus on Zeus's sleeplessness.

lines.original: εὗδον παννύχιοι, Δία δʼ οὐκ ἔχε νήδυμος ὕπνος,
lines.english: The other gods and chariot-fighting men slept all night long, but sweet sleep did not hold Zeus.
lines.gloss:
**εὗδον παννύχιοι, Δία δʼ οὐκ ἔχε νήδυμος ὕπνος,**

*εὗδον* (imperf. 3rd pl. of εὕδω): "were sleeping"; *παννύχιοι* (nom. pl. masc. adj.): "all night long"; *Δία* (acc. sg. of Ζεύς): "Zeus" (object); *ἔχε* (imperf. 3rd sg. of ἔχω): "held, possessed"; *νήδυμος* (nom. sg. masc. adj.): "sweet." The gods and warriors slept through the night, but sweet sleep did not take hold of Zeus.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὅ γε μερμήριζε κατὰ φρένα ὡς Ἀχιλῆα
lines.english: but he pondered in his mind how he might honor Achilles
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλʼ ὅ γε μερμήριζε κατὰ φρένα ὡς Ἀχιλῆα**

Key words: **ὅ γε** (pronoun, nominative singular masculine, "he," i.e., Zeus); **μερμήριζε** (verb, 3rd singular imperfect active indicative of μερμηρίζω, "was pondering/deliberating"); **φρένα** (noun, accusative singular of φρήν, "mind/heart"); **Ἀχιλῆα** (proper noun, accusative singular, "Achilles"). Zeus continues sleepless deliberation, pondering in his mind how to honor Achilles (by bringing destruction upon the Achaeans at their ships).

lines.original: τιμήσῃ, ὀλέσῃ δὲ πολέας ἐπὶ νηυσὶν Ἀχαιῶν.
lines.english: he might honor Achilles and destroy many men at the ships of the Achaeans
lines.gloss:
**τιμήσῃ** (3rd sg. aor. subj. act. of τιμάω): "he might honor" (Achilles); **ὀλέσῃ** (3rd sg. aor. subj. act. of ὄλλυμι): "he might destroy"; **πολέας** (acc. pl. masc. of πολύς): "many"; **νηυσί** (dat. pl. of νηῦς): "at the ships"; **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιός): "of the Achaeans." 

Zeus deliberates how to honor Achilles while destroying many Achaeans at their ships—the dual subjunctives express the alternatives of his pondered plan.

lines.original: ἥδε δέ οἱ κατὰ θυμὸν ἀρίστη φαίνετο βουλή,
lines.english: This plan seemed best to his heart.
lines.gloss:
**ἥδε** (pronoun, nom. fem. sg.) "this": demonstrative referring to the following plan.
**κατὰ θυμόν** (prep. + acc.) "in his mind/heart": idiomatic phrase for mental deliberation.
**ἀρίστη** (adj., nom. fem. sg., superlative of ἀγαθός) "best": modifying βουλή.
**φαίνετο** (verb, 3rd sg. impf. mid. of φαίνω) "seemed, appeared": expresses Zeus's judgment.
**βουλή** (noun, nom. fem. sg.) "plan, counsel": the subject, referring to Zeus's decision.

This best plan seemed to him in his mind—namely, to send a destructive dream to Agamemnon.

lines.original: πέμψαι ἐπʼ Ἀτρεΐδῃ Ἀγαμέμνονι οὖλον ὄνειρον·
lines.english: to send a destructive dream to Agamemnon son of Atreus
lines.gloss: **πέμψαι** (aorist active infinitive of πέμπω, "to send") serves as the subject infinitive of φαίνετο in the previous line. **Ἀτρεΐδῃ Ἀγαμέμνονι** (dative singular, "to Agamemnon son of Atreus") is the indirect object indicating the recipient. **οὖλον ὄνειρον** (accusative singular, "baneful dream" or "destructive dream") is the direct object to be sent, with οὖλον emphasizing its malicious nature.

lines.original: καί μιν φωνήσας ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα·
lines.english: And addressing him he spoke winged words.
lines.gloss:
**καί** (conjunction): "and"
**μιν** (pronoun, accusative singular): "him" (the Dream)
**φωνήσας** (participle, aorist active nominative singular, from φωνέω): "addressing, calling to"
**ἔπεα πτερόεντα** (noun + adjective, accusative plural neuter): "winged words," the formulaic expression for speech
**προσηύδα** (verb, imperfect active 3rd singular, from προσαυδάω): "he addressed, spoke to"

Zeus, addressing the Dream, spoke winged words to him.

lines.original: ὣς φάτο, βῆ δʼ ἄρʼ ὄνειρος ἐπεὶ τὸν μῦθον ἄκουσε·
lines.english: So he spoke, and the dream went forth when it heard his command.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): thus, in this way. **φάτο** (verb, 3rd sing. aor. mid. indic. of φημί): he/she spoke. **βῆ** (verb, 3rd sing. aor. indic. of βαίνω): went, departed. **ὄνειρος** (noun, nom. sing.): dream, the Dream (personified). **μῦθον** (noun, acc. sing.): speech, command. **ἄκουσε** (verb, 3rd sing. aor. indic. of ἀκούω): heard.

The Dream departed after hearing Zeus's command, with the introductory "thus he spoke" marking the transition from divine speech to action.

lines.original: καρπαλίμως δʼ ἵκανε θοὰς ἐπὶ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν,
lines.english: He swiftly reached the swift ships of the Achaeans.
lines.gloss: **καρπαλίμως** (adverb): "swiftly," "quickly" – describes the manner of the dream's journey. **ἵκανε** (3rd sing. aor. indic. mid. of ἱκνέομαι): "arrived at," "reached" – the main verb indicating the dream's arrival. **θοάς** (fem. acc. pl. adj.): "swift," modifies νῆας. **νῆας** (fem. acc. pl. of ναῦς): "ships," direct object. **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιοί): "of the Achaeans," possessive genitive modifying ships.

lines.original: βῆ δʼ ἄρʼ ἐπʼ Ἀτρεΐδην Ἀγαμέμνονα· τὸν δὲ κίχανεν
lines.english: He went to Agamemnon son of Atreus and found him
lines.gloss: **βῆ** (3rd sg. aor. of βαίνω): "he went"; **ἐπί** (prep. + acc.): "to, toward"; **Ἀτρεΐδην Ἀγαμέμνονα** (acc. sg.): "Agamemnon son of Atreus," object of motion; **κίχανεν** (3rd sg. aor. of κιχάνω): "he found, came upon." The dream-figure proceeds to Agamemnon and finds him in the state described in the next line.

lines.original: εὕδοντʼ ἐν κλισίῃ, περὶ δʼ ἀμβρόσιος κέχυθʼ ὕπνος.
lines.english: sleeping in his hut, and ambrosial sleep was poured around him.
lines.gloss: **εὕδοντα** (pres. act. participle, acc. sing. masc. of εὕδω): "sleeping"; **ἐν κλισίῃ** (prep. + dat. sing. of κλισίη): "in the hut/tent"; **ἀμβρόσιος** (nom. sing. masc. adj.): "ambrosial, divine"; **κέχυθʼ** (perf. mid./pass. indic. 3rd sing. of χέω): "was poured, spread"; **ὕπνος** (nom. sing. masc.): "sleep." The dream-god finds Agamemnon sleeping in his tent, with divine sleep poured around him.

lines.original: στῆ δʼ ἄρʼ ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς Νηληΐῳ υἷι ἐοικώς
lines.english: He stood above his head in the likeness of Neleus' son.
lines.gloss: **στῆ** (aorist, 3rd sg. of ἵστημι): "stood" or "appeared"; **ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς** (prep. + gen.): "above the head," indicating the dream's position over the sleeping figure; **Νηληΐῳ υἷι** (dat. sg.): "to/for the son of Neleus" (i.e., Nestor); **ἐοικώς** (perf. act. ptc., nom. sg. masc. of ἔοικα): "resembling" or "likening himself to." The dream-figure stations itself above Nestor's head, taking the form of Neleus' son.

lines.original: Νέστορι, τόν ῥα μάλιστα γερόντων τῖʼ Ἀγαμέμνων·
lines.english: to Nestor, whom Agamemnon honored most of all the elders
lines.gloss: **Νέστορι** (dat. sg. masc., "to Nestor") - the addressee in dative case. **τόν** (acc. sg. masc., relative pronoun, "whom") introduces a relative clause. **μάλιστα** (adv., "most of all") modifies the verb **τῖʼ** (3rd sg. imperf. act., τίω, "honored"). **γερόντων** (gen. pl. masc., "of the elders") - partitive genitive with μάλιστα. The dream appears to Nestor, whom Agamemnon honored most among the elders.

lines.original: τῷ μιν ἐεισάμενος προσεφώνεε θεῖος ὄνειρος·
lines.english: Taking his likeness the divine dream addressed him.
lines.gloss:
**Glossary for Iliad line: τῷ μιν ἐεισάμενος προσεφώνεε θεῖος ὄνειρος·**

- **τῷ** (dative singular, demonstrative pronoun): "to him" (referring to Nestor)
- **ἐεισάμενος** (aorist middle participle, nominative singular masculine, from *εἴδομαι*): "likening himself, taking the form of"
- **προσεφώνεε** (imperfect active, 3rd singular, from *προσφωνέω*): "addressed, spoke to"
- **θεῖος** (nominative singular masculine adjective): "divine, heavenly"
- **ὄνειρος** (nominative singular masculine noun): "dream"

The divine dream, taking the form of Nestor,

lines.original: ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας ἀπεβήσετο, τὸν δὲ λίπʼ αὐτοῦ
lines.english: So speaking he departed and left him there pondering in his heart things that were not to be fulfilled.
lines.gloss: ὣς ("thus") is an adverb; ἄρα is a particle marking narrative transition; φωνήσας is the aorist active participle of φωνέω ("having spoken"), nominative singular masculine; ἀπεβήσετο is the third singular aorist middle indicative of ἀποβαίνω ("he departed"); λίπʼ (from λείπω, "left") is the third singular aorist active indicative, with αὐτοῦ ("there, in that place") as an adverb of place. The Dream, having spoken thus, departed and left him there.

lines.original: τὰ φρονέοντʼ ἀνὰ θυμὸν ἅ ῥʼ οὐ τελέεσθαι ἔμελλον·
lines.english: pondering in his heart things that were not to be fulfilled
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** φρονέοντα (pres. act. participle, acc. sg. masc. from φρονέω) "thinking"; θυμόν (acc. sg. masc.) "heart, spirit"; τελέεσθαι (pres. mid./pass. inf. from τελέω) "to be accomplished, fulfilled"; ἔμελλον (imperf. act. 3rd pl. from μέλλω) "were destined, were about to."

Agamemnon is left there "thinking in his heart things which were not destined to be fulfilled," referring to his vain expectation of capturing Troy that very day.

lines.original: φῆ γὰρ ὅ γʼ αἱρήσειν Πριάμου πόλιν ἤματι κείνῳ
lines.english: For he thought he would take Priam's city on that very day.
lines.gloss: **φῆ** (3rd sg. impf. of φημί): "he thought/supposed"; **αἱρήσειν** (fut. inf. of αἱρέω): "to take, capture"; **Πριάμου** (gen. sg. of Πρίαμος): "of Priam"; **πόλιν** (acc. sg.): "city"; **ἤματι κείνῳ** (dat. sg.): "on that day." The line expresses Agamemnon's vain expectation that he would capture Troy on that very day, continuing the theme of his delusion.

lines.original: νήπιος, οὐδὲ τὰ ᾔδη ἅ ῥα Ζεὺς μήδετο ἔργα·
lines.english: The fool, he did not know what deeds Zeus was planning.
lines.gloss: νήπιος (nom. sg. masc. adj.) "fool" or "simple-minded one"; οὐδέ (conj.) "nor, and not"; ᾔδη (3rd sg. pluperfect of οἶδα) "he knew"; μήδετο (3rd sg. impf. mid. of μήδομαι) "was devising, planning"; ἔργα (acc. pl. neut. of ἔργον) "deeds, works." Agamemnon is called a fool for not knowing what works Zeus was planning (the disasters still to come).

lines.original: θήσειν γὰρ ἔτʼ ἔμελλεν ἐπʼ ἄλγεά τε στοναχάς τε
lines.english: For Zeus was yet to bring both pains and groans upon Trojans and Danaans through mighty battles.
lines.gloss: **θήσειν** (fut. act. inf. of τίθημι) "to bring about, cause"; **ἔμελλεν** (3rd sg. impf. of μέλλω) "was destined, was about to"; **ἄλγεά** (acc. pl. neut. of ἄλγος) "pains, griefs"; **στοναχάς** (acc. pl. fem. of στοναχή) "groans, lamentations." Zeus was still destined to bring about both pains and groans, emphasizing the continued suffering he planned for both armies through the unfolding events of the war.

lines.original: Τρωσί τε καὶ Δαναοῖσι διὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας.
lines.english: Upon both Trojans and Danaans through mighty battles.
lines.gloss: **Τρωσί** (dat. pl. of Τρώς) "for the Trojans"; **Δαναοῖσι** (dat. pl. of Δαναός) "for the Danaans/Greeks"; **διά** (prep. + acc.) "through, throughout"; **κρατερὰς** (acc. pl. fem. of κρατερός) "mighty, violent"; **ὑσμίνας** (acc. pl. of ὑσμίνη) "battles, combats." This line specifies that Zeus was destined to bring suffering and groans to both Trojans and Greeks through mighty battles.

lines.original: ἔγρετο δʼ ἐξ ὕπνου, θείη δέ μιν ἀμφέχυτʼ ὀμφή·
lines.english: He awoke from sleep, and the divine voice poured around him.
lines.gloss: **ἔγρετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ἐγείρω) "he awoke"; **ἐξ ὕπνου** (prep. + gen.) "from sleep"; **θείη** (fem. nom. sg. adj.) "divine, god-sent"; **ὀμφή** (nom. sg.) "voice"; **ἀμφέχυτʼ** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἀμφιχέω) "poured around, enveloped." He awoke from sleep, and the divine voice having spoken enveloped him.

lines.original: ἕζετο δʼ ὀρθωθείς, μαλακὸν δʼ ἔνδυνε χιτῶνα
lines.english: He sat up straight and put on his soft tunic.
lines.gloss:
**ἕζετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ἕζομαι): "he sat up"
**ὀρθωθείς** (aor. pass. participle nom. sg. masc. of ὀρθόω): "having raised himself upright"
**μαλακόν** (adj. acc. sg. masc.): "soft"
**ἔνδυνε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of ἐνδύω): "he put on"
**χιτῶνα** (acc. sg. masc.): "tunic"

He sat up, raising himself upright, and put on a soft tunic.

lines.original: καλὸν νηγάτεον, περὶ δὲ μέγα βάλλετο φᾶρος·
lines.english: He put on a beautiful soft tunic and cast a great cloak about him.
lines.gloss: **καλὸν** (adj. acc. sg. neut.) "beautiful" modifies **νηγάτεον** (adj. acc. sg. neut.) "freshly-woven, new-made" describing **φᾶρος** (n. acc. sg. neut.) "cloak." **περὶ** (adv.) "around" and **βάλλετο** (verb 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of βάλλω) "he cast (for himself)" complete the image: "he cast around himself a beautiful new-woven cloak." The line continues the arming/dressing scene with emphasis on the cloak's fine quality.

lines.original: ποσσὶ δʼ ὑπὸ λιπαροῖσιν ἐδήσατο καλὰ πέδιλα,
lines.english: He bound fair sandals beneath his shining feet.
lines.gloss: **ποσσὶ** (dat. pl. of πούς): "on/to his feet" – dative of place where. **λιπαροῖσιν** (dat. pl. adj. of λιπαρός): "shining, sleek" – modifies ποσσί. **ἐδήσατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of δέω): "he bound (for himself)" – middle voice emphasizes personal interest. **καλὰ** (acc. pl. neut. adj. of καλός): "beautiful, fair" – modifies πέδιλα. **πέδιλα** (acc. pl. neut. of πέδιλον): "sandals" – direct object. The line describes the arming scene detail of fastening fine sandals onto shining feet.

lines.original: ἀμφὶ δʼ ἄρʼ ὤμοισιν βάλετο ξίφος ἀργυρόηλον·
lines.english: He cast his silver-studded sword about his shoulders.
lines.gloss:
**ἀμφί** (prep. + dat.): "around" or "upon," governing ὤμοισιν. **ὤμοισιν** (dat. pl. of ὦμος): "shoulders." **βάλετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. of βάλλω): "he cast" or "he put (for himself)." **ξίφος** (acc. sg. neut.): "sword," object of βάλετο. **ἀργυρόηλον** (acc. sg. neut. adj.): "silver-studded" or "with silver nails," modifying ξίφος.

The hero slings his silver-studded sword around his shoulders, completing his arming.

lines.original: εἵλετο δὲ σκῆπτρον πατρώϊον ἄφθιτον αἰεὶ
lines.english: He took up his father's imperishable scepter.
lines.gloss: **εἵλετο** (aorist middle, 3rd singular of αἱρέω): "he took" or "grasped." **σκῆπτρον** (neuter accusative singular): "scepter," object of εἵλετο. **πατρώϊον** (adjective, accusative singular neuter): "ancestral" or "of his fathers," modifying σκῆπτρον. **ἄφθιτον** (adjective, accusative singular neuter): "imperishable" or "undying." **αἰεί** (adverb): "forever" or "always." The priest grasps his ancestral scepter, imperishable forever, as he proceeds to the Achaean ships.

lines.original: σὺν τῷ ἔβη κατὰ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν χαλκοχιτώνων·
lines.english: With it he went among the ships of the bronze-clad Achaeans.
lines.gloss:
**σὺν τῷ ἔβη κατὰ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν χαλκοχιτώνων·**

**σὺν τῷ** (preposition + demonstrative pronoun, dative singular neuter): "with this/it" (referring to the scepter). **ἔβη** (verb, 3rd singular aorist indicative of βαίνω): "he went." **κατὰ νῆας** (preposition + noun, accusative plural): "along/down to the ships." **Ἀχαιῶν** (proper noun, genitive plural): "of the Achaeans." **χαλκοχιτώνων** (compound adjective, genitive plural): "bronze-clad" or "bronze-corseted."

Chryses walks with his ancestral scepter down

lines.original: ἠὼς μέν ῥα θεὰ προσεβήσετο μακρὸν Ὄλυμπον
lines.english: Dawn the goddess went up to tall Olympus.
lines.gloss: **ἠώς** (nom. sg. fem., "Dawn") **μέν** (particle, "on the one hand") **ῥα** (particle, "indeed/then") **θεά** (nom. sg. fem., "goddess") **προσεβήσετο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of προσβαίνω, "went up to/approached") **μακρόν** (acc. sg. masc., "lofty/tall") **Ὄλυμπον** (acc. sg. masc., "Olympus"). The goddess Dawn ascended to lofty Olympus, with **μέν** anticipating a contrasting clause about what happens next on earth.

lines.original: Ζηνὶ φόως ἐρέουσα καὶ ἄλλοις ἀθανάτοισιν·
lines.english: bearing light to Zeus and the other immortals.
lines.gloss: **Ζηνί** (dat. sg. of Ζεύς) "to Zeus"; **φόως** (acc. sg. neut. of φάος) "light, news"; **ἐρέουσα** (fut. part. fem. nom. sg. of εἴρω/ἐρέω) "about to tell, going to announce"; **ἀθανάτοισιν** (dat. pl. masc. of ἀθάνατος) "to the immortals." Dawn as goddess ascends Olympus to report the light/news to Zeus and the other immortal gods.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ὃ κηρύκεσσι λιγυφθόγγοισι κέλευσε
lines.english: And he commanded the clear-voiced heralds
lines.gloss:
**αὐτὰρ** (conj.) "but, then" – transitions to Agamemnon's action. **κηρύκεσσι** (dat. pl. of κῆρυξ) "to the heralds" – indirect object of command. **λιγυφθόγγοισι** (dat. pl. adj.) "clear-voiced, loud-voiced" – epithet modifying heralds. **κέλευσε** (3rd sg. aor. ind. of κελεύω) "he commanded" – main verb, Agamemnon orders the heralds.

Agamemnon commands his clear-voiced heralds to summon an assembly of the long-haired Achaeans.

lines.original: κηρύσσειν ἀγορὴν δὲ κάρη κομόωντας Ἀχαιούς·
lines.english: to summon to assembly the long-haired Achaeans.
lines.gloss: **κηρύσσειν** (pres. inf., "to proclaim/summon") and **ἀγορήν** (acc. sing., "assembly") form an accusative-infinitive construction dependent on the previous κέλευσε. **κάρη κομόωντας** (acc. pl. masc., pres. part., "long-haired" or "wearing hair on the head") is a traditional Homeric epithet modifying **Ἀχαιούς** (acc. pl., "Achaeans"), the object of the proclamation. The heralds are commanded to summon the long-haired Achaeans to assembly.

lines.original: οἳ μὲν ἐκήρυσσον, τοὶ δʼ ἠγείροντο μάλʼ ὦκα·
lines.english: The heralds made proclamation and the men gathered very swiftly.
lines.gloss:
**οἳ** (pronoun, nom. pl. masc., relative): "who" or "they who" - referring to the heralds. **ἐκήρυσσον** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. act. indic., *κηρύσσω*): "were proclaiming/heralding." **τοὶ** (pronoun, nom. pl. masc., demonstrative): "they" or "these" - referring to the Achaeans. **ἠγείροντο** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. mid./pass. indic., *ἀγείρω*): "were gathering/assembling." **μάλʼ ὦκα** (adverb + adverb): "very swiftly."

The line contrasts the heralds' proclamation with the Achaeans' swift response to assemble, using parallel

lines.original: βουλὴν δὲ πρῶτον μεγαθύμων ἷζε γερόντων
lines.english: First he convened a council of the great-hearted elders.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for βουλὴν δὲ πρῶτον μεγαθύμων ἷζε γερόντων:**

**βουλήν** (acc. fem. sg., "council") is the direct object of **ἷζε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of ἵζω, "he seated/convened"). **πρῶτον** (adv., "first") indicates temporal priority. **μεγαθύμων** (gen. masc. pl. of μεγάθυμος, "great-hearted") and **γερόντων** (gen. masc. pl. of γέρων, "elders") form a descriptive genitive modifying the implied members. The line describes Agamemnon first convening a council of great-hearted elders.

lines.original: Νεστορέῃ παρὰ νηῒ Πυλοιγενέος βασιλῆος·
lines.english: beside the ship of Nestor, the king born in Pylos
lines.gloss:
**Νεστορέῃ** (adjective, dative singular feminine): "belonging to Nestor," modifying νηΐ. **παρά** (preposition + dative): "beside, at." **νηΐ** (noun, dative singular): "ship." **Πυλοιγενέος** (adjective, genitive singular masculine): "Pylos-born," compound epithet modifying βασιλῆος. **βασιλῆος** (noun, genitive singular): "king," in apposition to the implied Nestor.

Agamemnon convenes the council of elders beside the ship of Nestor, the Pylos-born king.

lines.original: τοὺς ὅ γε συγκαλέσας πυκινὴν ἀρτύνετο βουλήν·
lines.english: He called them together and arranged a close counsel.
lines.gloss:
**τοὺς ὅ γε συγκαλέσας πυκινὴν ἀρτύνετο βουλήν·**

**τούς** (demonstrative pronoun, acc. pl. masc.) = "them"; **συγκαλέσας** (aor. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc., συγκαλέω) = "having summoned together"; **πυκινήν** (adj. acc. sg. fem.) = "close, shrewd, well-considered"; **ἀρτύνετο** (impf. mid. 3rd sg., ἀρτύνω) = "he prepared, arranged"; **βουλήν** (noun acc. sg. fem.) = "counsel, plan." Agamemnon summons his leaders and arranges a shrewd deliberation.

lines.original: ἤτοι ὅ γʼ ὣς εἰπὼν κατʼ ἄρʼ ἕζετο, τοῖσι δʼ ἀνέστη
lines.english: So speaking he sat down, and among them arose
lines.gloss:
**ἤτοι** (particle): "and so, then" – marks transition in narrative. **εἰπών** (aorist active participle, nom. sg. masc. of *λέγω*/*εἶπον*): "having spoken." **κατ(ά)...ἕζετο** (tmesis; aorist middle, 3rd sg. of *καθίζω*): "he sat down." **ἀνέστη** (aorist, 3rd sg. of *ἀνίστημι*): "stood up, arose."

The line describes the speaker sitting down after his speech, whereupon another figure (Nestor, as the next line reveals) stood up to address the assembly.

lines.original: Νέστωρ, ὅς ῥα Πύλοιο ἄναξ ἦν ἠμαθόεντος,
lines.english: Nestor, who was lord of sandy Pylos,
lines.gloss: **Νέστωρ** (nom. sg. masc., proper name): Nestor, the aged counselor from Pylos. **Πύλοιο** (gen. sg. neut., "Πύλος"): of Pylos, genitive of place. **ἄναξ** (nom. sg. masc.): lord, king, ruler. **ἠμαθόεντος** (gen. sg. neut., adjective): sandy, describing Pylos with its characteristic sandy terrain. Nestor, who was lord of sandy Pylos, then stood up to speak wisely to the assembly.

lines.original: ὅ σφιν ἐὺ φρονέων ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπεν·
lines.english: He with good intent addressed them and spoke among them.
lines.gloss:
**Target line:** ὅ σφιν ἐὺ φρονέων ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπεν·

**Key words:** 
- **σφιν** (pronoun, dat. pl.): "to/for them" (dative of interest)
- **ἐὺ φρονέων** (adverb + present participle, nom. sg. masc.): "thinking well, with good intent"
- **ἀγορήσατο** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic.): "addressed (the assembly), spoke"
- **μετέειπεν** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. act. indic.): "spoke among/to (them), addressed"

Nestor, thinking wisely on their behalf, addressed the assembly and spoke to them; the line emphasizes his

lines.original: ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας βουλῆς ἐξῆρχε νέεσθαι,
lines.english: So speaking he took the lead in departing from the council.
lines.gloss: **φωνήσας** (aorist participle, nominative masculine singular of φωνέω): "having spoken"; **βουλῆς** (genitive singular of βουλή): "of the council"; **ἐξῆρχε** (imperfect, 3rd singular of ἐξάρχω): "he led the way, began"; **νέεσθαι** (present infinitive of νέομαι): "to go, to return." Thus having spoken, he began to lead the way back from the council, initiating the departure.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἐπανέστησαν πείθοντό τε ποιμένι λαῶν
lines.english: The others rose up and obeyed the shepherd of the people.
lines.gloss:
**οἳ δʼ ἐπανέστησαν πείθοντό τε ποιμένι λαῶν**

*οἳ* (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "they who" refers to the assembled leaders; *ἐπανέστησαν* (3rd pl. aor. indic. act. of ἐπανίστημι) "stood up"; *πείθοντο* (3rd pl. imperf. indic. mid. of πείθω) "were obeying, heeded"; *ποιμένι* (dat. sg. masc. of ποιμήν) "shepherd," dative of the person obeyed, referring to Agamemnon; *λαῶν* (gen. pl. of λαός) "of the people/hosts," completing the common Homeric epithet

lines.original: σκηπτοῦχοι βασιλῆες· ἐπεσσεύοντο δὲ λαοί.
lines.english: The sceptered kings, and the people came hastening forth.
lines.gloss: **σκηπτοῦχοι** (adjective, nom. pl. masc.) "scepter-bearing," modifying βασιλῆες; **βασιλῆες** (noun, nom. pl.) "kings, chiefs"; **ἐπεσσεύοντο** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. mid.) "rushed forward, hastened"; **λαοί** (noun, nom. pl.) "the people, troops." The scepter-bearing kings led while the common troops rushed forward in response.

lines.original: ἠΰτε ἔθνεα εἶσι μελισσάων ἁδινάων
lines.english: Like the many tribes of thronging bees going forth
lines.gloss:
**ἠΰτε ἔθνεα εἶσι μελισσάων ἁδινάων**

*ἠΰτε* (conjunction) "just as, like" introduces an extended simile. *ἔθνεα* (nom. pl. neut., ἔθνος) "swarms, throngs" is the subject. *εἶσι* (3rd pl. pres. indic., εἶμι) "go, come forth." *μελισσάων* (gen. pl. fem., μέλισσα) "of bees" modifies ἔθνεα. *ἁδινάων* (gen. pl. fem., ἁδινός) "dense, crowded, thronging" further describes the bees. The simile compares the surging Greek armies to dense swarms of bees emerging from their

lines.original: πέτρης ἐκ γλαφυρῆς αἰεὶ νέον ἐρχομενάων,
lines.english: from a hollow rock ever coming forth anew
lines.gloss:
**πέτρης** (gen. sg. fem. of πέτρα): "from a rock," genitive of separation with ἐκ.
**γλαφυρῆς** (gen. sg. fem. of γλαφυρός): "hollow," attributive adjective modifying πέτρης.
**αἰεί**: "continually, ever," adverb modifying the participial phrase.
**ἐρχομενάων** (gen. pl. fem. pres. part. of ἔρχομαι): "coming forth," participle modifying an implied noun (the bees), genitive absolute or attributive construction.

The line depicts bees perpetually emerging anew from their hollow rock dwelling, completing the extended simile comparing warriors to swarming bees.

lines.original: βοτρυδὸν δὲ πέτονται ἐπʼ ἄνθεσιν εἰαρινοῖσιν·
lines.english: They fly in clusters upon the spring flowers.
lines.gloss:
**βοτρυδὸν** (adverb): "in clusters" or "like grapes," modifying how the bees fly in dense groups. **πέτονται** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. mid./pass. indic., πέτομαι): "they fly." **ἐπʼ** (preposition + dative): "upon" or "over," governing ἄνθεσιν. **ἄνθεσιν** (noun, dat. pl. neut., ἄνθος): "flowers." **εἰαρινοῖσιν** (adjective, dat. pl. neut., εἰαρινός): "spring" or "of spring," modifying ἄνθεσιν. 

The line depicts bees flying in clusters over spring flowers, continuing the extended simile comparing warriors to swarming bees.

lines.original: αἳ μέν τʼ ἔνθα ἅλις πεποτήαται, αἳ δέ τε ἔνθα·
lines.english: some fly in swarms this way and some that way
lines.gloss:
**αἳ** (fem. nom. pl., relative/demonstrative pronoun) "some" (referring to groups of bees/warriors); **ἅλις** (adverb) "in swarms, abundantly"; **πεποτήαται** (3rd pl. perfect middle/passive indicative of *ποτάομαι*) "have flown, are flying about"; **ἔνθα** (adverb, repeated) "here...there." 

The line depicts the swarms flying in different directions—some in abundant clusters here, others there—continuing the simile comparing Greek troops pouring from ships to bees swarming from a hive.

lines.original: ὣς τῶν ἔθνεα πολλὰ νεῶν ἄπο καὶ κλισιάων
lines.english: So their many tribes from the ships and huts moved forth
lines.gloss: **ὣς** (adverb): thus, in this way, introducing the comparison's application. **ἔθνεα** (noun, nominative plural neuter): tribes, bands, companies of men. **πολλά** (adjective, nominative plural neuter): many, modifying ἔθνεα. **νεῶν** (noun, genitive plural feminine): of the ships, with ἄπο indicating source. **κλισιάων** (noun, genitive plural feminine): of the huts, temporary shelters; paired with νεῶν to show where the troops emerge from.

lines.original: ἠϊόνος προπάροιθε βαθείης ἐστιχόωντο
lines.english: They marched in ranks before the deep shore.
lines.gloss:
**ἠϊόνος** (ἠιών, -όνος, ἡ): genitive singular of "shore, beach" – describes the location relative to which they were marching.

**προπάροιθε**: preposition (+gen.) meaning "in front of, before" – indicates spatial position ahead of the shore.

**βαθείης**: genitive singular feminine of βαθύς, "deep" – modifies ἠϊόνος, describing the depth of the shore/beach.

**ἐστιχόωντο**: 3rd plural imperfect middle/passive of στιχάω, "they went in rows/ranks, marched in formation" – describes the orderly movement of the troops toward the assembly.

The armies marched in ordered ranks before the deep shore toward the assembly.

lines.original: ἰλαδὸν εἰς ἀγορήν· μετὰ δέ σφισιν ὄσσα δεδήει
lines.english: in companies to the assembly, and among them Rumor blazed urging them to go.
lines.gloss: **ἰλαδόν** (adverb): "in throngs," "in companies" — describes the manner of assembly. **εἰς ἀγορήν** (preposition + accusative): "to/into the assembly" — destination of movement. **μετὰ δέ** (preposition + particle): "and among/with" — transitional phrase. **σφισιν** (dative plural pronoun): "them," "for them" — dative of interest. **ὄσσα** (nom. dual neuter, ὄσσε): "the two eyes" — subject. **δεδήει** (3rd sg. pluperfect, δαίω): "were blazing," "had been kindled" — describes the flashing eyes (likely of Iris as divine messenger).

lines.original: ὀτρύνουσʼ ἰέναι Διὸς ἄγγελος· οἳ δʼ ἀγέροντο.
lines.english: Zeus's messenger Rumor urged them to go, and they gathered together.
lines.gloss: **ὀτρύνουσʼ** (pres. act. participle, nom. pl., from ὀτρύνω) "urging" – refers to Iris, Zeus's messenger, spurring the assembly. **ἰέναι** (pres. inf. of εἶμι) "to go" – complementary infinitive with the participle. **Διὸς ἄγγελος** (gen. + nom.) "messenger of Zeus" – identifies Iris in her divine role. **ἀγέροντο** (imperf. mid., 3rd pl. of ἀγείρω) "were gathering" – describes the troops assembling in response to the summons.

lines.original: τετρήχει δʼ ἀγορή, ὑπὸ δὲ στεναχίζετο γαῖα
lines.english: The assembly grew tumultuous, and the earth groaned beneath as the people sat down.
lines.gloss: **τετρήχει** (3rd sing. pluperf. act. indic. of *τετρίγω*) "was clamoring/resounding"; **ἀγορή** (nom. sing. fem.) "assembly"; **ὑπὸ** (prep. with gen.) "beneath, under"; **στεναχίζετο** (3rd sing. imperf. mid./pass. indic. of *στεναχίζω*) "was groaning"; **γαῖα** (nom. sing. fem.) "earth, ground." The assembly was roaring with noise, and the earth beneath was groaning under the weight of the people sitting down.

lines.original: λαῶν ἱζόντων, ὅμαδος δʼ ἦν· ἐννέα δέ σφεας
lines.english: as the people sat down, and there was tumult; nine heralds tried to restrain them
lines.gloss: λαῶν ἱζόντων (genitive plural present participle of ἵζω, "sitting down"): the people as they were taking their seats. ὅμαδος (genitive singular, "tumult/clamor"): continuing the description of the din. ἦν: imperfect of εἰμί, "there was." ἐννέα: "nine," introducing the number of heralds. σφεας (accusative plural pronoun, "them"): referring to the heralds attempting to restore order.

lines.original: κήρυκες βοόωντες ἐρήτυον, εἴ ποτʼ ἀϋτῆς
lines.english: Nine heralds shouting tried to restrain them, if ever they might cease from their clamor.
lines.gloss: **κήρυκες** (nominative plural, "heralds") **βοόωντες** (present participle nominative plural, "shouting") **ἐρήτυον** (imperfect 3rd plural, "were restraining/checking") **ἀϋτῆς** (genitive singular, "uproar/clamor"). The heralds were shouting and attempting to restrain the assembly from its tumultuous noise so that the kings might be heard.

lines.original: σχοίατʼ, ἀκούσειαν δὲ διοτρεφέων βασιλήων.
lines.english: that they might cease their clamor and listen to the god-nurtured kings.
lines.gloss:
**σχοίατʼ, ἀκούσειαν δὲ διοτρεφέων βασιλήων.**

σχοίατο (3rd pl. opt. aor. 2 mid. ἔχω): "they might cease/hold back" (from shouting). ἀκούσειαν (3rd pl. opt. aor. act. ἀκούω): "they might hear/listen to." διοτρεφέων (gen. pl. masc. part. pres. διοτρεφής): "Zeus-nurtured," modifying βασιλήων (gen. pl. βασιλεύς): "of the kings." The heralds urge the assembly to cease their clamor and listen to their divinely-nurtured kings.

lines.original: σπουδῇ δʼ ἕζετο λαός, ἐρήτυθεν δὲ καθʼ ἕδρας
lines.english: The people sat down eagerly and were restrained in their seats.
lines.gloss: **σπουδῇ** (noun, dat. sg. fem.) "with haste, eagerly"; **ἕζετο** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of ἕζομαι) "sat down"; **λαός** (noun, nom. sg. masc.) "the host, army"; **ἐρήτυθεν** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. pass. indic. of ἐρητύω) "was restrained, held back"; **ἕδρας** (noun, acc. pl. fem.) "seats, places." The army sat down eagerly and was restrained in their seats, ceasing their clamor as Agamemnon prepares to speak.

lines.original: παυσάμενοι κλαγγῆς· ἀνὰ δὲ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: having ceased their clamor, and lord Agamemnon stood up
lines.gloss: **παυσάμενοι** (aorist middle participle, nominative plural masculine of παύω): "having ceased, having stopped" - modifying λαός from the previous line, indicating the people stopped their clamor. **κλαγγῆς** (genitive singular feminine of κλαγγή): "from the shouting/clamor" - genitive of separation with παυσάμενοι. **ἀνὰ δέ** (adverb + particle): "up, stood up" - tmesis with ἔστη in the next line, forming ἀνίστημι. **κρείων** (nominative singular masculine of κρείων): "lord, ruler" - epithet modifying Ἀγαμέμνων. **Ἀγαμέμνων** (nominative singular of Ἀγαμέμνων): "

lines.original: ἔστη σκῆπτρον ἔχων τὸ μὲν Ἥφαιστος κάμε τεύχων.
lines.english: He stood holding the scepter which Hephaestus had wrought with toil.
lines.gloss: **ἔστη** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἵστημι) "stood up"; **σκῆπτρον** (acc. sg. neut. noun) "scepter," object of ἔχων; **ἔχων** (pres. act. participle of ἔχω, nom. sg. masc.) "holding"; **κάμε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of κάμνω) "labored, fashioned"; **τεύχων** (pres. act. participle of τεύχω, nom. sg. masc.) "making, crafting." Agamemnon stood holding the scepter which Hephaestus toiled in making, introducing the genealogy of this royal staff.

lines.original: Ἥφαιστος μὲν δῶκε Διὶ Κρονίωνι ἄνακτι,
lines.english: Hephaestus gave it to Zeus the son of Cronus who is lord.
lines.gloss: **Ἥφαιστος** (nom. sg. masc., subject) "Hephaestus"; **δῶκε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of δίδωμι) "gave"; **Διὶ** (dat. sg. of Ζεύς) "to Zeus"; **Κρονίωνι** (dat. sg. masc., patronymic) "son of Kronos"; **ἄνακτι** (dat. sg. masc. noun in apposition) "lord, king." Hephaestus gave [the scepter] to Zeus Kronion the lord, continuing the genealogy of the scepter begun in the previous line.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἄρα Ζεὺς δῶκε διακτόρῳ ἀργεϊφόντῃ·
lines.english: Zeus in turn gave it to the messenger Argiophontes.
lines.gloss:
**αὐτὰρ ἄρα Ζεὺς δῶκε διακτόρῳ ἀργεϊφόντῃ·**

*αὐτὰρ* (particle): "but, moreover" - continues the genealogical sequence. *δῶκε* (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of δίδωμι): "gave" - continues the pattern of divine gift-giving. *διακτόρῳ* (dat. sg. masc. of διάκτορος): "to the messenger" - epithet modifying Hermes. *ἀργεϊφόντῃ* (dat. sg. masc.): "the slayer of Argus" - standard Homeric epithet for Hermes, recipient of Zeus's gift.

lines.original: Ἑρμείας δὲ ἄναξ δῶκεν Πέλοπι πληξίππῳ,
lines.english: Lord Hermes gave it to Pelops the charioteer.
lines.gloss: **Ἑρμείας** (nom. sing., subject) "Hermes"; **ἄναξ** (nom. sing., appositive) "lord"; **δῶκεν** (3rd sing. aor. indic. act. of δίδωμι) "gave"; **Πέλοπι** (dat. sing., indirect object) "to Pelops"; **πληξίππῳ** (dat. sing. masc., epithet) "driver/goader of horses." Lord Hermes gave (the scepter) to Pelops the charioteer, continuing the genealogy of Agamemnon's ancestral staff.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ὃ αὖτε Πέλοψ δῶκʼ Ἀτρέϊ ποιμένι λαῶν,
lines.english: Pelops in turn gave it to Atreus shepherd of the people.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for:** αὐτὰρ ὃ αὖτε Πέλοψ δῶκʼ Ἀτρέϊ ποιμένι λαῶν

**αὐτάρ** (conjunction): "but, and" - transitional particle continuing the genealogical narrative. **Πέλοψ** (nom. sing.): Pelops, subject who gives. **δῶκε** (3rd sing. aor. act. indic. of δίδωμι): "gave" - elided to δῶκ'. **Ἀτρέϊ** (dat. sing.): "to Atreus" - recipient. **ποιμένι λαῶν** (dat. sing.): "shepherd of the people" - traditional epithet for rulers, in apposition to Atreus.

lines.original: Ἀτρεὺς δὲ θνῄσκων ἔλιπεν πολύαρνι Θυέστῃ,
lines.english: Atreus dying left it to Thyestes rich in flocks.
lines.gloss: **Ἀτρεὺς** (nom. sg. masc.): Atreus, subject of the sentence. **θνῄσκων** (pres. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc., θνῄσκω): "dying," temporal circumstance modifying Atreus. **ἔλιπεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. ind., λείπω): "left behind, bequeathed." **πολύαρνι** (dat. sg. masc./neut., πολύαρνος): "rich in flocks," epithet modifying Thyestes. **Θυέστῃ** (dat. sg. masc.): to Thyestes, indirect object receiving the inheritance. Atreus, upon dying, left the scepter to Thyestes who was rich in sheep.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ὃ αὖτε Θυέστʼ Ἀγαμέμνονι λεῖπε φορῆναι,
lines.english: Atreus dying left it to rich-flocked Thyestes, and he in turn left it to Agamemnon to bear.
lines.gloss: **Iliad 2.107**: αὐτὰρ (conj., "but, and"), ὃ (nom. sg. masc. demonstrative pronoun, "he," i.e., Thyestes), αὖτε (adv., "in turn, again"), Θυέστʼ (nom. sg., "Thyestes," subject), Ἀγαμέμνονι (dat. sg., "to/for Agamemnon," indirect object), λεῖπε (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of λείπω, "left, bequeathed"), φορῆναι (pres. act. infin. of φορέω, "to bear, to wield"). Thyestes in turn left the scepter to Agamemnon to bear, continuing the genealogy of Mycenaean kingship.

lines.original: πολλῇσιν νήσοισι καὶ Ἄργεϊ παντὶ ἀνάσσειν.
lines.english: to rule over many islands and all of Argos.
lines.gloss: **Key words:** πολλῇσιν (dative plural feminine of πολύς, "many") modifying νήσοισι (dative plural of νῆσος, "islands"); Ἄργεϊ (dative singular of Ἄργος, "Argos"); παντί (dative singular neuter of πᾶς, "all," modifying Ἄργεϊ); ἀνάσσειν (present infinitive of ἀνάσσω, "to rule over"). The line describes the scepter's power to rule over many islands and all of Argos, with the datives governed by the infinitive ἀνάσσειν.

lines.original: τῷ ὅ γʼ ἐρεισάμενος ἔπεʼ Ἀργείοισι μετηύδα·
lines.english: Leaning on it he spoke words among the Argives.
lines.gloss:
**τῷ** (pronoun, dative singular neuter of ὁ): "on this/it," referring to the scepter; **ἐρεισάμενος** (participle, aorist middle nominative singular masculine of ἐρείδω): "having leaned, propping himself"; **ἔπεα** (noun, accusative plural neuter of ἔπος): "words, speech"; **μετηύδα** (verb, imperfect active 3rd singular of μεταυδάω): "he spoke, addressed."

Leaning on the scepter, he addressed words to the Argives—the physical act of propping oneself on the staff of authority emphasizes the formal weight of the following speech.

lines.original: ὣς φάτο, τοῖσι δὲ θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ὄρινε
lines.english: So he spoke and stirred the spirit in their breasts.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" – marks the conclusion of direct speech.
**φάτο** (verb, 3rd sing. aorist middle indicative of φημί): "he spoke."
**θυμόν** (noun, accusative singular): "spirit, heart" – the object stirred by Agamemnon's words.
**στήθεσσιν** (noun, dative plural of στῆθος): "in breasts, in chests" – locative dative.
**ὄρινε** (verb, 3rd sing. aorist active indicative of ὀρίνω): "he stirred, roused."

The verse describes how the speaker's words stirred the spirits in the breasts of his listeners (the Argives).

lines.original: πᾶσι μετὰ πληθὺν ὅσοι οὐ βουλῆς ἐπάκουσαν·
lines.english: to all throughout the throng who had not heard the council
lines.gloss: **πᾶσι** (πᾶς, dative plural masculine): "to all"; **μετὰ πληθύν** (μετά + πληθύς, accusative singular feminine): "among/throughout the multitude"; **ὅσοι** (ὅσος, nominative plural masculine, relative pronoun): "who/as many as"; **βουλῆς** (βουλή, genitive singular): "of the council"; **ἐπάκουσαν** (ἐπ-ακούω, 3rd plural aorist): "heard, were present at." The line describes how Agamemnon's speech stirred the hearts of all the common soldiers who had not attended the council of chiefs.

lines.original: κινήθη δʼ ἀγορὴ φὴ κύματα μακρὰ θαλάσσης
lines.english: The assembly stirred like the long waves of the sea.
lines.gloss:
**κινήθη** (3rd sg. aor. pass. indic. of κινέω) "was set in motion, was stirred"; **ἀγορή** (nom. sg. fem.) "assembly"; **φή** (adv., or nom. sg. fem. of φή) "like"; **κύματα** (nom./acc. pl. neut. of κῦμα) "waves"; **μακρά** (nom./acc. pl. neut. of μακρός) "long, great"; **θαλάσσης** (gen. sg. fem. of θάλασσα) "of the sea."

The assembly was stirred like the long waves of the sea, introducing an extended simile comparing the tumultuous gathering to ocean swells.

lines.original: πόντου Ἰκαρίοιο, τὰ μέν τʼ Εὖρός τε Νότος τε
lines.english: of the Icarian sea, which both the East Wind and the South Wind
lines.gloss:
**πόντου Ἰκαρίοιο, τὰ μέν τʼ Εὖρός τε Νότος τε**

*πόντου* (gen. sg. of πόντος): "of the sea," genitive depending on κύματα from the previous line. *Ἰκαρίοιο* (gen. sg. of Ἰκάριος): "Icarian," the epithet specifying the Icarian Sea in the eastern Aegean. *Εὖρός* and *Νότος* (nom. sg.): "the East Wind" and "the South Wind," personified winds as subjects that stir the waves. The relative pronoun *τά* (acc. pl. neut.) refers to κύματα, introducing a comparison of the assembly's tumult to wind-driven waves.

lines.original: ὤρορʼ ἐπαΐξας πατρὸς Διὸς ἐκ νεφελάων.
lines.english: rushing upon them when the East Wind and South Wind drive down from the clouds of father Zeus.
lines.gloss:
**ὤρορʼ ἐπαΐξας πατρὸς Διὸς ἐκ νεφελάων.**

**ὤρορε** (3rd sg. perf. act. indic. of ὄρνυμι): "has roused [them]," "has stirred up"
**ἐπαΐξας** (aor. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc. of ἐπαΐσσω): "rushing upon," "sweeping down"
**πατρός** (gen. sg. of πατήρ): "of [his] father"
**Διός** (gen. sg. of Ζεύς): "Zeus"
**νεφελάων** (gen. pl. of νεφέλη): "from the clouds"

Zeus, rushing down from his clouds,

lines.original: ὡς δʼ ὅτε κινήσῃ Ζέφυρος βαθὺ λήϊον ἐλθὼν
lines.english: As when the West Wind stirs the deep grainfield coming upon it
lines.gloss:
**κινήσῃ** (verb, aorist subjunctive 3rd sg. of κινέω) "stir, set in motion"; **Ζέφυρος** (noun, nominative sg.) "the West Wind"; **βαθὺ** (adjective, accusative sg. neut.) "deep, thick"; **λήϊον** (noun, accusative sg.) "grain-field, standing grain"; **ἐλθὼν** (participle, aorist active nominative sg. of ἔρχομαι) "having come, coming." 

The simile begins: "As when the West Wind, having come, stirs the deep grain-field"—introducing an extended comparison of battlefield tumult to wind moving across crops.

lines.original: λάβρος ἐπαιγίζων, ἐπί τʼ ἠμύει ἀσταχύεσσιν,
lines.english: rushing violently upon it, and the ears of grain bend beneath it
lines.gloss: **λάβρος** (nom. sg. masc. adj.) "violent, furious" modifies Ζέφυρος. **ἐπαιγίζων** (nom. sg. masc. pres. act. ptcp. of ἐπαιγίζω) "rushing upon, sweeping over." **ἠμύει** (3rd sg. impf. act. of ἠμύω) "made a murmuring sound, rustled." **ἀσταχύεσσιν** (dat. pl. of ἄσταχυς) "upon the ears of grain." The line depicts the west wind violently sweeping over and rustling through the grain field, completing the simile that compares this natural movement to the stirring of the assembly.

lines.original: ὣς τῶν πᾶσʼ ἀγορὴ κινήθη· τοὶ δʼ ἀλαλητῷ
lines.english: So their whole assembly was stirred, and they with a cry
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" - introducing a simile conclusion comparing the assembly's movement to wind-driven grain.

**κινήθη** (3rd sg. aor. pass. indic. of κινέω): "was stirred, was set in motion" - describing the agitation of the entire assembly.

**πᾶσʼ ἀγορὴ** (nom. sg. fem., with elided πᾶσα): "the whole assembly" - the subject, referring to the gathered Achaean army.

**ἀλαλητῷ** (dat. sg. masc. of ἀλαλητός): "with shouting, with war-cry" - manner in which they rushed forth.

The assembly surges forward with shouting, completing the extended simile of wind over grain fields.

lines.original: νῆας ἔπʼ ἐσσεύοντο, ποδῶν δʼ ὑπένερθε κονίη
lines.english: They rushed to the ships, and dust rose up beneath their feet.
lines.gloss: **νῆας** (acc. pl. fem. of ναῦς) "ships"; **ἔπʼ** (= ἐπί with elision, preposition + acc.) "toward"; **ἐσσεύοντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid. of σεύω) "they were rushing"; **ποδῶν** (gen. pl. masc. of πούς) "of feet"; **ὑπένερθε** (adverb/preposition + gen.) "beneath, from under"; **κονίη** (nom. sg. fem. of κονίη) "dust." The troops rushed toward the ships, while dust rose up from beneath their feet.

lines.original: ἵστατʼ ἀειρομένη· τοὶ δʼ ἀλλήλοισι κέλευον
lines.english: The dust rose up as they stirred, and they urged one another on.
lines.gloss: **ἵστατο** (3rd sg. impf. mid. of ἵστημι) "was rising"; **ἀειρομένη** (pres. mid. part. nom. sg. fem. of ἀείρω) "being raised up"; **τοί** (nom. pl. masc. demonstrative pronoun) "they, these men"; **ἀλλήλοισι** (dat. pl. reciprocal pronoun) "to one another"; **κέλευον** (3rd pl. impf. act. of κελεύω) "were urging, exhorting." The dust was rising up from beneath their feet, and the warriors were shouting encouragement to each other as they rushed toward the ships.

lines.original: ἅπτεσθαι νηῶν ἠδʼ ἑλκέμεν εἰς ἅλα δῖαν,
lines.english: to lay hold of the ships and drag them down to the bright sea
lines.gloss: **ἅπτεσθαι** (pres. mid./pass. inf. < ἅπτω) "to lay hold of, grasp"; **νηῶν** (gen. pl. < ναῦς) "of the ships"; **ἑλκέμεν** (pres. act. inf. < ἕλκω) "to drag, haul"; **ἅλα** (acc. sg. < ἅλς) "sea"; **δῖαν** (acc. sg. fem. < δῖος) "bright, shining." The men urge one another to take hold of the ships and drag them down into the shining sea.

lines.original: οὐρούς τʼ ἐξεκάθαιρον· ἀϋτὴ δʼ οὐρανὸν ἷκεν
lines.english: They were clearing out the channels and the clamor reached the sky.
lines.gloss: **οὐρούς** (acc. pl. masc. of οὖρος) "channel-ways, stern-cable trenches" – direct object of ἐξεκάθαιρον. **ἐξεκάθαιρον** (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic. of ἐκκαθαίρω) "they were clearing out." **ἀϋτή** (nom. sg. fem. of ἀϋτή) "shouting, clamor" – subject of ἷκεν. **οὐρανόν** (acc. sg. masc. of οὐρανός) "heaven, sky" – direct object. **ἷκεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἱκνέομαι) "reached, arrived at." The Achaeans clear the ship

lines.original: οἴκαδε ἱεμένων· ὑπὸ δʼ ᾕρεον ἕρματα νηῶν.
lines.english: longing for home, and they were pulling out the props from under the ships
lines.gloss:
**οἴκαδε** (adverb) "homeward" - directional adverb with -δε suffix indicating motion toward home. **ἱεμένων** (present middle participle, genitive plural, from ἵημι) "of those eager/hastening" - genitive absolute construction modifying the Argives. **ὑπό** (preposition with tmesis) governs the compound verb. **ᾕρεον** (imperfect active, 3rd plural, from ὑπ-αιρέω) "they were lifting up/removing" - the iterative action of removing. **ἕρματα** (accusative plural neuter, ἕρμα) "props/supports" - the blocks or wedges supporting beached ships.

The Argives eager for home were removing the props from under their ships in preparation for departure.

lines.original: ἔνθά κεν Ἀργείοισιν ὑπέρμορα νόστος ἐτύχθη
lines.english: Then would a homecoming beyond fate have been accomplished for the Argives
lines.gloss:
**ἔνθά κεν Ἀργείοισιν ὑπέρμορα νόστος ἐτύχθη**

**ἔνθα** (adverb): "then," "at that moment"; **κεν** (particle) = ἄν, marks the potential/counterfactual mood with aorist indicative; **Ἀργείοισιν** (dative plural of Ἀργεῖοι): "for the Argives"; **ὑπέρμορα** (accusative neuter singular of ὑπέρμορος): "beyond fate," "contrary to destiny"; **ἐτύχθη** (3rd singular aorist passive indicative of τυγχάνω): "would have occurred/happened." The line presents a counterfactual: "Then a homecoming beyond fate would have occurred for

lines.original: εἰ μὴ Ἀθηναίην Ἥρη πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν·
lines.english: if Hera had not spoken to Athena with these words
lines.gloss: **Ἀθηναίην** (acc. sing. of Ἀθηναίη): Athena, goddess object of Hera's speech. **Ἥρη** (nom. sing.): Hera, subject of the verb, initiates communication. **μῦθον** (acc. sing. of μῦθος): speech, word; object of the preposition πρός. **ἔειπεν** (3rd sing. aor. of εἶπον/ἀγορεύω): spoke, addressed. The line presents a counterfactual condition: the Greeks would have achieved premature homecoming "if Hera had not spoken to Athena."

lines.original: ὣς ἔφατʼ, οὐδʼ ἀπίθησε θεὰ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη,
lines.english: So she spoke, and the goddess grey-eyed Athena did not disobey.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" — marks the conclusion of direct speech.
**ἔφατʼ** (3rd sg. aor. indic. mid. of φημί): "she spoke" — Hera finished speaking.
**ἀπίθησε** (3rd sg. aor. indic. act. of ἀπιθέω): "disobeyed" — with οὐδ', "nor did she disobey."
**γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. epithet): "bright-eyed, gleaming-eyed" — standard epithet of Athena.

Athena immediately obeys Hera's command without resistance, demonstrating divine hierarchy and swift action.

lines.original: βῆ δὲ κατʼ Οὐλύμποιο καρήνων ἀΐξασα·
lines.english: She darted down from the peaks of Olympus.
lines.gloss: **βῆ** (3rd sg. aorist of βαίνω): "she went"; **κατά** + gen.: "down from"; **Οὐλύμποιο** (gen. sg. of Οὔλυμπος): "of Olympus"; **καρήνων** (gen. pl. of κάρηνον): "peaks, summits"; **ἀΐξασα** (aor. participle fem. nom. sg. of ἀΐσσω): "darting, rushing." Athena descends swiftly from the peaks of Olympus.

lines.original: καρπαλίμως δʼ ἵκανε θοὰς ἐπὶ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν.
lines.english: and swiftly she came to the swift ships of the Achaeans
lines.gloss:
**καρπαλίμως** (adverb): swiftly, quickly. **ἵκανε** (3rd sing. aorist indicative of ἱκνέομαι): she arrived, she reached. **θοάς** (fem. acc. pl. of θοός): swift, fast-moving. **νῆας** (acc. pl. of ναῦς): ships. **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιοί): of the Achaeans.

Athena swiftly arrives at the swift ships of the Achaeans, continuing her descent from Olympus to find Odysseus among the Greek forces.

lines.original: εὗρεν ἔπειτʼ Ὀδυσῆα Διὶ μῆτιν ἀτάλαντον
lines.english: He found then Odysseus equal to Zeus in counsel
lines.gloss: **εὗρεν** (3rd sg. aorist act. indic. of εὑρίσκω, "he found"), **Ὀδυσῆα** (acc. sg. of Ὀδυσσεύς, "Odysseus"), **Διὶ** (dat. sg. of Ζεύς, "to Zeus"), **μῆτιν** (acc. sg., "counsel, wisdom"), **ἀτάλαντον** (acc. sg. masc. of ἀτάλαντος, "equal to"). "Then he found Odysseus, equal to Zeus in counsel"—the standard Homeric formula emphasizing Odysseus's strategic intelligence.

lines.original: ἑσταότʼ· οὐδʼ ὅ γε νηὸς ἐϋσσέλμοιο μελαίνης
lines.english: standing there, nor was he touching his black benched ship
lines.gloss: **ἑσταότʼ·** (ἑσταότα) perfect active participle, accusative singular masculine of ἵστημι, "standing"; **νηὸς** (νηός) genitive singular of ναῦς, "of the ship"; **ἐϋσσέλμοιο** (ἐϋσσέλμου) genitive singular adjective modifying νηός, "well-benched"; **μελαίνης** genitive singular feminine of μέλας, "black," modifying νηός. Athena finds Odysseus standing idle, not touching his black, well-benched ship.

lines.original: ἅπτετʼ, ἐπεί μιν ἄχος κραδίην καὶ θυμὸν ἵκανεν·
lines.english: He did not touch the black benched ship, since grief had reached his heart and spirit.
lines.gloss:
**ἅπτετʼ, ἐπεί μιν ἄχος κραδίην καὶ θυμὸν ἵκανεν·**

**ἅπτετο** (3rd sg. impf. mid. of ἅπτω): "he touched" or "was grasping" (the ship). **ἄχος** (nom. sg. neut.): "grief, pain." **κραδίην** (acc. sg. fem.): "heart." **ἵκανεν** (3rd sg. aor. of ἱκάνω/ἱκνέομαι): "had reached, seized." Achilles did not touch his ship because grief had seized his heart and spirit.

lines.original: ἀγχοῦ δʼ ἱσταμένη προσέφη γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη·
lines.english: Standing close beside him grey-eyed Athena spoke to him.
lines.gloss: **ἀγχοῦ** (adv.): near, close by; **ἱσταμένη** (pres. mid. part. nom. sg. fem. of ἵστημι): standing, taking her stand; **προσέφη** (3rd sg. aor. ind. of προσφημί): she addressed, spoke to; **γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. adj.): bright-eyed, gleaming-eyed (epithet of Athena); **Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg. fem.): Athena. The bright-eyed goddess Athena stands close beside (Achilles) and addresses him.

lines.original: ὣς φάθʼ, ὃ δὲ ξυνέηκε θεᾶς ὄπα φωνησάσης,
lines.english: Thus she spoke, and he recognized the voice of the goddess as she addressed him.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς φάθʼ, ὃ δὲ ξυνέηκε θεᾶς ὄπα φωνησάσης,**

ὣς (adverb) "thus, in this way"; φάθʼ = ἔφατο (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί) "she spoke"; ξυνέηκε (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ξυνίημι) "he understood, perceived"; ὄπα (acc. sg. of ὄψ) "voice, utterance"; φωνησάσης (aor. act. fem. gen. sg. participle of φωνέω) "of [the goddess] speaking." Thus she spoke, and he perceived the voice of the goddess speaking.

lines.original: βῆ δὲ θέειν, ἀπὸ δὲ χλαῖναν βάλε· τὴν δὲ κόμισσε
lines.english: He started running and cast off his cloak, which the herald Eurybates of Ithaca who attended him took up.
lines.gloss: **βῆ** (3rd sg. aorist of βαίνω): "he went" or "set off"; **θέειν** (present infinitive of θέω): "to run"; **χλαῖναν** (acc. sg. fem. of χλαῖνα): "cloak," direct object of βάλε; **βάλε** (3rd sg. aorist of βάλλω): "threw off" or "cast aside"; **κόμισσε** (3rd sg. aorist of κομίζω): "took charge of" or "carried." Odysseus springs into motion, running while casting off his cloak, which the herald Eurybates takes.

lines.original: κῆρυξ Εὐρυβάτης Ἰθακήσιος ὅς οἱ ὀπήδει·
lines.english: The herald Eurybates of Ithaca who attended him took it up.
lines.gloss: κῆρυξ (nom. sg. masc.) "herald" - subject, identifying Eurybates' role. Εὐρυβάτης (nom. sg. masc.) "Eurybates" - proper name in apposition. Ἰθακήσιος (nom. sg. masc. adj.) "Ithacan, of Ithaca" - ethnic designation modifying Eurybates. ὀπήδει (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of ὀπηδέω) "attended, accompanied" - describes his service relationship, with οἱ (dat. sg.) referring to Odysseus.

lines.original: αὐτὸς δʼ Ἀτρεΐδεω Ἀγαμέμνονος ἀντίος ἐλθὼν
lines.english: He himself came up to face Agamemnon son of Atreus
lines.gloss:
**αὐτὸς** (pronoun, nominative singular masculine): "he himself" (Eurybates). **Ἀτρεΐδεω** (noun, genitive singular): "of the son of Atreus," dependent on Ἀγαμέμνονος in apposition. **Ἀγαμέμνονος** (noun, genitive singular): "of Agamemnon," governed by ἀντίος. **ἀντίος** (adjective, nominative singular masculine): "face to face with, opposite to" (+ genitive). **ἐλθών** (participle, aorist active nominative singular masculine from ἔρχομαι): "having gone, going."

The herald himself, going to meet Agamemnon son of Atreus face to face, receives the scepter.

lines.original: δέξατό οἱ σκῆπτρον πατρώϊον ἄφθιτον αἰεί·
lines.english: He received from him the ancestral scepter, imperishable forever.
lines.gloss:
**δέξατό** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of δέχομαι) "received, took"; **σκῆπτρον** (acc. sg. neut. noun) "scepter, staff"; **πατρώϊον** (acc. sg. neut. adj.) "ancestral, paternal"; **ἄφθιτον** (acc. sg. neut. adj.) "imperishable, undecaying"; **αἰεί** (adv.) "always, forever." 

Agamemnon received the ancestral scepter, which is eternally imperishable, before proceeding with Chryses to the ships.

lines.original: σὺν τῷ ἔβη κατὰ νῆας Ἀχαιῶν χαλκοχιτώνων.
lines.english: With this he went throughout the ships of the bronze-clad Achaeans.
lines.gloss: **σὺν** (preposition + dative): "with" (governing τῷ, referring to the scepter). **ἔβη** (3rd singular aorist indicative of βαίνω): "he went." **κατὰ νῆας** (preposition + accusative plural): "along/throughout the ships." **Ἀχαιῶν χαλκοχιτώνων** (genitive plural): "of the bronze-clad Achaeans" (χαλκοχιτώνων is a compound epithet, "bronze-tunic-wearing"). Odysseus proceeds with the ancestral scepter among the Achaean fleet to restore order.

lines.original: ὅν τινα μὲν βασιλῆα καὶ ἔξοχον ἄνδρα κιχείη
lines.english: Whichever king or man of rank he came upon
lines.gloss: **ὅν** (relative pronoun, acc. masc. sing.) = "whomever"; **βασιλῆα** (noun, acc. masc. sing.) = "king"; **ἔξοχον** (adj., acc. masc. sing.) = "outstanding, distinguished"; **ἄνδρα** (noun, acc. masc. sing.) = "man"; **κιχείη** (verb, 3rd sing. opt. pres. act.) = "he might encounter, find." Odysseus encounters whichever distinguished king or outstanding man, restraining them with gentle words as he moves through the Greek forces.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἀγανοῖς ἐπέεσσιν ἐρητύσασκε παραστάς·
lines.english: him he would stand beside and restrain with gentle words
lines.gloss: **τὸν** (demonstrative pronoun, accusative singular masculine): "him" - refers to the king or excellent man from the previous line. **ἀγανοῖς ἐπέεσσιν** (adjective + noun, dative plural neuter): "with gentle words" - instrumental dative expressing means. **ἐρητύσασκε** (imperfect iterative verb, 3rd singular): "he would restrain/check repeatedly" - the iterative suffix -σκε marks repeated action in past time. **παραστάς** (aorist participle, nominative singular masculine): "standing beside" - from παρίστημι, indicating Odysseus's physical proximity as he addresses nobles.

lines.original: ὃν δʼ αὖ δήμου τʼ ἄνδρα ἴδοι βοόωντά τʼ ἐφεύροι,
lines.english: But whichever man of the common people he saw and found shouting,
lines.gloss:
**ὃν** (relative pronoun, acc. sing. masc.) "whom"; **δήμου** (noun, gen. sing.) "of the common people/demos"; **ἴδοι** (optative, 3rd sing. aor. act. from ὁράω) "he should see"; **βοόωντα** (participle, acc. sing. masc. pres. act. from βοάω) "shouting"; **ἐφεύροι** (optative, 3rd sing. aor. act. from ἐφευρίσκω) "he should find."

Odysseus restrains nobles gently, but when he sees and finds a man of the common people shouting, he takes a different approach (striking him with the scepter).

lines.original: τὸν σκήπτρῳ ἐλάσασκεν ὁμοκλήσασκέ τε μύθῳ·
lines.english: He would strike him with the scepter and rebuke him with words.
lines.gloss: **τὸν** (demonstrative pronoun, masculine accusative singular) "him" – the common man just mentioned. **σκήπτρῳ** (noun, neuter dative singular) "with his scepter" – instrument of Odysseus's authority. **ἐλάσασκεν** (verb, 3rd singular imperfect iterative from ἐλαύνω) "he would strike repeatedly." **ὁμοκλήσασκέ** (verb, 3rd singular imperfect iterative from ὁμοκλέω) "he would rebuke repeatedly." The iterative imperfects indicate Odysseus's habitual actions when encountering common soldiers shouting in the assembly.

lines.original: ὣς ὅ γε κοιρανέων δίεπε στρατόν· οἳ δʼ ἀγορὴν δὲ
lines.english: Thus he marshaling them set the army in order, and they to the assembly again
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ὅ γε κοιρανέων δίεπε στρατόν· οἳ δʼ ἀγορὴν δὲ**

*ὣς* (adverb): "thus, in this way"; *κοιρανέων* (present participle, nominative singular masculine, from κοιρανέω): "ruling, commanding"; *δίεπε* (imperfect, 3rd singular, from διέπω): "he marshaled, arranged"; *στρατόν* (accusative singular): "the army, host"; *ἀγορήν* (accusative singular): "to the assembly." Thus he, ruling as commander, marshaled the host, and they rushed to the assembly.

lines.original: αὖτις ἐπεσσεύοντο νεῶν ἄπο καὶ κλισιάων
lines.english: They rushed back to the assembly from the ships and huts.
lines.gloss:
**αὖτις ἐπεσσεύοντο νεῶν ἄπο καὶ κλισιάων**

**αὖτις** (adverb): "back again," "once more" — the troops return to assembly. **ἐπεσσεύοντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid. ἐπισεύω): "they rushed toward/upon," describing the Achaeans' eager movement. **νεῶν** (gen. pl. ναῦς): "from the ships," with **ἄπο** (tmesis from compound verb). **κλισιάων** (gen. pl. κλισία): "huts," "shelters" — the temporary dwellings of the Greek camp.

lines.original: ἠχῇ, ὡς ὅτε κῦμα πολυφλοίσβοιο θαλάσσης
lines.english: with a roar, as when a wave of the loud-thundering sea
lines.gloss: **ἠχῇ** (dat. sg. fem. of ἠχή): "with din/uproar," dative of manner describing the noise of troops rushing forward. **ὡς ὅτε** (comparative particle + temporal particle): "as when," introducing an extended epic simile comparing the soldiers' noise to the sea. **κῦμα** (nom. sg. neut. of κῦμα): "wave," subject of the simile. **πολυφλοίσβοιο** (gen. sg. neut. of πολυφλοίσβοιος): "loud-roaring/many-dashing," compound epithet modifying θαλάσσης, emphasizing the sea's tumultuous sound. **θαλάσσης** (gen. sg. fem. of θάλασσα): "of the sea," genitive with κῦμα.

lines.original: αἰγιαλῷ μεγάλῳ βρέμεται, σμαραγεῖ δέ τε πόντος.
lines.english: The great shore roars and the sea crashes thunderously.
lines.gloss: **αἰγιαλῷ** (dative singular, "on the shore") **μεγάλῳ** (dative singular, "great/loud") **βρέμεται** (3rd singular present, "roars/crashes") **σμαραγεῖ** (3rd singular present, "resounds/crashes") **πόντος** (nominative singular, "sea/deep"). The simile continues: the great shore roars when waves crash upon it, and the sea itself resounds—depicting the tumultuous noise of the assembled Achaean army.

lines.original: ἄλλοι μέν ῥʼ ἕζοντο, ἐρήτυθεν δὲ καθʼ ἕδρας·
lines.english: The others sat down and kept to their seats.
lines.gloss: **ἄλλοι** (ἄλλος): nominative plural masculine, "the others"; **ἕζοντο** (ἕζομαι): 3rd plural aorist middle indicative, "sat down"; **ἐρήτυθεν** (ἐρητύω): 3rd plural aorist passive indicative, "were restrained/held in check"; **ἕδρας** (ἕδρα): accusative plural feminine, "seats." The Achaeans take their seats and are restrained in their places, contrasting with Thersites alone who continues to rail (next line).

lines.original: Θερσίτης δʼ ἔτι μοῦνος ἀμετροεπὴς ἐκολῴα,
lines.english: But Thersites alone still clamored on with unmeasured words.
lines.gloss: **Θερσίτης** (nom. sg. masc., proper noun) "Thersites" - the notorious troublemaker. **μοῦνος** (nom. sg. masc., adjective) "alone, only" - emphasizing his isolation. **ἀμετροεπής** (nom. sg. masc., compound adjective) "immoderate in speech, reckless-talking" - from ἀ- + μέτρον + ἔπος. **ἐκολῴα** (3rd sg. impf. act., κολοιόω) "he clamored, kept up a din" - onomatopoetic verb suggesting harsh, crow-like noise. While others sat down and were restrained in their seats, Thersites alone continued his intemperate shouting.

lines.original: ὃς ἔπεα φρεσὶν ᾗσιν ἄκοσμά τε πολλά τε ᾔδη
lines.english: who knew in his mind many words both disorderly and abundant
lines.gloss: **ὃς** (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) "who"; **ἔπεα** (noun, acc. pl. neut.) "words"; **φρεσίν** (noun, dat. pl. fem.) "in his mind/heart"; **ἄκοσμα** (adj., acc. pl. neut.) "disorderly, unseemly"; **ᾔδη** (verb, 3rd sg. plpf. act.) "he knew/had." Thersites is characterized as one who "knew in his mind many disorderly words"—emphasizing his undisciplined speech and abundance of improper utterances stored mentally.

lines.original: μάψ, ἀτὰρ οὐ κατὰ κόσμον, ἐριζέμεναι βασιλεῦσιν,
lines.english: rashly and not in proper order to quarrel with kings
lines.gloss:
**μάψ** (adverb): "idly, recklessly, without purpose" — modifies the manner of speaking.

**κατὰ κόσμον** (prepositional phrase): κατά + accusative of κόσμος, "according to order/propriety, fittingly" — negated by οὐ to indicate unseemly speech.

**ἐριζέμεναι** (present middle/passive infinitive of ἐρίζω): "to quarrel with, contend against" — epexegetic infinitive explaining the disorderly nature of his speech.

**βασιλεῦσιν** (dative plural of βασιλεύς): "with kings" — dative object of ἐριζέμεναι.

The line describes speaking rashly and not in proper order, quarreling with kings.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὅ τι οἱ εἴσαιτο γελοίϊον Ἀργείοισιν
lines.english: but whatever he thought would be laughable to the Argives
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ὅ τι (neuter relative pronoun, "whatever"), εἴσαιτο (3rd sg. aorist optative middle of *εἴδομαι*, "seemed to him"), γελοίϊον (adjective, neuter accusative sg., "laughable, ridiculous"), Ἀργείοισιν (dative plural, "to/for the Argives").

**Gloss:** The line describes how Thersites would say whatever seemed to him likely to be ridiculous/laughable to the Argives, suggesting his aim was to provoke laughter rather than speak properly.

lines.original: ἔμμεναι· αἴσχιστος δὲ ἀνὴρ ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθε·
lines.english: He was the ugliest man who came to Troy.
lines.gloss:
**ἔμμεναι· αἴσχιστος δὲ ἀνὴρ ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθε·**

**ἔμμεναι** (infinitive, present of εἰμί) "to be" — completes the indirect discourse from the previous line. **αἴσχιστος** (superlative adjective, nominative masculine singular) "ugliest, most shameful" — describes Thersites. **ἀνήρ** (noun, nominative singular) "man." **ὑπό** (preposition + acc.) "to." **ἦλθε** (3rd singular aorist indicative of ἔρχομαι) "came, went." 

This line concludes the description of Thersites as the ugliest man who came to Troy.

lines.original: φολκὸς ἔην, χωλὸς δʼ ἕτερον πόδα· τὼ δέ οἱ ὤμω
lines.english: He was bandy-legged and lame in one foot, and his shoulders
lines.gloss: **φολκὸς** (nom. sg. adj.): "bandy-legged," describing physical deformity. **χωλὸς** (nom. sg. adj.): "lame," describing his lameness. **ἕτερον** (acc. sg. adj.): "one (of two)," modifying **πόδα** (acc. sg. masc. noun): "foot." **ὤμω** (nom. dual masc. noun): "shoulders" (dual form). The line continues the description of Thersites' ugliness, detailing his bow-leggedness, lame foot, and hunched shoulders.

lines.original: κυρτὼ ἐπὶ στῆθος συνοχωκότε· αὐτὰρ ὕπερθε
lines.english: rounded over his chest and drawn together, and above
lines.gloss: κυρτώ (nominative dual neuter of κυρτός, "curved, hunched") describes his two shoulders bent forward; ἐπί + στῆθος (accusative singular, "chest") indicates their position over the chest; συνοχωκότε (perfect active participle, dual, from συνοχάω/συνέχω, "drawn together, compressed") modifies the shoulders as hunched together; ὕπερθε (adverb, "above, overhead") sets up the description of what lies above in the next line. This line continues the physical description of Thersites' deformities, focusing on his hunched, rounded shoulders curving over his chest.

lines.original: φοξὸς ἔην κεφαλήν, ψεδνὴ δʼ ἐπενήνοθε λάχνη.
lines.english: He was pointed in the head, and sparse hair sprouted upon it.
lines.gloss: **φοξός** (adj., nom. sg. masc.) "pointed, tapering" describes his head shape; **κεφαλήν** (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "head" is the accusative of respect; **ψεδνή** (adj., nom. sg. fem.) "sparse, scanty"; **ἐπενήνοθε** (pluperfect, 3rd sg.) "had grown upon" from ἐπι-ανθέω; **λάχνη** (noun, nom. sg. fem.) "down, hair, wool." The line describes Thersites' pointed head with sparse hair grown upon it.

lines.original: ἔχθιστος δʼ Ἀχιλῆϊ μάλιστʼ ἦν ἠδʼ Ὀδυσῆϊ·
lines.english: He was most hateful to Achilles and to Odysseus.
lines.gloss: ἔχθιστος: superlative adjective (nominative singular masculine) from ἐχθρός, "most hateful/most hated." Ἀχιλῆϊ and Ὀδυσῆϊ: dative singular proper nouns, "to Achilles" and "to Odysseus," indicating the persons to whom Thersites was most hateful. μάλιστα: superlative adverb, "especially/most of all," intensifying ἔχθιστος. The line establishes Thersites' particular enmity with these two heroes, singling them out from the other Greeks.

lines.original: τὼ γὰρ νεικείεσκε· τότʼ αὖτʼ Ἀγαμέμνονι δίῳ
lines.english: For he used to quarrel with those two, but now at godlike Agamemnon
lines.gloss:
**τὼ γὰρ νεικείεσκε· τότʼ αὖτʼ Ἀγαμέμνονι δίῳ**

**τώ** (acc. dual, demonstrative pronoun): "these two," referring to Achilles and Odysseus. **νεικείεσκε** (3rd sg. impf. ind., νεικέω): "he used to revile/quarrel with," iterative imperfect indicating habitual action. **Ἀγαμέμνονι δίῳ** (dat. sg., proper name + epithet): "to godlike Agamemnon," dative object of the verb of abuse now being described.

lines.original: ὀξέα κεκλήγων λέγʼ ὀνείδεα· τῷ δʼ ἄρʼ Ἀχαιοὶ
lines.english: shouting sharp rebukes he spoke words of reproach, and at him the Achaeans
lines.gloss: **ὀξέα** (adj., nom./acc. pl. neut., "sharp, piercing") modifies **ὀνείδεα** (noun, acc. pl. neut., "reproaches, taunts"), the object of **λέγʼ** (= ἔλεγε, impf. 3rd sg., "he spoke, he uttered"). **κεκλήγων** (perf. ptcp., nom. sg. masc., "shouting, crying out") describes the manner of speaking. **τῷ** (dem. pron., dat. sg., "at this, therefore") introduces the reaction, with **Ἀχαιοί** (nom. pl., "the Achaeans") as the subject of the following clause.

lines.original: ἐκπάγλως κοτέοντο νεμέσσηθέν τʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ.
lines.english: They were terribly angry and felt indignation in their hearts.
lines.gloss:
**ἐκπάγλως** (adv.): "exceedingly, terribly" – intensifying adverb modifying the verb, emphasizing the extreme degree of the Achaeans' anger.

**κοτέοντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid. κοτέω): "they were angry" – describes the Achaeans' wrathful reaction to Thersites' abuse of Agamemnon.

**νεμέσσηθέν** (3rd pl. aor. mid. νεμεσσάομαι): "they felt indignation" – expresses moral disapproval or righteous anger.

**θυμῷ** (dat. sg. θυμός): "in (their) heart/spirit" – locative dative indicating where the indignation was felt. The line conveys that the Achaeans were exceedingly angry and felt indign

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ὃ μακρὰ βοῶν Ἀγαμέμνονα νείκεε μύθῳ·
lines.english: But he loudly rebuked Agamemnon with words.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** *αὐτάρ* (conjunction, "but, then"); *μακρά* (adverbial accusative neuter plural of μακρός, "at length, loudly"); *βοῶν* (present active participle nominative singular masculine of βοάω, "shouting, crying out"); *νείκεε* (imperfect active 3rd singular of νεικέω, "he reviled, rebuked"); *μύθῳ* (dative singular of μῦθος, "with a speech, in words"). 

Achilles loudly and repeatedly reviles Agamemnon with abusive speech, the participle *βοῶν* emphasizing his vehement shouting.

lines.original: ὣς φάτο νεικείων Ἀγαμέμνονα ποιμένα λαῶν,
lines.english: Thus he spoke reviling Agamemnon shepherd of the people,
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus," "in this way," referring back to Thersites' manner of speaking. **φάτο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic., φημί): "he spoke." **νεικείων** (pres. act. participle, nom. sg. masc., νεικέω): "reviling," "reproaching." **Ἀγαμέμνονα** (acc. sg., proper name): direct object of νεικείων. **ποιμένα λαῶν** (acc. sg., ποιμήν + gen. pl., λαοί): "shepherd of the people," a traditional epithet for leaders.

The line describes how Thersites spoke in this reviling manner against Agamemnon, the shepherd of the people.

lines.original: Θερσίτης· τῷ δʼ ὦκα παρίστατο δῖος Ὀδυσσεύς,
lines.english: Thersites; but swift beside him stood godlike Odysseus.
lines.gloss: **Θερσίτης** (nom. sg. masc.): Thersites, the insubordinate commoner who rails against Agamemnon. **τῷ** (dat. sg. masc.): dative of disadvantage, "against him" or "beside him." **ὦκα** (adv.): "swiftly, quickly." **παρίστατο** (3rd sg. impf. mid.): "stood beside, confronted" (from παρίστημι). **δῖος** (nom. sg. masc.): "noble, godlike," epithet modifying Odysseus. After Thersites spoke, noble Odysseus swiftly stood beside him (to rebuke him).

lines.original: καί μιν ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν χαλεπῷ ἠνίπαπε μύθῳ·
lines.english: Looking at him darkly he rebuked him with harsh words.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.245:**

**ὑπόδρα** (adverb): "scowling, with a dark look," modifying the participle *ἰδών*. **ἰδών** (aorist participle, masculine nominative singular of *ὁράω*): "having looked at, looking at," describing Odysseus's manner. **χαλεπῷ** (adjective, dative singular): "harsh, stern," modifying *μύθῳ*. **ἠνίπαπε** (aorist indicative, 3rd singular of *ἐνίπτω*): "he rebuked, he chided." **μύθῳ** (noun, dative singular): "with a word, with speech," dative of means. Odysseus looks darkly at Thersites and rebukes him with a harsh word.

lines.original: ὣς ἄρʼ ἔφη, σκήπτρῳ δὲ μετάφρενον ἠδὲ καὶ ὤμω
lines.english: So he spoke, and with his scepter struck his back and shoulders.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ἄρʼ ἔφη, σκήπτρῳ δὲ μετάφρενον ἠδὲ καὶ ὤμω**

Key words: **ὣς** (adverb) "thus, so"; **ἔφη** (3rd sg. imperfect, φημί) "he spoke"; **σκήπτρῳ** (dat. sg. neuter, σκῆπτρον) "with the staff/scepter" (instrumental); **μετάφρενον** (acc. sg. neuter, μετάφρενον) "back, upper back"; **ὤμω** (acc. dual, ὦμος) "shoulders." Having spoken thus, he struck his back and both shoulders with the scepter.

lines.original: πλῆξεν· ὃ δʼ ἰδνώθη, θαλερὸν δέ οἱ ἔκπεσε δάκρυ·
lines.english: He struck him, and he cowered, and a thick tear fell from him.
lines.gloss: **πλῆξεν** (aorist active indicative, 3rd singular of πλήσσω): "he struck." **ἰδνώθη** (aorist passive indicative, 3rd singular of ἰδνόομαι): "he crouched down" or "he shrank back." **θαλερὸν** (adjective, accusative singular neuter, modifying δάκρυ): "warm, fresh." **ἔκπεσε** (aorist active indicative, 3rd singular of ἐκπίπτω): "fell out, fell down." **δάκρυ** (noun, nominative/accusative singular neuter): "tear." Odysseus struck the commoner, who shrank back as a warm tear fell from his eye.

lines.original: σμῶδιξ δʼ αἱματόεσσα μεταφρένου ἐξυπανέστη
lines.english: A bloody welt rose up upon his back.
lines.gloss:
**σμῶδιξ** (nom. sg. fem.): "stripe, welt"; subject of ἐξυπανέστη. **αἱματόεσσα** (nom. sg. fem.): "bloody, bloodied"; adjective modifying σμῶδιξ. **μεταφρένου** (gen. sg. neut.): "back, shoulders" (literally "between the midriff"); genitive of place from which. **ἐξυπανέστη** (3rd sg. aor. ind. mid.): "rose up, swelled up" (from ἐξ-υπ-ανίστημι); main verb. 

A bloody welt swelled up on his back (from the blow of the golden scepter).

lines.original: σκήπτρου ὕπο χρυσέου· ὃ δʼ ἄρʼ ἕζετο τάρβησέν τε,
lines.english: under the golden scepter, and he sat down in fear.
lines.gloss: **σκήπτρου** (genitive singular neuter of σκῆπτρον): "of the scepter" – instrument or means. **ὕπο** (preposition + genitive): "under, by" – indicating agency or means. **χρυσέου** (genitive singular neuter of χρύσεος): "golden" – modifying σκήπτρου. **ἕζετο** (3rd singular aorist middle indicative of ἕζομαι): "he sat down." **τάρβησέν** (3rd singular aorist active indicative of ταρβέω): "he was afraid, he feared." The line describes someone sitting down in fear under the threat of a golden scepter.

lines.original: ἀλγήσας δʼ ἀχρεῖον ἰδὼν ἀπομόρξατο δάκρυ.
lines.english: In pain and seeing himself as worthless, he wiped away a tear.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλγήσας** (aorist participle, nominative singular masculine from ἀλγέω): "grieving" or "pained." **ἀχρεῖον** (adjective, accusative singular neuter): "useless" or "worthless," modifying an implied or understood object. **ἰδών** (aorist participle from ὁράω): "seeing" or "having seen." **ἀπομόρξατο** (aorist middle, 3rd singular from ἀπομόρσσω): "wiped away." **δάκρυ** (noun, accusative singular neuter): "tear." 

The line describes someone who, grieving and seeing something as useless/futile, wiped away a tear.

lines.original: οἳ δὲ καὶ ἀχνύμενοί περ ἐπʼ αὐτῷ ἡδὺ γέλασσαν·
lines.english: They, though grieved for him, laughed sweetly at it.
lines.gloss:
**οἳ δὲ καὶ ἀχνύμενοί περ ἐπʼ αὐτῷ ἡδὺ γέλασσαν·**

**ἀχνύμενοί** (pres. mid. participle, nom. pl. masc. from ἄχνυμαι): "grieving, being distressed"; **περ** (enclitic particle): "although, even" (concessive with participle); **ἐπʼ αὐτῷ** (preposition + pronoun, dat. sg.): "at him/it"; **ἡδύ** (adverb, acc. as adverbial): "sweetly, pleasantly"; **γέλασσαν** (aor. act. indic., 3rd pl. from γελάω): "they laughed."

lines.original: ὧδε δέ τις εἴπεσκεν ἰδὼν ἐς πλησίον ἄλλον·
lines.english: And thus would a man speak looking at another beside him:
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Iliad line: ὧδε δέ τις εἴπεσκεν ἰδὼν ἐς πλησίον ἄλλον·**

*ὧδε* (adverb): "thus, in this way"; *τις* (indefinite pronoun, nominative singular): "someone, a certain one"; *εἴπεσκεν* (verb, 3rd singular imperfect iterative of εἶπον): "would say, kept saying" (indicating repeated action); *ἰδὼν* (participle, aorist active nominative singular masculine of ὁράω): "looking, having looked"; *πλησίον* (adverb/substantive with ἐς): "to his neighbor, to the one nearby." The line depicts individuals in the crowd repeatedly making similar remarks while glancing at those next to them.

lines.original: ὣς φάσαν ἣ πληθύς· ἀνὰ δʼ ὃ πτολίπορθος Ὀδυσσεὺς
lines.english: So spoke the multitude, and then Odysseus sacker of cities stood up.
lines.gloss:
**φάσαν** (φημί): 3rd pl. imperfect, "they were saying." **πληθύς** (πληθύς, -ύος, ἡ): nominative singular, "the throng, multitude." **ἀνὰ** (ἀνά): adverb (tmesis with ὤρορεν understood or ἔστη from next line), "up, arose." **πτολίπορθος** (πτολίπορθος, -ον): nominative singular masculine, epithet "sacker of cities." **Ὀδυσσεύς**: nominative singular, subject "Odysseus."

The multitude was speaking thus, and up rose Odysseus the sacker of cities.

lines.original: ἔστη σκῆπτρον ἔχων· παρὰ δὲ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη
lines.english: He stood holding his scepter, and beside him grey-eyed Athena stood.
lines.gloss: **ἔστη** (aorist, 3rd sg. of ἵστημι): "stood up" or "took his stand." **σκῆπτρον** (acc. sg. neuter): "scepter," object of **ἔχων** (pres. act. participle of ἔχω), "holding." **παρά** (adverb): "beside" or "nearby." **γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. epithet): "gray-eyed" or "flashing-eyed," modifying **Ἀθήνη**. Odysseus stands holding the scepter while gray-eyed Athena stands nearby.

lines.original: εἰδομένη κήρυκι σιωπᾶν λαὸν ἀνώγει,
lines.english: Looking like a herald she commanded the army to be silent
lines.gloss: **εἰδομένη** (pf. mid./pass. participle, nom. sg. fem., from *εἴδομαι*): "having made herself like, resembling" (Athena disguised as a herald). **κήρυκι** (dat. sg. masc.): "to/as a herald." **σιωπᾶν** (pres. inf.): "to be silent." **ἀνώγει** (pres. indic. 3rd sg., from *ἄνωγα*): "she commands, bids." Athena, disguised as a herald, commands the host to be silent so all might hear Agamemnon's speech.

lines.original: ὡς ἅμα θʼ οἳ πρῶτοί τε καὶ ὕστατοι υἷες Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: so that both the first and the last of the sons of the Achaeans
lines.gloss: **ὡς** (adverb): "so that," expressing purpose. **πρῶτοί** (adjective, nominative plural masculine): "first," modifying "sons." **ὕστατοι** (adjective, nominative plural masculine): "last" or "hindmost," paired with πρῶτοί to indicate all ranks. **υἷες** (noun, nominative plural): "sons." **Ἀχαιῶν** (noun, genitive plural): "of the Achaeans," the Greeks. The line emphasizes that all ranks of the Greek army, from front to back, might hear the message.

lines.original: μῦθον ἀκούσειαν καὶ ἐπιφρασσαίατο βουλήν·
lines.english: that they might hear his speech and consider his counsel
lines.gloss: **μῦθον** (accusative singular of μῦθος): "speech, word" - direct object of ἀκούσειαν. **ἀκούσειαν** (3rd plural aorist optative active of ἀκούω): "might hear, would hear" - optative in purpose clause. **ἐπιφρασσαίατο** (3rd plural aorist optative middle of ἐπιφράζομαι): "might consider, mark well" - coordinate with ἀκούσειαν. **βουλήν** (accusative singular of βουλή): "counsel, plan" - direct object of ἐπιφρασσαίατο. The line expresses purpose: "that they might hear his speech and mark well his counsel."

lines.original: ὅ σφιν ἐὺ φρονέων ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπεν·
lines.english: who spoke among them with good sense and addressed them thus
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** σφιν (σφι, dat. pl. pronoun) "for them/to them"; ἐὺ φρονέων (εὖ φρονέω, pres. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc.) "thinking well, being well-disposed"; ἀγορήσατο (ἀγορεύω, aor. mid. indic. 3rd sg.) "spoke in assembly, addressed"; μετέειπεν (μετα-εἶπον, aor. act. indic. 3rd sg.) "spoke among them, addressed."

The speaker addresses them with good intention and speaks in assembly.

lines.original: ὣς ἔφατʼ, Ἀργεῖοι δὲ μέγʼ ἴαχον, ἀμφὶ δὲ νῆες
lines.english: So he spoke, and the Argives shouted loud, and all around the ships
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" – marks the close of Nestor's speech.
**ἔφατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί): "he spoke" – the subject is the wise counselor from the previous line.
**Ἀργεῖοι** (nom. pl. masc.): "the Argives" – the Greek forces responding.
**ἴαχον** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of ἰάχω): "shouted, cried out" – their vocal approval.
**νῆες** (nom. pl. fem. of ναῦς): "ships" – the hollow ships resound in response to the Achaean roar, as the next line confirms.

lines.original: σμερδαλέον κονάβησαν ἀϋσάντων ὑπʼ Ἀχαιῶν,
lines.english: The ships echoed terribly at the shouting of the Achaeans.
lines.gloss: **σμερδαλέον** (adverb, "terribly, dreadfully") modifies **κονάβησαν** (3rd pl. aorist indicative of κοναβέω, "resounded, rang out"), describing the ships' reverberating noise. **ἀϋσάντων** (aorist active participle gen. pl. of ἀΰω, "shouting") with **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl., "of the Achaeans") forms a genitive absolute: "as the Achaeans shouted." The ships resounded terribly under/from the shouting Achaeans.

lines.original: μῦθον ἐπαινήσαντες Ὀδυσσῆος θείοιο·
lines.english: praising the speech of godlike Odysseus
