lines.gloss: **μῦθον** (accusative singular of μῦθος): "speech" or "plan," object of ἐπαινήσαντες. **ἐπαινήσαντες** (aorist active participle, nominative plural masculine of ἐπαινέω): "having praised" or "approving," modifying an understood subject (the Achaeans). **Ὀδυσσῆος** (genitive singular of Ὀδυσσεύς): "of Odysseus," possessive genitive with μῦθον. **θείοιο** (genitive singular of θεῖος): "godlike" or "divine," epithet modifying Ὀδυσσῆος. The Achaeans approved the speech of godlike Odysseus.

lines.original: τοῖσι δὲ καὶ μετέειπε Γερήνιος ἱππότα Νέστωρ·
lines.english: Then Gerenian horseman Nestor also spoke among them.
lines.gloss: **τοῖσι** (dat. pl. demonstrative pronoun) "to them"; **μετέειπε** (3rd sg. aor. indic. of μετα-ειπεῖν) "spoke among/after"; **Γερήνιος** (nom. sg. adj.) "Gerenian" (epithet); **ἱππότα** (nom. sg. m. noun/epithet) "horseman, knight"; **Νέστωρ** (nom. sg. proper noun) "Nestor." Nestor of Gerenia, the horseman, then spoke among them in response.

lines.original: τὸν δʼ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων·
lines.english: Then in answer to him spoke lord Agamemnon.
lines.gloss:
**ἀπαμειβόμενος** (present middle participle, nominative singular masculine, from ἀπαμείβομαι): "answering in turn, replying"
**προσέφη** (3rd singular aorist indicative active, from προσφημί): "addressed, spoke to"
**κρείων** (present active participle, nominative singular masculine, from κρείω, used as epithet): "ruling, lordly"
**Ἀγαμέμνων** (nominative singular proper noun): "Agamemnon"

Agamemnon, lord of men, answers Nestor's speech with a formal reply, the participle ἀπαμειβόμενος marking the exchange pattern typical of Homeric dialogue.

lines.original: ὣς ἔφατʼ, Ἀργεῖοι δὲ μέγʼ ἴαχον ὡς ὅτε κῦμα
lines.english: So he spoke, and the Argives shouted loud as a wave
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ἔφατʼ, Ἀργεῖοι δὲ μέγʼ ἴαχον ὡς ὅτε κῦμα**

Key words: **ἔφατʼ** (3rd sg. aor. ind. mid. of φημί, "he spoke"); **Ἀργεῖοι** (nom. pl. masc., "the Argives"); **ἴαχον** (3rd pl. aor. ind. of ἰάχω, "they shouted"); **ὡς ὅτε** (comparative formula, "as when"); **κῦμα** (nom. sg. neut., "wave"). The simile compares the Argives' shouting response to a wave, introducing an extended maritime comparison.

lines.original: ἀκτῇ ἐφʼ ὑψηλῇ, ὅτε κινήσῃ Νότος ἐλθών,
lines.english: against a high cliff when the South Wind stirs it up upon arriving
lines.gloss: **ἀκτῇ** (dat. sg. fem. of ἀκτή): "on/against the headland/shore"; **ἐφʼ** (prep. ἐπί with elision): "upon"; **ὑψηλῇ** (dat. sg. fem. of ὑψηλός): "high, lofty"; **κινήσῃ** (3rd sg. aor. subj. act. of κινέω): "should stir up, set in motion"; **Νότος** (nom. sg. masc.): "the South Wind." The simile continues: the Achaeans' shouting is compared to waves against a high headland whenever the South Wind comes and stirs them up.

lines.original: προβλῆτι σκοπέλῳ· τὸν δʼ οὔ ποτε κύματα λείπει
lines.english: on a jutting rock which the waves never leave
lines.gloss: **προβλῆτι** (dat. sg. masc. pres. part. of προβάλλω): "jutting out," modifying σκοπέλῳ. **σκοπέλῳ** (dat. sg. masc. noun): "cliff, rock." **κύματα** (nom. pl. neut. noun): "waves," subject of λείπει. **λείπει** (3rd sg. pres. indic. of λείπω): "leaves, abandons." The line describes a projecting cliff that the waves never leave—an image of perpetual assault, completing the simile of Paris facing the Greeks' relentless attacks.

lines.original: παντοίων ἀνέμων, ὅτʼ ἂν ἔνθʼ ἢ ἔνθα γένωνται.
lines.english: from winds of every kind, whenever they arise from this side or that
lines.gloss:
**παντοίων** (gen. pl. adj. of παντοῖος) "of all kinds," modifies ἀνέμων. **ἀνέμων** (gen. pl. of ἄνεμος) "of winds," genitive of source or agent. **ὅτʼ ἂν** (ὅτε + ἄν) "whenever," introduces an indefinite temporal clause. **γένωνται** (3rd pl. aor. subj. mid. of γίγνομαι) "they come to be/arise," subjunctive with ἄν expressing general condition. 

The line describes winds of every kind, whenever they arise from one direction or another, completing the simile of the rock constantly battered by waves and winds.

lines.original: ἀνστάντες δʼ ὀρέοντο κεδασθέντες κατὰ νῆας,
lines.english: Rising up they scattered and rushed back to their ships.
lines.gloss: **ἀνστάντες** (ἀνίστημι, aorist participle nominative plural masculine): "having stood up, arising." **ὀρέοντο** (ὄρνυμι, imperfect middle 3rd plural): "they stirred themselves, set out." **κεδασθέντες** (κεδάννυμι, aorist passive participle nominative plural masculine): "having been scattered, dispersing." **κατὰ νῆας**: "throughout the ships" (distributive). The Achaeans rise and make their way back, dispersing among their ships after the assembly.

lines.original: κάπνισσάν τε κατὰ κλισίας, καὶ δεῖπνον ἕλοντο.
lines.english: They kindled fires throughout the huts and took their meal.
lines.gloss:
**κάπνισσάν** (aorist, 3rd plural, καπνίζω): "they made burnt offerings," ritual smoking/sacrifice to the gods. **κατὰ κλισίας**: "throughout the huts," prepositional phrase indicating distribution across the camp shelters. **δεῖπνον** (accusative singular neuter): "dinner/meal," object of ἕλοντο. **ἕλοντο** (aorist middle, 3rd plural, αἱρέω): "they took (for themselves)," i.e., they partook of their meal.

The Achaeans, dispersed to their ships, performed sacrifice in their individual quarters and then took their evening meal.

lines.original: ἄλλος δʼ ἄλλῳ ἔρεζε θεῶν αἰειγενετάων
lines.english: Each man made sacrifice to a different one of the immortal gods.
lines.gloss:
**ἄλλος δʼ ἄλλῳ ἔρεζε θεῶν αἰειγενετάων**

**ἄλλος** (nom. sg. m., "one") and **ἄλλῳ** (dat. sg. m., "to another"): correlative pronouns indicating reciprocal distribution among the Greek warriors. **ἔρεζε** (3rd sg. impf. mid., < εὔχομαι, "prayed"): each man made prayer. **θεῶν** (gen. pl., < θεός, "of the gods") and **αἰειγενετάων** (gen. pl. m., < αἰειγενέτης, "ever-living, eternal"): descriptive genitive with the compound epithet emphasizing divine immortality. Each warrior prayed to a different immortal god

lines.original: εὐχόμενος θάνατόν τε φυγεῖν καὶ μῶλον Ἄρηος.
lines.english: praying to escape death and the turmoil of Ares
lines.gloss: **εὐχόμενος** (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. masc. of εὔχομαι): "praying," modifying the subject (Agamemnon); **θάνατόν** (acc. sg. masc. of θάνατος): "death," object of φυγεῖν; **φυγεῖν** (aor. act. infinitive of φεύγω): "to escape," complementing εὐχόμενος; **μῶλον** (acc. sg. masc. of μῶλος): "toil, struggle," in apposition with θάνατόν; **Ἄρηος** (gen. sg. masc. of Ἄρης): "of Ares," genitive of possession modifying μῶλον. Agamemnon prays to escape death and the struggle

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ὃ βοῦν ἱέρευσε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: Then the lord of men Agamemnon sacrificed an ox.
lines.gloss:
**Iliad** line: "αὐτὰρ ὃ βοῦν ἱέρευσε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων"

**αὐτάρ** (conjunction): "but, and then" – marks transition to the main action. **βοῦν** (accusative singular of βοῦς): "ox, bull" – the sacrificial victim. **ἱέρευσε** (aorist indicative, 3rd singular of ἱερεύω): "sacrificed, slaughtered for ritual purposes." **ἄναξ** (nominative singular): "lord, king" – formulaic epithet. **Ἀγαμέμνων** (nominative): Agamemnon, the Greek commander, performs the sacrifice.

lines.original: πίονα πενταέτηρον ὑπερμενέϊ Κρονίωνι,
lines.english: a fat five-year-old bull to the mighty son of Kronos
lines.gloss: **πίονα** (adj., acc. sing. masc.) "fat, sleek" modifies the bull being sacrificed. **πενταέτηρον** (adj., acc. sing. masc.) "five years old" specifies the age of the sacrificial victim. **ὑπερμενέϊ** (adj., dat. sing. masc.) "exceeding mighty, very powerful" modifies **Κρονίωνι** (noun, dat. sing. masc.) "son of Kronos," referring to Zeus as recipient of the sacrifice. Agamemnon sacrifices a prime five-year-old bull to Zeus.

lines.original: κίκλησκεν δὲ γέροντας ἀριστῆας Παναχαιῶν,
lines.english: He summoned the elders, the chieftains of all the Achaeans,
lines.gloss: **κίκλησκεν** (impf. act. ind. 3rd sg. of κικλήσκω) "he summoned" or "he was calling"; **γέροντας** (acc. pl. masc. of γέρων) "elders, old men"; **ἀριστῆας** (acc. pl. masc. of ἀριστεύς) "chiefs, best men"; **Παναχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Πανάχαιοι) "of all the Achaeans." Agamemnon summoned the elder chiefs from among all the Achaeans to a council.

lines.original: Νέστορα μὲν πρώτιστα καὶ Ἰδομενῆα ἄνακτα,
lines.english: Nestor first of all and lord Idomeneus,
lines.gloss:
**Νέστορα μὲν πρώτιστα καὶ Ἰδομενῆα ἄνακτα**

Νέστορα (acc. sg. of Νέστωρ): "Nestor," object of κίκλησκεν from previous line. πρώτιστα (adv., superlative of πρῶτος): "first of all," "very first." Ἰδομενῆα (acc. sg. of Ἰδομενεύς): "Idomeneus," Cretan leader, second object. ἄνακτα (acc. sg. of ἄναξ): "lord," "king," in apposition to Ἰδομενῆα. Agamemnon summons the elders, beginning with Nestor first and then lord Idomeneus.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἔπειτʼ Αἴαντε δύω καὶ Τυδέος υἱόν,
lines.english: and then the two Ajaxes and the son of Tydeus
lines.gloss:
**αὐτὰρ ἔπειτʼ** (adverb + adverb): "but then," "next" - transitional formula marking sequence in the narrative.

**Αἴαντε** (noun, acc. dual, masc.): "the two Ajaxes" - dual form referring to Ajax son of Telamon and Ajax son of Oïleus.

**δύω** (numeral, acc. dual): "two" - emphasizing the pair.

**Τυδέος υἱόν** (noun gen. + noun acc.): "son of Tydeus" - patronymic periphrasis for Diomedes.

The line continues the catalogue of summoned leaders, now naming the two Ajaxes and Diomedes.

lines.original: ἕκτον δʼ αὖτʼ Ὀδυσῆα Διὶ μῆτιν ἀτάλαντον.
lines.english: and sixth again Odysseus equal to Zeus in counsel.
lines.gloss: **ἕκτον** (adjective, accusative singular masculine) "sixth" - ordinal number modifying Odysseus in the sequence of warriors summoned. **Ὀδυσῆα** (proper noun, accusative singular) "Odysseus" - object of an implied verb of summoning. **Διὶ** (proper noun, dative singular) "to Zeus" - dative of comparison. **μῆτιν** (noun, accusative singular feminine) "in counsel/cunning" - accusative of respect. **ἀτάλαντον** (adjective, accusative singular masculine) "equal, comparable" - agreeing with Odysseus, describing him as Zeus's equal in strategic intelligence.

lines.original: αὐτόματος δέ οἱ ἦλθε βοὴν ἀγαθὸς Μενέλαος·
lines.english: And Menelaus good at the war cry came to him of his own accord.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** αὐτόματος (nominative singular masculine adjective) "of his own accord, unbidden"; ἦλθε (3rd singular aorist indicative of ἔρχομαι) "came"; βοὴν ἀγαθός (nominative singular masculine, formulaic epithet) "good at the war cry, good in battle," modifying Μενέλαος.

Menelaus, good at the war cry, came to him unbidden/of his own accord (without being summoned).

lines.original: ᾔδεε γὰρ κατὰ θυμὸν ἀδελφεὸν ὡς ἐπονεῖτο.
lines.english: For he knew in his heart how his brother was laboring.
lines.gloss:
**ᾔδεε** (pluperfect, 3rd sg. of οἶδα): "he knew"; **κατὰ θυμόν**: "in his heart/mind" (prepositional phrase); **ἀδελφεός** (acc. sg. masc.): "brother"; **ὡς**: "how" (conjunction); **ἐπονεῖτο** (impf. mid./pass., 3rd sg. of πονέομαι): "was toiling/distressed." 

Menelaus intuitively knew in his heart how his brother was laboring or in distress, prompting his spontaneous arrival to help.

lines.original: βοῦν δὲ περιστήσαντο καὶ οὐλοχύτας ἀνέλοντο·
lines.english: They stood around the ox and took up the barley grains.
lines.gloss: **βοῦν** (acc. sg. m. of βοῦς) "ox/bull," direct object of περιστήσαντο. **περιστήσαντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. indic. of περιίστημι) "they stood around," the preparatory ritual action. **οὐλοχύτας** (acc. pl. f. of οὐλοχύτη) "barley grains," ritual grain scattered on the victim. **ἀνέλοντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. indic. of ἀναιρέω) "they took up/lifted." The line describes the initial sacrificial ritual: they stood around the bull and took up the sacred barley grains to scatter.

lines.original: τοῖσιν δʼ εὐχόμενος μετέφη κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων·
lines.english: Praying among them spoke lord Agamemnon.
lines.gloss: **τοῖσιν** (dative plural demonstrative pronoun) "among them/to these"; **εὐχόμενος** (present middle participle, nominative singular masculine) "praying, making a vow"; **μετέφη** (3rd singular aorist middle indicative of μεταφημί) "spoke among, addressed"; **κρείων** (nominative singular masculine present participle of κρείω) "ruling, lord"; **Ἀγαμέμνων** (nominative singular) "Agamemnon." Lord Agamemnon spoke among them while praying/making his vow.

lines.original: ὣς ἔφατʼ, οὐδʼ ἄρα πώ οἱ ἐπεκραίαινε Κρονίων,
lines.english: So he spoke, but the son of Cronus did not yet bring it to fulfillment for him.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" – marks the conclusion of Agamemnon's prayer.

**ἔφατʼ** (3rd sg. impf. mid., φημί): "he spoke" – refers to Agamemnon's prayer just completed.

**ἐπεκραίαινε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἐπικραιαίνω): "was fulfilling, was granting" – the negated verb indicates Zeus's refusal.

**Κρονίων** (nom. sg. masc., Κρονίων): "son of Kronos, Zeus" – the subject who does not yet grant the prayer.

The line marks the tragic irony: Agamemnon spoke thus, but the son of Kronos was not yet fulfilling his prayer for him.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὅ γε δέκτο μὲν ἱρά, πόνον δʼ ἀμέγαρτον ὄφελλεν.
lines.english: but he accepted the sacrifice yet increased their immeasurable toil
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** δέκτο (3rd sg. impf. mid. δέχομαι) "he received"; ἱρά (n. pl. acc. ἱερόν) "sacrifices, offerings"; πόνον (m. sg. acc. πόνος) "toil, suffering"; ἀμέγαρτον (m. sg. acc. ἀμέγαρτος) "unenvied, grievous"; ὄφελλεν (3rd sg. impf. ὀφέλλω) "he was heaping up, increasing."

The verse depicts Zeus accepting the sacrifices but simultaneously increasing grievous suffering—the contrast between μέν and δέ emphasizes the ironic disparity between receiving worship and granting disaster.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεί ῥʼ εὔξαντο καὶ οὐλοχύτας προβάλοντο,
lines.english: But when they had prayed and scattered the barley grains,
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** εὔξαντο (aorist middle, 3rd pl. of εὔχομαι, "they prayed"), οὐλοχύτας (acc. pl. of οὐλοχύται, "barley grains" for ritual sprinkling), προβάλοντο (aorist middle, 3rd pl. of προβάλλω, "they threw forward/scattered"). 

**Gloss:** This line describes the preliminary ritual actions of sacrifice: after they prayed and scattered the barley grains (a standard opening to Greek animal sacrifice), the next verse will detail the actual slaughter.

lines.original: αὐέρυσαν μὲν πρῶτα καὶ ἔσφαξαν καὶ ἔδειραν,
lines.english: They first drew back the heads and slaughtered and flayed them.
lines.gloss: **αὐέρυσαν** (ἀνερύω, 3rd pl. aor. indic. act.) "they drew back [the victims' heads]"; **πρῶτα** (adv.) "first"; **ἔσφαξαν** (σφάζω, 3rd pl. aor. indic. act.) "they slaughtered"; **ἔδειραν** (δέρω, 3rd pl. aor. indic. act.) "they flayed." This line describes the initial stages of sacrificial ritual: drawing back the victims' heads, slaughtering them, and flaying the carcasses, with **μέν** anticipating a subsequent step in the procedure.

lines.original: μηρούς τʼ ἐξέταμον κατά τε κνίσῃ ἐκάλυψαν
lines.english: They cut out the thigh pieces and covered them with fat.
lines.gloss:
**μηρούς** (acc. pl. masc. of μηρός): thighs, the portions cut for the gods. **ἐξέταμον** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of ἐκτέμνω): they cut out. **κατά** (tmesis with ἐκάλυψαν): over, upon. **κνίσῃ** (dat. sg. fem. of κνίσα/κνίση): fat. **ἐκάλυψαν** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of καλύπτω): they covered.

They cut out the thigh-bones and covered them over with fat, the standard ritual preparation for burning portions offered to the gods.

lines.original: δίπτυχα ποιήσαντες, ἐπʼ αὐτῶν δʼ ὠμοθέτησαν.
lines.english: They made them double-folded and placed the raw meat upon them.
lines.gloss: **δίπτυχα** (adj. acc. pl. neut.) "double-folded," modifying an understood object (the thigh pieces); **ποιήσαντες** (aor. act. ptc. nom. pl. masc. from ποιέω) "having made"; **ἐπ' αὐτῶν** (prep. + gen. pl.) "upon them"; **ὠμοθέτησαν** (aor. act. ind. 3rd pl. from ὠμοθετέω) "they placed raw flesh." Having made the thigh pieces double-folded, they placed raw meat upon them before burning.

lines.original: καὶ τὰ μὲν ἂρ σχίζῃσιν ἀφύλλοισιν κατέκαιον,
lines.english: They burned these upon stripped sticks after splitting them.
lines.gloss:
**καὶ τὰ μὲν ἂρ σχίζῃσιν ἀφύλλοισιν κατέκαιον:**

**τὰ** (neuter plural accusative, demonstrative pronoun): "these things," referring to the thigh pieces wrapped in fat; **σχίζῃσιν** (dative plural, from σχίζα): "on split wood" or "on spits/kindling"; **ἀφύλλοισιν** (dative plural adjective, from ἄφυλλος): "leafless," modifying σχίζῃσιν; **κατέκαιον** (3rd plural imperfect active, from κατακαίω): "they were burning" or "they burned up/consumed." The line describes the ritual burning of the thigh bones wrapped in fat on stripped sticks during

lines.original: σπλάγχνα δʼ ἄρʼ ἀμπείραντες ὑπείρεχον Ἡφαίστοιο.
lines.english: They spitted the inner parts and held them over Hephaestus's flame.
lines.gloss: **σπλάγχνα** (neuter accusative plural, "inner organs, entrails") is the direct object of **ἀμπείραντες** (aorist active participle, nominative plural masculine, from ἀναπείρω, "having pierced through, having spitted"). **ὑπείρεχον** (imperfect active, 3rd plural, from ὑπερέχω, "they held over") describes how they held the spitted organs over **Ἡφαίστοιο** (genitive singular, "of Hephaestus," i.e., the fire). The line depicts the ritual roasting of sacrificial organs after burning the thigh-pieces.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ κατὰ μῆρε κάη καὶ σπλάγχνα πάσαντο,
lines.english: And when the thigh pieces were burned and they had tasted the inner parts,
lines.gloss: **αὐτὰρ** (particle) "but, and then" marks transition to next stage of sacrifice. **κατὰ ... κάη** (κατακαίω, aor. pass. 3rd sg.) "were burned down/consumed," describing the thighbones burned on altar. **μῆρε** (μηρός, acc. dual) "thighbones," the portions offered to gods. **σπλάγχνα** (σπλάγχνον, acc. pl. neut.) "inner organs, entrails." **πάσαντο** (πατέομαι, aor. mid. 3rd pl.) "they tasted, partook of," referring to ritual tasting of roasted organs.

lines.original: μίστυλλόν τʼ ἄρα τἆλλα καὶ ἀμφʼ ὀβελοῖσιν ἔπειραν,
lines.english: They cut up the rest into pieces and threaded them on spits.
lines.gloss:
**μίστυλλον** (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of μιστυλλέω): "they cut up (the meat into small pieces)"; **τἆλλα** (= τὰ ἄλλα, acc. pl. neut. of ἄλλος): "the rest, the remaining parts"; **ὀβελοῖσιν** (dat. pl. of ὀβελός): "on/with spits"; **ἔπειραν** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of πείρω): "they pierced, threaded."

After the thigh pieces burned and they tasted the entrails, they cut up the remaining meat and pierced it onto spits in preparation for roasting.

lines.original: ὤπτησάν τε περιφραδέως, ἐρύσαντό τε πάντα.
lines.english: They roasted everything carefully and drew all the meat from the spits.
lines.gloss: **ὤπτησαν** (ὀπτάω, 3rd pl. aor. act. indic.) "they roasted"; **περιφραδέως** (adv.) "skillfully, with care"; **ἐρύσαντο** (ἐρύω, 3rd pl. aor. mid. indic.) "they drew off, pulled [from the spits]"; **πάντα** (πᾶς, neut. acc. pl., substantive) "all things, everything." The line describes the completion of roasting the meat carefully and removing it all from the spits.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ παύσαντο πόνου τετύκοντό τε δαῖτα
lines.english: But when they had ceased from toil and prepared the feast
lines.gloss: **αὐτὰρ** (particle): "but, and then" (transitional conjunction). **ἐπεὶ** (conjunction): "when, after" (+ aorist). **παύσαντο** (verb): 3rd pl. aorist middle indicative of παύω, "they ceased, stopped" (from labor). **τετύκοντο** (verb): 3rd pl. pluperfect middle indicative of τεύχω, "they had prepared, made ready." The line marks the transition from food preparation to feasting: after they stopped their labor and had prepared the meal.

lines.original: δαίνυντʼ, οὐδέ τι θυμὸς ἐδεύετο δαιτὸς ἐΐσης.
lines.english: They feasted, and their hearts lacked nothing of the equal feast.
lines.gloss:
**δαίνυντʼ** (δαίνυνται, 3rd pl. impf. mid., "they feasted"); **θυμός** (nom. sg., "heart, spirit"); **ἐδεύετο** (3rd sg. impf. mid. of δεύομαι, "lacked, wanted"); **δαιτός** (gen. sg. fem., "feast, banquet"); **ἐΐσης** (gen. sg. fem. of ἐΐσος, "equal, fair"). 

They feasted, and no one's heart lacked anything of the equal/well-shared banquet—a typical Homeric formula indicating satisfying hospitality where all received proper portions.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ ἐπεὶ πόσιος καὶ ἐδητύος ἐξ ἔρον ἕντο,
lines.english: But when they had put away their desire for food and drink
lines.gloss: **ἐπεί** (conjunction) "when, after"; **πόσιος** (gen. sg. of πόσις) "of drink"; **ἐδητύος** (gen. sg. of ἐδητύς) "of food"; **ἔρον** (acc. sg. of ἔρος) "desire, appetite"; **ἕντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. of ἵημι) "they satisfied, put from themselves." The line marks the transition from feasting to speech: "But when they had satisfied their desire for food and drink."

lines.original: τοῖς ἄρα μύθων ἦρχε Γερήνιος ἱππότα Νέστωρ·
lines.english: Then the Gerenian horseman Nestor began to speak among them.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** τοῖς (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural, "to them/among them"), ἦρχε (verb, 3rd singular imperfect active indicative of ἄρχω, "began"), Γερήνιος (adjective, nominative singular masculine, "Gerenian," epithet of Nestor), ἱππότα (noun, nominative singular masculine, "horseman/knight," epithet), Νέστωρ (proper noun, nominative singular, "Nestor"). 

Among them Gerenian Nestor the horseman began his speech; the imperfect ἦρχε introduces Nestor's direct address.

lines.original: ὣς ἔφατʼ, οὐδʼ ἀπίθησεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων.
lines.english: So he spoke, and Agamemnon lord of men did not disobey.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ἔφατʼ, οὐδʼ ἀπίθησεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων.**

Key words: **ἔφατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί, "he spoke"), **ἀπίθησεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἀπιθέω, "disobeyed," here negated by οὐδέ), **ἄναξ** (nom. sg. masc., "lord, king"), **ἀνδρῶν** (gen. pl. of ἀνήρ, "of men"). Thus he spoke, and the lord of men Agamemnon did not disobey.

lines.original: αὐτίκα κηρύκεσσι λιγυφθόγγοισι κέλευσε
lines.english: He commanded the clear-voiced heralds at once
lines.gloss: **αὐτίκα** (adv.): immediately, at once. **κηρύκεσσι** (dat. pl. of κῆρυξ): to the heralds. **λιγυφθόγγοισι** (adj. dat. pl., modifying κηρύκεσσι): clear-voiced, loud-voiced. **κέλευσε** (3rd sg. aor. ind. act. of κελεύω): he commanded, ordered. Agamemnon immediately commanded the clear-voiced heralds to summon the long-haired Achaeans to war.

lines.original: κηρύσσειν πόλεμον δὲ κάρη κομόωντας Ἀχαιούς·
lines.english: to proclaim war to the long-haired Achaeans.
lines.gloss: κηρύσσειν (present infinitive of κηρύσσω, "to proclaim") depends on κέλευσε from the previous line. πόλεμον (accusative singular masculine of πόλεμος, "war") is the object of κηρύσσειν. κάρη κομόωντας (accusative plural masculine present participle of κομάω, "wearing long hair") modifies Ἀχαιούς (accusative plural of Ἀχαιοί, "the Achaeans"), creating the traditional epithet "long-haired Achaeans." The infinitive construction completes Agamemnon's command to the heralds to summon the Greeks to war.

lines.original: οἳ μὲν ἐκήρυσσον, τοὶ δʼ ἠγείροντο μάλʼ ὦκα.
lines.english: The heralds made proclamation and the men gathered very swiftly.
lines.gloss:
**οἳ** (hoi): demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine, "these men" (the heralds).

**ἐκήρυσσον** (ekērysson): imperfect active 3rd plural of κηρύσσω, "were proclaiming/announcing" (the call to war).

**ἠγείροντο** (ēgeironto): imperfect middle/passive 3rd plural of ἐγείρω, "were gathering/being roused."

**μάλʼ ὦκα** (mal' ōka): adverbial phrase, "very swiftly/quickly" (elided μάλα + ὦκα).

The line contrasts the heralds' proclamation with the Achaeans' swift response to assemble.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἀμφʼ Ἀτρεΐωνα διοτρεφέες βασιλῆες
lines.english: The god-nurtured kings gathered around the sons of Atreus.
lines.gloss:
**οἳ** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "they" — δέ (postpositive particle) "and, but" — **ἀμφʼ** (preposition + acc., elided from ἀμφί) "around" — **Ἀτρεΐωνα** (acc. sg. masc., patronymic) "the son of Atreus" [Agamemnon] — **διοτρεφέες** (adj., nom. pl. masc.) "Zeus-nurtured, divinely fostered" — **βασιλῆες** (noun, nom. pl. masc.) "kings, chieftains." 

The chieftains gather around Agamemnon, contrasting with the general assembly being marshaled.

lines.original: θῦνον κρίνοντες, μετὰ δὲ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη
lines.english: The chiefs around the sons of Atreus rushed about marshaling the troops, and among them gleaming-eyed Athena.
lines.gloss: **θῦνον** (imperfect, 3rd pl. of θύνω): "were rushing about" or "were moving busily." **κρίνοντες** (pres. act. participle, nom. pl. masc. of κρίνω): "marshaling" or "arranging" (the troops). **μετὰ** (preposition + acc.): "among" (them). **γλαυκῶπις** (nom. sg. fem. epithet): "gray-eyed" or "bright-eyed." **Ἀθήνη** (nom. sg. fem.): "Athena." The kings rush about marshaling their forces, with gray-eyed Athena moving among them.

lines.original: αἰγίδʼ ἔχουσʼ ἐρίτιμον ἀγήρων ἀθανάτην τε,
lines.english: holding the aegis, precious, ageless and immortal,
lines.gloss: **αἰγίδα** (accusative singular feminine of αἰγίς): "aegis," the divine shield or breastplate of Athena. **ἔχουσα** (present active participle, nominative singular feminine of ἔχω): "holding" or "bearing." **ἐρίτιμον** (accusative singular feminine of ἐρίτιμος): "very precious" or "highly honored." **ἀγήρων** (accusative singular feminine of ἀγήρως): "ageless." **ἀθανάτην** (accusative singular feminine of ἀθάνατος): "immortal." Athena holds her aegis, described with three emphatic epithets emphasizing its divine, eternal nature as both precious and imperishable.

lines.original: τῆς ἑκατὸν θύσανοι παγχρύσεοι ἠερέθονται,
lines.english: from which a hundred golden tassels hung fluttering
lines.gloss:
**τῆς** (genitive singular feminine of ὁ ἡ τό): "of it/from it," referring to the aegis. **ἑκατόν** (indeclinable numeral): "hundred." **θύσανοι** (nominative plural masculine of θύσανος): "tassels, fringes." **παγχρύσεοι** (nominative plural masculine of παγχρύσεος): "all-golden, entirely of gold." **ἠερέθονται** (3rd plural present passive of ἠερέθομαι): "are suspended, hang down."

From the aegis a hundred all-golden tassels hang suspended, describing the ornate decoration of Athena's divine armor.

lines.original: πάντες ἐϋπλεκέες, ἑκατόμβοιος δὲ ἕκαστος·
lines.english: all finely woven, and each worth a hundred oxen.
lines.gloss: **πάντες** (πᾶς, nom. masc. pl.): "all," agreeing with θύσανοι from the previous line. **ἐϋπλεκέες** (ἐϋπλεκής, nom. masc. pl.): "well-plaited, finely woven," describing the tassels. **ἑκατόμβοιος** (ἑκατόμβοιος, gen. fem. sg.): "worth a hundred oxen," genitive of value modifying the following noun. **ἕκαστος** (ἕκαστος, nom. masc. sg.): "each one," emphasizing the individual value of each tassel. The line continues the description of Athena's aegis, noting that all the tassels are finely crafted and each is worth a hecatomb.

lines.original: σὺν τῇ παιφάσσουσα διέσσυτο λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: With her she rushed gleaming through the host of the Achaeans.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** σὺν τῇ (preposition + dative pronoun, "with her/it"), παιφάσσουσα (present participle nominative feminine singular from παιφάσσω, "flashing/glancing"), διέσσυτο (3rd singular aorist middle indicative from *διασεύομαι*, "rushed through/darted through"), λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν (accusative singular λαός + genitive plural, "the host of the Achaeans"). 

Athena, flashing with her aegis, rushed through the Achaean army, rousing each warrior's strength for battle.

lines.original: ὀτρύνουσʼ ἰέναι· ἐν δὲ σθένος ὦρσεν ἑκάστῳ
lines.english: urging them to go, and she stirred strength in the heart of each man
lines.gloss:
**ὀτρύνουσʼ ἰέναι· ἐν δὲ σθένος ὦρσεν ἑκάστῳ**

**ὀτρύνουσα** (pres. act. participle, nom. fem. sg. of ὀτρύνω): "urging, rousing"
**ἰέναι** (pres. inf. of εἶμι): "to go"
**σθένος** (noun, acc. neut. sg.): "strength, might"
**ὦρσεν** (aor. act. ind. 3rd sg. of ὄρνυμι): "she stirred up, roused"
**ἑκάστῳ** (adj./pron., dat. masc. sg.): "to each (man)"

Ath

lines.original: καρδίῃ ἄλληκτον πολεμίζειν ἠδὲ μάχεσθαι.
lines.english: in the heart unwearying strength to war and fight.
lines.gloss: **καρδίῃ** (dat. sing. fem. of καρδία): "in heart/spirit," dative of respect or location. **ἄλληκτον** (acc. sing. neut. of ἄλληκτος): "unceasingly, without pause," adverbial accusative modifying the infinitives. **πολεμίζειν** (pres. act. inf. of πολεμίζω): "to wage war." **μάχεσθαι** (pres. mid. inf. of μάχομαι): "to fight." The line describes their unwavering spirit to fight continuously, with complementary infinitives expressing the action they desire in their hearts.

lines.original: τοῖσι δʼ ἄφαρ πόλεμος γλυκίων γένετʼ ἠὲ νέεσθαι
lines.english: War became sweeter to them than returning home in their hollow ships.
lines.gloss:
**τοῖσι** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural): "for them/these men"
**ἄφαρ** (adverb): "straightaway, immediately"
**γλυκίων** (comparative adjective, nominative singular masculine): "sweeter," from γλυκύς
**γένετο** (verb, 3rd singular aorist middle indicative of γίγνομαι): "became"
**νέεσθαι** (verb, present middle infinitive of νέομαι): "to return (home)"

For these men, war immediately became sweeter than returning home, contrasting the goddess-induced battle-lust with the prospect of sailing back to their fatherland.

lines.original: ἐν νηυσὶ γλαφυρῇσι φίλην ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν.
lines.english: in their hollow ships to their dear native land
lines.gloss: **νηυσὶ** (noun, dative plural of ναῦς): "in ships," dative of place where or means. **γλαφυρῇσι** (adjective, dative plural feminine of γλαφυρός): "hollow, curved," modifying νηυσί. **φίλην** (adjective, accusative singular feminine of φίλος): "dear, beloved," modifying πατρίδα γαῖαν. **πατρίδα** (adjective, accusative singular feminine of πατρίς): "fatherland, native," with γαῖαν forming "native land." The line describes returning home in their hollow ships to their dear fatherland.

lines.original: ἠΰτε πῦρ ἀΐδηλον ἐπιφλέγει ἄσπετον ὕλην
lines.english: As a blazing fire consumes a vast forest.
lines.gloss:
**ἠΰτε πῦρ ἀΐδηλον ἐπιφλέγει ἄσπετον ὕλην**

**ἠΰτε** (conjunction): "just as," introduces epic simile comparing the gleam of weapons to fire. **πῦρ** (neuter nominative singular): "fire," subject of the simile. **ἀΐδηλον** (adjective, nominative neuter singular): "destructive, devouring," modifying πῦρ. **ἐπιφλέγει** (3rd singular present indicative): "blazes up, kindles," from ἐπιφλέγω. **ἄσπετον** (adjective, accusative feminine singular): "unspeakable, immense," modifying ὕλην. **ὕλην** (accusative

lines.original: οὔρεος ἐν κορυφῇς, ἕκαθεν δέ τε φαίνεται αὐγή,
lines.english: on a mountain peak, and the blaze is seen from afar
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** *οὔρεος* (gen. sg. of ὄρος) "of a mountain"; *κορυφῇς* (dat. pl. of κορυφή) "on the peaks"; *ἕκαθεν* (adv.) "from afar"; *φαίνεται* (3rd sg. pres. mid./pass. of φαίνω) "is seen, appears"; *αὐγή* (nom. sg.) "gleam, light."

The simile continues: the fire blazes on the mountain peaks, and from afar the gleam is visible—establishing the visual magnitude of the bronze armor's brightness across the moving Greek army.

lines.original: ὣς τῶν ἐρχομένων ἀπὸ χαλκοῦ θεσπεσίοιο
lines.english: so from them as they marched the gleam of their wondrous bronze flashed through the upper air to heaven
lines.gloss: **ὣς** (adverb): thus, so; introduces the comparison's application. **τῶν ἐρχομένων** (genitive plural masculine present participle of ἔρχομαι): "of them going/marching," referring to the advancing warriors. **ἀπὸ χαλκοῦ** (preposition + genitive singular): "from the bronze," indicating the source of the gleam from their armor. **θεσπεσίοιο** (genitive singular adjective): "wondrous, marvelous, god-sent," modifying χαλκοῦ and emphasizing the divine quality of their bronze equipment.

lines.original: αἴγλη παμφανόωσα διʼ αἰθέρος οὐρανὸν ἷκε.
lines.english: A gleaming radiance from the bronze reached through the bright air to heaven.
lines.gloss:
**αἴγλη** (nom. sg. fem., "gleam, radiance") **παμφανόωσα** (pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. fem. from παμφανάω, "shining all around, flashing brightly") **διʼ** (prep. + gen., δια with elision, "through") **αἰθέρος** (gen. sg. masc., "upper air, sky") **οὐρανὸν** (acc. sg. masc., "heaven, sky") **ἷκε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. from ἱκνέομαι, "reached, came to"). 

The gleaming radiance, flashing all around, reached through the upper air to heaven—describing the brilliant light reflecting from the bronze armor of the advancing warriors.

lines.original: τῶν δʼ ὥς τʼ ὀρνίθων πετεηνῶν ἔθνεα πολλὰ
lines.english: And of them as of winged birds many tribes
lines.gloss:
**τῶν** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive plural) "of them"; **ὀρνίθων** (noun, genitive plural from ὄρνις) "of birds"; **πετεηνῶν** (adjective, genitive plural from πετεηνός) "winged, flying"; **ἔθνεα** (noun, nominative/accusative plural from ἔθνος) "tribes, flocks"; **πολλά** (adjective, nominative/accusative plural neuter) "many." 

The line introduces a simile comparing the multitudes of warriors to many flocks of winged birds, with the genitive construction specifying "flocks of flying birds."

lines.original: χηνῶν ἢ γεράνων ἢ κύκνων δουλιχοδείρων
lines.english: geese or cranes or long-necked swans
lines.gloss:
**χηνῶν** (genitive plural of χήν): "of geese"; **γεράνων** (genitive plural of γέρανος): "of cranes"; **κύκνων** (genitive plural of κύκνος): "of swans"; **δουλιχοδείρων** (genitive plural adjective, modifying κύκνων): "long-necked." 

The line catalogs three types of waterfowl in genitive partitive construction, completing the simile comparing the numerous Greek tribes to flocks of birds; the compound epithet δουλιχοδείρων ("long-necked") applies specifically to the swans.

lines.original: Ἀσίω ἐν λειμῶνι Καϋστρίου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα
lines.english: in the Asian meadow around the streams of Cayster
lines.gloss:
**Ἀσίω ἐν λειμῶνι Καϋστρίου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα**

*Ἀσίω* (adj. dat. sg. neut.): "Asian," modifying *λειμῶνι*. *λειμῶνι* (noun dat. sg. masc.): "in the meadow," locative dative. *Καϋστρίου* (proper name gen. sg.): "of the Cayster," a river in Asia Minor near Ephesus. *ἀμφὴ* (prep. + acc.): "around, near." *ῥέεθρα* (noun acc. pl. neut.): "streams, waters." The birds settle around the flowing waters of the Cayster River in the Asian meadow.

lines.original: ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ποτῶνται ἀγαλλόμενα πτερύγεσσι
lines.english: darting here and there exulting in their wings
lines.gloss: **ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα** (adverb): "hither and thither," "in one direction and another"—a formulaic phrase indicating movement in all directions. **ποτῶνται** (3rd pl. pres. mid./pass. indic. of *ποτάομαι*): "they fly about," describing the birds' flight. **ἀγαλλόμενα** (nom./acc. pl. neut. pres. mid. participle of *ἀγάλλομαι*): "exulting," "glorying," modifying the birds in their joyful display. **πτερύγεσσι** (dat. pl. of *πτέρυξ*): "in their wings," instrumental dative expressing the means of their exultation.

lines.original: κλαγγηδὸν προκαθιζόντων, σμαραγεῖ δέ τε λειμών,
lines.english: settling down with clamor, and the meadow resounds beneath them
lines.gloss: **κλαγγηδόν** (adverb): "with clamor/din," describing the noisy settling down of the troops. **προκαθιζόντων** (present participle, genitive plural masculine from προκαθίζω): "of those sitting/settling down before," genitive absolute construction. **σμαραγεῖ** (present indicative, 3rd singular from σμαραγέω): "roars/resounds," the meadow echoes with sound. **λειμών** (nominative singular masculine): "meadow/plain," subject of the verb, the field where the troops gather.

lines.original: ὣς τῶν ἔθνεα πολλὰ νεῶν ἄπο καὶ κλισιάων
lines.english: So the many tribes from the ships and the huts poured forth into the Scamandrian plain.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" – drawing the simile's comparison between birds and Greek forces.

**ἔθνεα** (noun, nominative plural, neuter): "tribes, companies, bands" – the organized contingents of Greek warriors.

**νεῶν** (noun, genitive plural, feminine): "from the ships" – the beached Greek fleet at Troy.

**κλισιάων** (noun, genitive plural, feminine): "huts, barracks" – the temporary shelters of the Greek camp.

The countless Greek companies poured forth from their ships and encampments onto the plain.

lines.original: ἐς πεδίον προχέοντο Σκαμάνδριον· αὐτὰρ ὑπὸ χθὼν
lines.english: poured forth onto the Scamandrian plain, and beneath them the earth
lines.gloss:
**ἐς πεδίον προχέοντο Σκαμάνδριον· αὐτὰρ ὑπὸ χθὼν**

*προχέοντο* (imperfect middle/passive, 3rd plural of προχέω): "poured forth" or "streamed forth," describing the massed movement of troops. *πεδίον* (accusative singular neuter noun): "plain," the destination of motion with *ἐς*. *Σκαμάνδριον* (accusative singular adjective): "Scamandrian," modifying *πεδίον* and referring to the plain near the river Scamander. *χθὼν* (nominative singular feminine noun): "earth" or "ground," subject of the next clause introduced by *αὐτάρ*.

lines.original: σμερδαλέον κονάβιζε ποδῶν αὐτῶν τε καὶ ἵππων.
lines.english: The earth beneath boomed terribly from the feet of the men and horses.
lines.gloss: **σμερδαλέον** (adverb, "terribly, dreadfully") **κονάβιζε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of κοναβίζω, "resounded, thundered") **ποδῶν** (gen. pl. of πούς, "of feet") **ἵππων** (gen. pl. of ἵππος, "of horses"). The earth resounded terribly beneath the feet of both the men themselves and their horses as they poured forth across the plain.

lines.original: ἔσταν δʼ ἐν λειμῶνι Σκαμανδρίῳ ἀνθεμόεντι
lines.english: They stood in the flowery meadow of Scamander.
lines.gloss: **ἔσταν** (3rd pl. aorist indicative of ἵστημι) "they stood"; **λειμῶνι** (dative singular masculine of λειμών) "in the meadow"; **Σκαμανδρίῳ** (dative singular adjective modifying λειμῶνι) "of Scamander," referring to the Trojan river; **ἀνθεμόεντι** (dative singular adjective) "flowery, blooming." The Achaean forces took their stand in the flowery meadow along the Scamander river.

lines.original: μυρίοι, ὅσσά τε φύλλα καὶ ἄνθεα γίγνεται ὥρῃ.
lines.english: countless as the leaves and flowers that come forth in their season
lines.gloss: **μυρίοι** (adjective, nominative plural masculine) "countless, numberless"; **φύλλα** (noun, nominative plural neuter) "leaves"; **ἄνθεα** (noun, nominative plural neuter) "flowers"; **γίγνεται** (verb, 3rd singular present middle/passive) "come into being, are born"; **ὥρῃ** (noun, dative singular feminine) "in season, in springtime." The verse uses a double simile comparing the countless Achaean troops to leaves and flowers that bloom in their season.

lines.original: ἠΰτε μυιάων ἁδινάων ἔθνεα πολλὰ
lines.english: Like the many swarming tribes of thick-clustering flies
lines.gloss: **ἠΰτε** (comparative particle) "just as"; **μυιάων** (genitive plural of μυῖα) "of flies"; **ἁδινάων** (genitive plural adjective) "swarming, clustering"; **ἔθνεα** (nominative/accusative plural neuter of ἔθνος) "swarms, tribes"; **πολλὰ** (nominative/accusative plural neuter adjective) "many." The simile compares the multitude of warriors to many swarms of clustering flies, emphasizing their dense numbers.

lines.original: αἵ τε κατὰ σταθμὸν ποιμνήϊον ἠλάσκουσιν
lines.english: which dart about the shepherd's farmstead in springtime when milk wets the pails
lines.gloss: **αἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. fem.) "which" – refers back to the swarms of flies; **κατά** (preposition + acc.) "throughout, around"; **σταθμόν** (acc. sg. masc.) "farmstead, stable" – the shepherds' dwelling; **ποιμνήϊον** (adj. acc. sg. masc.) "of the flocks, pastoral" – modifies σταθμόν; **ἠλάσκουσιν** (3rd pl. pres. indic.) "buzz about, dart around" – iterative verb describing the flies' swarming motion around the pastoral buildings.

lines.original: ὥρῃ ἐν εἰαρινῇ ὅτε τε γλάγος ἄγγεα δεύει,
lines.english: in the spring season when milk drenches the pails
lines.gloss:
**ὥρῃ** (dat. sg. fem. of ὥρη): "in the season," temporal dative indicating when the action occurs.
**εἰαρινῇ** (dat. sg. fem. of εἰαρινός): "of spring," adjective modifying ὥρῃ.
**γλάγος** (nom. sg. neut. of γλάγος): "milk," subject of the verb, referring to fresh milk from ewes.
**ἄγγεα** (acc. pl. neut. of ἄγγος): "pails" or "vessels," direct object, containers for the milk.
**δεύει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of δεύω): "wets" or "moistens," describing how the abundant milk fills the vessels. This simile elaborates the pastoral comparison, depicting the springtime abundance

lines.original: τόσσοι ἐπὶ Τρώεσσι κάρη κομόωντες Ἀχαιοὶ
lines.english: So many were the long-haired Achaeans standing against the Trojans.
lines.gloss: **τόσσοι** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine): "so many," correlating with the preceding simile. **ἐπί** (preposition + dative): "against" (with hostile sense). **Τρώεσσι** (noun, dative plural): "the Trojans," indicating the target of the Achaeans' advance. **κάρη κομόωντες** (noun + participle, nominative plural masculine): "long-haired," literally "wearing their hair on their heads," a traditional Homeric epithet. **Ἀχαιοί** (noun, nominative plural): "the Achaeans," subject of the sentence in the following line.

lines.original: ἐν πεδίῳ ἵσταντο διαρραῖσαι μεμαῶτες.
lines.english: They stood on the plain eager to tear them apart.
lines.gloss:
**ἐν πεδίῳ** (preposition + dative neuter singular of πεδίον): "in the plain"
**ἵσταντο** (3rd plural imperfect middle-passive indicative of ἵστημι): "stood, took their stand"
**διαρραῖσαι** (aorist active infinitive of διαρραίω): "to break through, to shatter"
**μεμαῶτες** (nominative masculine plural perfect active participle of μέμονα): "eager, striving"

The long-haired Achaeans stood arrayed in the plain, eager to break through (the Trojan lines).

lines.original: τοὺς δʼ ὥς τʼ αἰπόλια πλατέʼ αἰγῶν αἰπόλοι ἄνδρες
lines.english: And as goatherds easily separate their wide-scattered flocks of goats
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** αἰπόλια (nom. pl. neut., "herds of goats"), αἰγῶν (gen. pl. fem., "of goats"), αἰπόλοι (nom. pl. masc., "goatherds"), ἄνδρες (nom. pl. masc., "men"), πλατέα (acc. pl. neut., "wide-ranging, scattered").

The leaders organize their troops just as goatherd men easily separate wide-ranging herds of goats; the simile continues the pastoral comparison begun in the previous lines.

lines.original: ῥεῖα διακρίνωσιν ἐπεί κε νομῷ μιγέωσιν,
lines.english: easily separate them when they have mingled together at pasture
lines.gloss: **ῥεῖα** (adverb): "easily," modifying the verb διακρίνωσιν. **διακρίνωσιν** (3rd pl. aor. subj. act. of διακρίνω): "they separate," referring to the shepherds sorting their flocks. **ἐπεί κε** (temporal conjunction + modal particle): "whenever," introducing a temporal clause. **νομῷ** (dat. sg. of νομός): "in/at pasture," locative dative indicating where the mixing occurs. **μιγέωσιν** (3rd pl. aor. subj. pass. of μίγνυμι): "they have become mixed," describing the goats mingling together.

lines.original: ὣς τοὺς ἡγεμόνες διεκόσμεον ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα
lines.english: Thus the leaders marshaled them here and there.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς** (adverb): "thus, so" — marks the transition back to the main narrative after the simile.

**ἡγεμόνες** (noun, nominative plural): "leaders, commanders" — the Greek chieftains organizing their troops.

**διεκόσμεον** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect active): "were marshaling, were arranging in order" — iterative action of organizing the troops for battle.

**ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα** (adverbial phrase): "here and there, in every direction" — emphasizes the commanders' activity throughout the ranks.

The verse concludes the shepherd simile, describing how the Greek leaders marshaled their forces in all directions, just as shepherds easily separate their mingled flocks.

lines.original: ὑσμίνην δʼ ἰέναι, μετὰ δὲ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων
lines.english: to enter the battle, and among them lord Agamemnon
lines.gloss:
**ὑσμίνην δʼ ἰέναι, μετὰ δὲ κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων**

*ὑσμίνην* (acc. sing., "battle," "combat") is the object of the infinitive *ἰέναι* (pres. inf. of εἶμι, "to go"). *κρείων* (nom. sing. masc., "lordly," "powerful") modifies *Ἀγαμέμνον* (nom. sing.), and *μετὰ* here functions as an adverb meaning "among them" or "in their midst." The line describes the marshaling into battle with lordly Agamemnon prominent among the troops.

lines.original: ὄμματα καὶ κεφαλὴν ἴκελος Διὶ τερπικεραύνῳ,
lines.english: In eyes and head like Zeus who delights in thunder,
lines.gloss:
**ὄμματα καὶ κεφαλὴν ἴκελος Διὶ τερπικεραύνῳ**

ὄμματα (nom. pl. neut., ὄμμα): "eyes"; καὶ κεφαλὴν (acc. sg. fem., κεφαλή): "and head"; ἴκελος (nom. sg. masc., ἴκελος): "like, resembling" (+ dat.); Διὶ (dat. sg., Ζεύς): "to Zeus"; τερπικεραύνῳ (dat. sg. masc., τερπικέραυνος): "who delights in thunder/lightning." In respect to his eyes and head, Agamemnon resembles Zeus who delights in the thunderbolt—a comparison emphasizing his commanding,

lines.original: Ἄρεϊ δὲ ζώνην, στέρνον δὲ Ποσειδάωνι.
lines.english: his waist like Ares and his chest like Poseidon.
lines.gloss: **Ἄρεϊ** (dat. sg., Ἄρης): "to Ares," dative of comparison or likeness. **ζώνην** (acc. sg., ζώνη): "waist/belt," direct object. **στέρνον** (acc. sg., στέρνον): "chest/breast," direct object in the second clause. **Ποσειδάωνι** (dat. sg., Ποσειδάων): "to Poseidon," dative of comparison. The line continues the heroic comparison, with Agamemnon's waist like Ares and chest like Poseidon, emphasizing his martial prowess and physical majesty through divine parallels.

lines.original: ἠΰτε βοῦς ἀγέληφι μέγʼ ἔξοχος ἔπλετο πάντων
lines.english: As a bull stands out far above all the others in the herd.
lines.gloss:
**ἠΰτε** (conjunction): "just as," introduces a simile comparing the subject to a bull among cattle.

**βοῦς** (noun, nominative singular masculine): "bull," subject of the simile.

**ἀγέληφι** (noun, dative singular feminine): "in/among the herd," locative dative indicating position within the group.

**μέγʼ ἔξοχος** (adverb + adjective): "greatly preeminent/outstanding," μέγα (elided) intensifies ἔξοχος (nominative singular), modifying βοῦς.

The line presents a heroic simile: "just as a bull stands out greatly preeminent among all in the herd."

lines.original: ταῦρος· ὃ γάρ τε βόεσσι μεταπρέπει ἀγρομένῃσι·
lines.english: a bull, for he stands out conspicuous among the gathering cattle
lines.gloss:
**ταῦρος·** (nom. sg. masc.) "bull" – the subject completing the simile from the previous line.

**μεταπρέπει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of μεταπρέπω) "stands out among" – the verb describing the bull's pre-eminence.

**βόεσσι** (dat. pl. fem. of βοῦς) "among cattle" – dative of comparison.

**ἀγρομένῃσι** (dat. pl. fem. pres. mid. participle of ἀγείρω) "when gathered together" – modifying the cattle as they are assembled in a herd.

The line completes the simile: the bull stands out conspicuously among the assembled cattle, just as Agamemnon stands pre-eminent among the warriors.

lines.original: τοῖον ἄρʼ Ἀτρεΐδην θῆκε Ζεὺς ἤματι κείνῳ
lines.english: Such did Zeus make the son of Atreus on that day.
lines.gloss: **τοῖον** (demonstrative pronoun, accusative singular masculine) "such a one"; **Ἀτρεΐδην** (patronymic noun, accusative singular) "son of Atreus" (referring to Agamemnon); **θῆκε** (aorist active indicative, 3rd singular of τίθημι) "made"; **Ζεύς** (nominative singular) "Zeus"; **ἤματι κείνῳ** (dative singular noun + demonstrative) "on that day." Zeus made the son of Atreus such a one on that day—connecting the simile of the preeminent bull to Agamemnon's distinction among heroes.

lines.original: ἐκπρεπέʼ ἐν πολλοῖσι καὶ ἔξοχον ἡρώεσσιν.
lines.english: preeminent among many and outstanding among heroes.
lines.gloss: **ἐκπρεπέα** (adj. acc. sg. masc., "conspicuous, outstanding") and **ἔξοχον** (adj. acc. sg. masc., "preeminent, surpassing") modify the Atreïd from the previous line, describing Zeus's elevation of him. **πολλοῖσι** (adj. dat. pl. masc., "many") and **ἡρώεσσιν** (noun dat. pl., "heroes") form a dative of comparison: "conspicuous among many and preeminent among heroes."

lines.original: ἔσπετε νῦν μοι Μοῦσαι Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχουσαι·
lines.english: Tell me now, Muses who dwell in Olympian halls.
lines.gloss: **ἔσπετε** (2nd pl. aorist imperative of *ἐνέπω*) "tell!": the poet invokes the Muses to relate the catalog of ships. **Μοῦσαι** (nom. pl., vocative function) "Muses": the goddesses of poetic inspiration addressed directly. **Ὀλύμπια δώματʼ ἔχουσαι** (pres. act. participle, fem. nom. pl. of *ἔχω* + acc. pl. *δώματα*) "who hold/dwell in Olympian halls": identifies the Muses by their divine abode. The invocation marks the transition to the great catalog, emphasizing that only divine knowledge can encompass all the Greek forces.

lines.original: ὑμεῖς γὰρ θεαί ἐστε πάρεστέ τε ἴστέ τε πάντα,
lines.english: For you are goddesses and are present and know all things.
lines.gloss: **ὑμεῖς** (pronoun, nom. pl., "you") emphasizes the Muses as opposed to mortals; **θεαί** (noun, nom. pl., "goddesses") identifies their divine nature; **πάρεστέ** (verb, 2nd pl. pres. indic. of πάρειμι, "you are present") stresses their direct witnessing of events; **ἴστέ** (verb, 2nd pl. perf. indic. of οἶδα, "you know") indicates their complete knowledge; **πάντα** (adj., acc. pl. neut., "all things") encompasses their total awareness. The threefold assertion (you are goddesses, are present, know all) contrasts the Muses' omniscience with mortal limitation expressed in the following line.

lines.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ κλέος οἶον ἀκούομεν οὐδέ τι ἴδμεν·
lines.english: We hear only rumor and know nothing ourselves.
lines.gloss: **ἡμεῖς** (pronoun, nom. pl., "we") contrasts mortals with the goddesses; **κλέος** (noun, acc. sg., "fame/report") is the indirect object of hearing; **οἶον** (adverb, "only/alone") emphasizes the limitation; **ἀκούομεν** (verb, 1st pl. pres. indic., "we hear") and **ἴδμεν** (verb, 1st pl. perf. indic. with pres. meaning, "we know") form a contrastive pair. The line stresses human dependence on hearsay versus divine omniscience.

lines.original: οἵ τινες ἡγεμόνες Δαναῶν καὶ κοίρανοι ἦσαν·
lines.english: who were the leaders and lords of the Danaans
lines.gloss:
**οἵ τινες ἡγεμόνες Δαναῶν καὶ κοίρανοι ἦσαν·**

**οἵ τινες** (relative pronoun, nominative plural masculine) "who(ever), which ones"; **ἡγεμόνες** (noun, nominative plural) "leaders, commanders"; **Δαναῶν** (noun, genitive plural) "of the Danaans/Greeks"; **κοίρανοι** (noun, nominative plural) "chiefs, lords"; **ἦσαν** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect) "were." The poet introduces the Catalogue of Ships by identifying which Greek leaders and chiefs he will enumerate.

lines.original: πληθὺν δʼ οὐκ ἂν ἐγὼ μυθήσομαι οὐδʼ ὀνομήνω,
lines.english: But the multitude I could not tell nor name,
lines.gloss: **πληθύν** (accusative singular feminine of πληθύς): "multitude, mass" — the countless throng of warriors. **μυθήσομαι** (1st singular future middle indicative of μυθέομαι): "I shall recount, tell of." **ὀνομήνω** (1st singular aorist subjunctive of ὀνομαίνω): "I could name, enumerate." The poet declares his inability to recount or name the multitude even if he tried (**οὐκ ἄν** with subjunctive expressing potential negation).

lines.original: οὐδʼ εἴ μοι δέκα μὲν γλῶσσαι, δέκα δὲ στόματʼ εἶεν,
lines.english: not even if I had ten tongues and ten mouths
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** *δέκα* (numeral, indeclinable) "ten"; *γλῶσσαι* (noun, nom. pl. fem. from γλῶσσα) "tongues"; *στόματα* (noun, nom. pl. neut. from στόμα) "mouths"; *εἶεν* (verb, 3rd pl. pres. opt. from εἰμί) "were, would be."

The poet employs a contrary-to-fact condition to emphasize impossibility: not even if he possessed ten tongues and ten mouths could he enumerate the Greek host.

lines.original: φωνὴ δʼ ἄρρηκτος, χάλκεον δέ μοι ἦτορ ἐνείη,
lines.english: an unbreakable voice, and a heart of bronze were within me,
lines.gloss:
**φωνὴ** (noun, nominative singular feminine) "voice" – subject of the implied verb "were." **ἄρρηκτος** (adjective, nominative singular feminine) "unbreakable, tireless" from ἀ-privative + ῥήγνυμι, modifying φωνή. **χάλκεον** (adjective, nominative singular neuter) "of bronze, brazen," modifying ἦτορ. **ἦτορ** (noun, nominative singular neuter) "heart" – subject in the clause. **ἐνείη** (verb, 3rd singular present optative active) "might be (in me)" from ἔνειμι, expressing an unreal condition. 

The poet continues his impossible wish: even if his voice were unbreakable and a bronze heart were within him, he still could not catalog all the ships without

lines.original: εἰ μὴ Ὀλυμπιάδες Μοῦσαι Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο
lines.english: if the Olympian Muses, daughters of aegis-bearing Zeus, had not
lines.gloss:
**Εἰ μὴ Ὀλυμπιάδες Μοῦσαι Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο**

**Ὀλυμπιάδες** (nom. pl. fem. adj.): "Olympian," modifying Μοῦσαι. **Μοῦσαι** (nom. pl. fem.): "Muses," subject of the implied verb (from next line). **Διὸς** (gen. sg. masc.): "of Zeus," possessive genitive. **αἰγιόχοιο** (gen. sg. masc. epithet): "aegis-bearing," modifying Διός. The poet invokes the Olympian Muses, daughters of aegis-bearing Zeus, acknowledging that without divine aid he cannot catalog all who came to Troy.

lines.original: θυγατέρες μνησαίαθʼ ὅσοι ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθον·
lines.english: daughters, would recall all those who came beneath Ilion
lines.gloss: **θυγατέρες** (nom. pl. fem., "daughters") μνησαίαθʼ = **μνησαίατο** (aor. opt. mid., 3rd pl., "should recount, remember") **ὅσοι** (nom. pl. masc., "all who, as many as") **ὑπὸ** (prep. + acc., "to, toward") **Ἴλιον** (acc. sg., "Ilios, Troy") **ἦλθον** (aor. ind. act., 3rd pl., "came"). The poet appeals to the Olympian Muses, daughters of Zeus, to recount all who came to Troy, introducing the Catalogue of Ships.

lines.original: ἀρχοὺς αὖ νηῶν ἐρέω νῆάς τε προπάσας.
lines.english: I will now tell of the leaders of the ships and all the ships.
lines.gloss: **ἀρχούς** (acc. pl. masc., "leaders") and **νηῶν** (gen. pl. fem., "of the ships") establish the subject matter. **ἐρέω** (1st sg. fut. act. indic. of *εἶπον*/λέγω, "I shall tell") announces the catalogue's scope. **προπάσας** (acc. pl. fem., "all," intensive form of πᾶς) modifies νῆας (acc. pl., "ships"), emphasizing comprehensive enumeration. This programmatic verse introduces the Catalogue of Ships, promising to list both the commanders and their complete naval forces.

lines.original: Βοιωτῶν μὲν Πηνέλεως καὶ Λήϊτος ἦρχον
lines.english: Of the Boeotians Peneleos and Leïtos were leaders
lines.gloss:
**Βοιωτῶν μὲν Πηνέλεως καὶ Λήϊτος ἦρχον**

Βοιωτῶν (gen. pl., Βοιωτοί) "of the Boeotians"; μέν (particle) marks the first item in the Catalogue; Πηνέλεως and Λήϊτος (nom. sg., proper names) "Peneleos and Leitus," subjects; ἦρχον (3rd pl. impf. act. indic., ἄρχω) "were leading/commanded." The verse introduces the Boeotian contingent, the first in the Catalogue of Ships, with two of their five leaders named.

lines.original: Ἀρκεσίλαός τε Προθοήνωρ τε Κλονίος τε,
lines.english: Arcesilaus and Prothoenor and Clonius led them.
lines.gloss:
**Ἀρκεσίλαός τε Προθοήνωρ τε Κλονίος τε** (Iliad 2.495)

**Ἀρκεσίλαός** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Arcesilaus"; **Προθοήνωρ** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Prothoenor"; **Κλονίος** (nom. sg. masc., proper name) "Clonius"; **τε... τε... τε** (enclitic conj.) "both... and... and," creating a tricolon. This line completes the list of five Boeotian commanders begun in the previous verse, naming the remaining three leaders with polysyndetic coordination.

lines.original: οἵ θʼ Ὑρίην ἐνέμοντο καὶ Αὐλίδα πετρήεσσαν
lines.english: those who held Hyria and rocky Aulis
lines.gloss: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who"; **ἐνέμοντο** (νέμω, 3rd pl. impf. mid.) "inhabited, dwelt in"; **Ὑρίην** (acc. sg. fem.) "Hyria" (place name); **Αὐλίδα** (acc. sg. fem.) "Aulis" (place name); **πετρήεσσαν** (adj. acc. sg. fem.) "rocky." The relative clause identifies warriors who inhabited Hyria and rocky Aulis, continuing the Boeotian catalogue.

lines.original: Σχοῖνόν τε Σκῶλόν τε πολύκνημόν τʼ Ἐτεωνόν,
lines.english: Schoenos and Scolos and Eteonos with its many ridges
lines.gloss:
**Σχοῖνόν τε Σκῶλόν τε πολύκνημόν τʼ Ἐτεωνόν**

Σχοῖνόν (acc. sing., place name): Schoinos, a Boeotian town; Σκῶλόν (acc. sing., place name): Skolos, another Boeotian settlement; πολύκνημόν (acc. sing. masc./fem., compound adjective): "rich in ridges/slopes," epithet modifying Ἐτεωνόν; Ἐτεωνόν (acc. sing., place name): Eteonos, a Boeotian town. The line continues the catalog's enumeration of Boeotian settlements, with the poetic epithet emphasizing Eteonos' hilly terrain.

lines.original: Θέσπειαν Γραῖάν τε καὶ εὐρύχορον Μυκαλησσόν,
lines.english: Thespeia and Graia and Mycalessus with its broad dancing-grounds
lines.gloss: **Θέσπειαν** (acc. sing. fem., Thespeia, Boeotian city), **Γραῖάν** (acc. sing. fem., Graia, another Boeotian city), **εὐρύχορον** (acc. sing. fem. adj., "wide-dancing" or "with broad dancing-ground," compound of εὐρύς "wide" + χορός "dancing-place"), **Μυκαλησσόν** (acc. sing. fem., Mycalessus, Boeotian city). This line continues the Boeotian catalogue, listing four more cities in asyndetic sequence, with the ornamental epithet *eurychoron* distinguishing Mycalessus.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ ἀμφʼ Ἅρμʼ ἐνέμοντο καὶ Εἰλέσιον καὶ Ἐρυθράς,
lines.english: and those who dwelt around Harma and Eilesion and Erythrai,
lines.gloss:
**οἵ τʼ ἀμφʼ Ἅρμʼ ἐνέμοντο καὶ Εἰλέσιον καὶ Ἐρυθράς**

**οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who, those who"; **ἀμφί** (preposition + acc., here elided before Ἅρμα) "around, about"; **ἐνέμοντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid. νέμω) "inhabited, occupied, held"; **Ἅρμα**, **Εἰλέσιον**, **Ἐρυθράς** (place names, acc.) "Harma," "Eilesion," and "Erythrae." The line continues the Catalogue of Ships, listing Boeot

lines.original: οἵ τʼ Ἐλεῶνʼ εἶχον ἠδʼ Ὕλην καὶ Πετεῶνα,
lines.english: those who held Eleon and Hyle and Peteon
lines.gloss: **οἵ τʼ** (nom. pl. masc. relative pronoun with τε) "those who" continues the catalog listing. **Ἐλεῶνʼ** (acc. sg., Eleon) a Boeotian town. **εἶχον** (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of ἔχω) "held, occupied." **Ὕλην** (acc. sg., Hyle) another Boeotian settlement. **Πετεῶνα** (acc. sg., Peteon) a third Boeotian town. The line enumerates three more Boeotian settlements controlled by the contingent, with the verb εἶχον governing all three accusative place names.

lines.original: Ὠκαλέην Μεδεῶνά τʼ ἐϋκτίμενον πτολίεθρον,
lines.english: Ocalea and Medeon the well-built citadel
lines.gloss:
**Ὠκαλέην Μεδεῶνά τʼ ἐϋκτίμενον πτολίεθρον**

Key words: **Ὠκαλέην** (acc. fem. sing., proper noun) "Ocalea"; **Μεδεῶνα** (acc. masc. sing., proper noun) "Medeon"; **ἐϋκτίμενον** (acc. neut. sing., perfect passive participle of εὖ + κτίζω) "well-built, well-founded"; **πτολίεθρον** (acc. neut. sing., noun) "citadel, town." 

This line continues the Boeotian catalog, listing Ocalea and the well-built citadel of Medeon as territories under Boeotian control.

lines.original: Κώπας Εὔτρησίν τε πολυτρήρωνά τε Θίσβην,
lines.english: Copae and Eutresis and Thisbe rich in doves
lines.gloss: **Κώπας** (acc. pl. fem.) – Copae, a Boeotian town; **Εὔτρησίν** (acc. sg. fem.) – Eutresis, another Boeotian town; **τε** (conj.) – "and," connecting items in the catalog; **πολυτρήρωνα** (acc. sg. fem.) – "rich in doves" or "with many doves," epithet modifying Thisbe; **Θίσβην** (acc. sg. fem.) – Thisbe, a Boeotian town. This line continues the Boeotian contingent in the Catalog of Ships, listing three towns with an ornamental epithet for the last.

lines.original: οἵ τε Κορώνειαν καὶ ποιήενθʼ Ἁλίαρτον,
lines.english: and those who held Coroneia and grassy Haliartus
lines.gloss: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "those who"; **τε** (enclitic particle) "and," connecting this clause with the preceding; **Κορώνειαν** (proper noun, acc. sing. fem.) "Coroneia," a Boeotian city; **ποιήενθʼ** (adjective, acc. sing. fem., < ποιήεις) "grassy" (with elided final -α); **Ἁλίαρτον** (proper noun, acc. sing. masc.) "Haliartus," another Boeotian city. The line continues the catalogue listing contingents, describing those who held Coroneia and grassy Haliartus.

lines.original: οἵ τε Πλάταιαν ἔχον ἠδʼ οἳ Γλισᾶντʼ ἐνέμοντο,
lines.english: and those who held Plataea and those who dwelt in Glisas,
lines.gloss:
**οἵ τε Πλάταιαν ἔχον ἠδʼ οἳ Γλισᾶντʼ ἐνέμοντο**

Key words: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc., "who/those who"), **Πλάταιαν** (proper noun, acc. sg. fem., "Plataea"), **ἔχον** (imperfect 3rd pl. of ἔχω, "they held/occupied"), **Γλισᾶντʼ** (proper noun, acc. sg. fem., "Glisas," with elided final alpha), **ἐνέμοντο** (imperfect 3rd pl. middle of νέμω, "they inhabited/dwelt in"). This verse continues the Boeotian catalogue, listing those who held

lines.original: οἵ θʼ Ὑποθήβας εἶχον ἐϋκτίμενον πτολίεθρον,
lines.english: and those who held Hypothebae, the well-built citadel,
lines.gloss: **Ὑποθήβας** (acc. pl., "Hypothebae"): city in Boeotia, often called "Lower Thebes." **εἶχον** (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of ἔχω, "they held/occupied"): governing verb. **ἐϋκτίμενον** (acc. sg. masc./neut. perf. pass. part. of ἐυκτίζω, "well-built"): epithet modifying **πτολίεθρον** (acc. sg. neut., "citadel/town"). The line identifies those Boeotians who held the well-founded town of Hypothebae.

lines.original: Ὀγχηστόν θʼ ἱερὸν Ποσιδήϊον ἀγλαὸν ἄλσος,
lines.english: and Onchestus the sacred grove of Poseidon bright with splendor
lines.gloss:
**Ὀγχηστόν** (acc. sing., proper noun): Onchestus, a Boeotian town sacred to Poseidon. **ἱερόν** (acc. sing. neut. adj.): sacred, holy. **Ποσιδήϊον** (gen. sing., "of Poseidon"): possessive form indicating the grove belongs to Poseidon. **ἀγλαόν** (acc. sing. neut. adj.): splendid, glorious. **ἄλσος** (acc. sing. neut. noun): grove, sacred precinct. 

This line describes those who held Onchestus, specifically its sacred and splendid grove belonging to Poseidon, continuing the Boeotian catalogue.

lines.original: οἵ τε πολυστάφυλον Ἄρνην ἔχον, οἵ τε Μίδειαν
lines.english: those who held grape-clustered Arne and those who held Mideia
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** πολυστάφυλον (adj. acc. fem. sg. from πολυστάφυλος, "rich in grapes"), Ἄρνην (acc. fem. sg., Arne, a Boeotian city), ἔχον (3rd pl. impf. act. indic. from ἔχω, "held, possessed"), Μίδειαν (acc. fem. sg., Mideia, another Boeotian city).

The relative clause continues the catalogue, describing those who held grape-rich Arne and those who held Mideia; the epithet πολυστάφυλον emphasizes Boeotia's agricultural fertility.

lines.original: Νῖσάν τε ζαθέην Ἀνθηδόνα τʼ ἐσχατόωσαν·
lines.english: and holy Nisa and Anthedon on the coast
lines.gloss:
**Νῖσάν** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Nisa, a Boeotian city. **ζαθέην** (acc. sg. fem., adj.): "very holy, sacred," modifying Νῖσάν. **Ἀνθηδόνα** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Anthedon, another Boeotian city. **τʼ ἐσχατόωσαν** (acc. sg. fem., pres. part.): "situated on the coast/frontier," from ἐσχατόω, modifying Ἀνθηδόνα. 

This line continues the Boeotian catalogue, listing those who held sacred Nisa and coastal Anthedon, with formulaic epic epithets distinguishing each city.

lines.original: τῶν μὲν πεντήκοντα νέες κίον, ἐν δὲ ἑκάστῃ
lines.english: Of these fifty ships went forth, and in each one
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (article, genitive plural masculine) "of these" — refers to the Boeotians mentioned in context. **πεντήκοντα** (numeral) "fifty" — the number of ships. **νέες** (noun, nominative plural feminine from ναῦς) "ships" — subject of the verb. **κίον** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect/aorist of εἶμι) "went, came" — describes the ships' movement. **ἑκάστῃ** (adjective, dative singular feminine) "in/on each" — refers to each individual ship.

lines.original: κοῦροι Βοιωτῶν ἑκατὸν καὶ εἴκοσι βαῖνον.
lines.english: In each ship one hundred and twenty young Boeotian men embarked.
lines.gloss:
**κοῦροι** (nom. pl. masc., κοῦρος): "young men, warriors"; **Βοιωτῶν** (gen. pl., Βοιωτοί): "of the Boeotians"; **ἑκατὸν καὶ εἴκοσι**: "one hundred and twenty"; **βαῖνον** (3rd pl. impf., βαίνω): "were going, embarked." 

Each of the fifty Boeotian ships carried 120 young warriors, emphasizing the large contingent contributed by this region to the Greek expedition.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ Ἀσπληδόνα ναῖον ἰδʼ Ὀρχομενὸν Μινύειον,
lines.english: Those who dwelt in Aspledon and Orchomenus of the Minyans
lines.gloss: **οἳ** (rel. pron., nom. pl. masc.) "who" introduces relative clause describing the previous contingent. **Ἀσπληδόνα** (acc. sg. fem.) "Aspledon," and **Ὀρχομενὸν Μινύειον** (acc. sg. masc. with ethnic adj.) "Minyan Orchomenus" are objects of **ναῖον** (impf. 3rd pl., ναίω) "they dwelt in/inhabited." **ἰδέ** (conj.) "and" connects the two geographic locations.

lines.original: τῶν ἦρχʼ Ἀσκάλαφος καὶ Ἰάλμενος υἷες Ἄρηος
lines.english: Ascalaphus and Ialmenus sons of Ares led them.
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (genitive plural, demonstrative pronoun) "of them"; **ἦρχʼ** (3rd singular imperfect, ἄρχω) "led, commanded"; **Ἀσκάλαφος** (nominative singular, proper noun) "Ascalaphus"; **Ἰάλμενος** (nominative singular, proper noun) "Ialmenus"; **υἷες** (nominative plural, υἱός) "sons"; **Ἄρηος** (genitive singular, proper noun) "of Ares." Ascalaphus and Ialmenus, sons of Ares, commanded these troops (from Aspledon and Orchomenus).

lines.original: οὓς τέκεν Ἀστυόχη δόμῳ Ἄκτορος Ἀζεΐδαο,
lines.english: whom Astyoche bore in the house of Actor son of Azeus
lines.gloss: **οὓς** (relative pronoun, masculine accusative plural) "whom" — refers back to Ascalaphus and Ialmenus. **τέκεν** (aorist, 3rd singular of τίκτω) "bore/gave birth to" — indicates Astyoche as their mother. **Ἀστυόχη** (proper noun, nominative) "Astyoche" — the maiden who bore the sons. **δόμῳ** (dative singular of δόμος) "in the house" — locative, indicating where she bore them. **Ἄκτορος Ἀζεΐδαο** (genitive proper nouns) "of Actor, son of Azeus" — patronymic identification of Actor.

lines.original: παρθένος αἰδοίη ὑπερώϊον εἰσαναβᾶσα
lines.english: a modest maiden who went up to the upper chamber with mighty Ares who lay with her in secret
lines.gloss:
**παρθένος αἰδοίη ὑπερώϊον εἰσαναβᾶσα**

παρθένος (noun, nom. sg. fem.): "maiden, virgin" — refers to Astyoche before her union with Ares. αἰδοίη (adj., nom. sg. fem.): "modest, reverent, chaste" — characterizes her maiden status. ὑπερώϊον (noun, acc. sg. neut.): "upper chamber" — the room where the encounter occurred. εἰσαναβᾶσα (participle, aor. nom. sg. fem., from εἰσαναβαίνω): "having gone up into" — describes her ascending to the chamber where Ares secretly lay with her.

lines.original: Ἄρηϊ κρατερῷ· ὃ δέ οἱ παρελέξατο λάθρῃ·
lines.english: to mighty Ares, and he lay with her in secret.
lines.gloss: **Ἄρηϊ κρατερῷ·** *Ἄρηϊ* (dat. sing. masc.) "to Ares," dative of the war god; *κρατερῷ* (dat. sing. masc. adj.) "mighty, strong," modifying Ἄρηϊ. **ὃ δέ** (nom. sing. masc. pron.) "and he," referring to Ares. **παρελέξατο** (3rd sing. aor. mid. indic.) "lay beside, slept with," from παραλέγομαι. **λάθρῃ** (dat. sing. fem.) "secretly, in secret," adverbial dative. The line describes Ares secretly sleeping with someone (likely Aphrodite in context).

lines.original: τοῖς δὲ τριήκοντα γλαφυραὶ νέες ἐστιχόωντο.
lines.english: And with them thirty hollow ships were ranged in order.
lines.gloss:
**τοῖς** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "for these/them," referring to the Phocians mentioned in the next line.

**τριήκοντα** (numeral): "thirty," the number of ships.

**γλαφυραί** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "hollow, curved," standard epithet for ships.

**νέες** (noun, nominative plural feminine): "ships," subject of the verb.

**ἐστιχόωντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle): "were marshaled/drawn up in rows," describing the arrangement of the Phocian contingent's thirty hollow ships.

lines.original: αὐτὰρ Φωκήων Σχεδίος καὶ Ἐπίστροφος ἦρχον
lines.english: Schedius and Epistrophus led the Phocians.
lines.gloss:
**αὐτὰρ** (δέ): "but, and" (postpositive conjunction, marking transition to new contingent). **Φωκήων** (Φωκεύς): genitive plural, "of the Phocians" (ethnic name). **Σχεδίος** and **Ἐπίστροφος**: nominative singular proper names, the two leaders. **ἦρχον** (ἄρχω): 3rd person dual imperfect active, "were leading, commanded."

The verse introduces the Phocian contingent with its dual commanders Schedius and Epistrophus, continuing the Catalogue's systematic enumeration of Greek forces.

lines.original: υἷες Ἰφίτου μεγαθύμου Ναυβολίδαο,
lines.english: sons of great-hearted Iphitus, son of Naubolus
lines.gloss:
**υἷες Ἰφίτου μεγαθύμου Ναυβολίδαο,**

υἷες (nom. pl. masc., "sons") identifies Schedius and Epistrophus as the sons of Iphitus; Ἰφίτου (gen. sg. masc., "of Iphitus") is the father's name; μεγαθύμου (gen. sg. masc., "great-hearted," "noble-spirited") is an epithet modifying Iphitus; Ναυβολίδαο (gen. sg. masc., "son of Naubolus") is a patronymic identifying Iphitus as the son of Naubolus.

lines.original: οἳ Κυπάρισσον ἔχον Πυθῶνά τε πετρήεσσαν
lines.english: who held Cyparissus and rocky Pytho
lines.gloss:
**οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who" — refers back to the sons of Iphitus. **Κυπάρισσον** (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Cyparissus" — a town in Phocis. **ἔχον** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. act.) "held, occupied" — main verb. **Πυθῶνά** (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Python" — alternative name for Delphi/Pytho. **πετρήεσσαν** (adj., acc. sg. fem.) "rocky" — describes Python/Pytho's mountainous terrain.

The line catalogues Phocian towns controlled by these leaders, emphasizing the sacred rocky site of Pytho/Delphi.

lines.original: Κρῖσάν τε ζαθέην καὶ Δαυλίδα καὶ Πανοπῆα,
lines.english: and sacred Crisa and Daulis and Panopeus
lines.gloss: **Κρῖσάν** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Crisa, a town in Phocis near Delphi. **ζαθέην** (acc. sg. fem., adj.): "very holy, sacred," modifying Crisa. **Δαυλίδα** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Daulis, another Phocian town. **Πανοπῆα** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Panopeus, a third town in the Phocian catalog. This verse continues the list of Phocian contingents, emphasizing sacred Crisa (associated with Apollo's cult) alongside Daulis and Panopeus, all governed by the verb ἔχον from the broader catalog structure.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ Ἀνεμώρειαν καὶ Ὑάμπολιν ἀμφενέμοντο,
lines.english: and those who dwelt around Anemoria and Hyampolis
lines.gloss: Key words: **οἵ** (relative pronoun, nominative plural masculine, "who/those who"), **Ἀνεμώρειαν** (proper noun, accusative singular feminine, "Anemorea," a Phocian town), **Ὑάμπολιν** (proper noun, accusative singular feminine, "Hyampolis," a Phocian town), **ἀμφενέμοντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle, "dwelt around" or "inhabited"). The line continues the catalogue of Phocian contingents, listing those who inhabited the areas around Anemorea and Hyampolis.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ ἄρα πὰρ ποταμὸν Κηφισὸν δῖον ἔναιον,
lines.english: those who dwelt beside the stream of sacred Cephisus
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** πὰρ (preposition + acc.) "beside"; ποταμὸν (acc. sg. m. of ποταμός) "river"; Κηφισὸν (acc. sg. of Κηφισός) "Cephisus"; δῖον (acc. sg. m. of δῖος) "divine, goodly"; ἔναιον (3rd pl. impf. of ναίω) "they dwelt."

This line continues the Phocian catalogue, describing those who dwelt beside the divine river Cephisus, a major waterway in Phocis and Boeotia.

lines.original: οἵ τε Λίλαιαν ἔχον πηγῇς ἔπι Κηφισοῖο·
lines.english: and those who held Lilaea at the springs of Cephisus
lines.gloss:
**οἵ τε Λίλαιαν ἔχον πηγῇς ἔπι Κηφισοῖο·**

*οἵ* (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who"; *Λίλαιαν* (proper noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Lilaea," a Phocian town; *ἔχον* (imperfect, 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held, occupied"; *πηγῇς* (noun, gen. sg. fem.) "of the source, spring"; *Κηφισοῖο* (proper noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of Cephisus" (river). Those who held Lilaea at the source of the Cephisus river.

lines.original: τοῖς δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.
lines.english: And with them forty black ships followed.
lines.gloss: **τοῖς** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "with them," referring to the Phocian contingent. **τεσσαράκοντα** (numeral): "forty," the number of ships. **μέλαιναι** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "black," modifying νῆες; conventional epithet for ships. **νῆες** (noun, nominative plural): "ships." **ἕποντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle): "were following" or "accompanied." This verse enumerates the Phocian naval contribution to the Greek expedition.

lines.original: οἳ μὲν Φωκήων στίχας ἵστασαν ἀμφιέποντες,
lines.english: These men deployed the ranks of the Phocians, taking their place beside them.
lines.gloss: **οἳ** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative plural masculine) "these men" refers to the contingent just mentioned. **Φωκήων** (proper noun, genitive plural) "of the Phocians" indicates the troops being supported. **στίχας** (noun, accusative plural) "ranks, lines" denotes battle formations. **ἵστασαν** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect active) "were setting up, arranging." **ἀμφιέποντες** (participle, nominative plural masculine present active) "attending to, taking care of." These men were positioning and supporting the Phocian battle lines.

lines.original: Βοιωτῶν δʼ ἔμπλην ἐπʼ ἀριστερὰ θωρήσσοντο.
lines.english: The Boeotians armed themselves nearby on the left.
lines.gloss: **Βοιωτῶν** (gen. pl. of Βοιωτοί) "of the Boeotians" – genitive of reference. **ἔμπλην** (adv.) "nearby, close at hand" – locative adverb. **ἀριστερά** (acc. pl. neut. of ἀριστερός) "on the left" – accusative of place where. **θωρήσσοντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid./pass. of θωρήσσω) "were arming themselves" – describes the Boeotians taking their position and equipping themselves for battle on the left flank, near the Phocians mentioned in the previous line.

lines.original: Λοκρῶν δʼ ἡγεμόνευεν Ὀϊλῆος ταχὺς Αἴας
lines.english: The swift Ajax son of Oileus led the Locrians.
lines.gloss: **Λοκρῶν** (gen. pl. of Λοκροί): "of the Locrians," genitive of the people governed by *ἡγεμόνευεν*. **ἡγεμόνευεν** (imperf. 3rd sg. of ἡγεμονεύω): "was leading, commanded," governing genitive. **Ὀϊλῆος** (gen. sg. of Ὀϊλεύς): "of Oileus," patronymic genitive. **ταχύς** (nom. sg. masc. of ταχύς): "swift," epithet of Ajax. **Αἴας** (nom. sg.): "Ajax," the lesser Ajax, son of Oileus, distinguished from Telamonian Ajax.

lines.original: μείων, οὔ τι τόσος γε ὅσος Τελαμώνιος Αἴας
lines.english: Lesser, not nearly so great as Telamonian Ajax.
lines.gloss: **μείων** (comparative adjective, nominative singular masculine) "smaller, lesser" – describes Ajax of Oileus; **τόσος** (demonstrative adjective, nominative singular masculine) "so great"; **ὅσος** (relative adjective, nominative singular masculine) "as great as" – together forming a correlative comparison "not so great as"; **Τελαμώνιος** (patronymic adjective, nominative singular masculine) "son of Telamon," referring to the greater Ajax. The line distinguishes the lesser Ajax of Oileus from his much larger namesake, Telamonian Ajax.

lines.original: ἀλλὰ πολὺ μείων· ὀλίγος μὲν ἔην λινοθώρηξ,
lines.english: but much smaller; he was small and wore a linen corslet.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλὰ πολὺ μείων· ὀλίγος μὲν ἔην λινοθώρηξ,**

Key words: **μείων** (comparative adjective, nom. sg. masc., "smaller/lesser"), **ὀλίγος** (adjective, nom. sg. masc., "small"), **ἔην** (3rd sg. imperfect of εἰμί, "he was"), **λινοθώρηξ** (compound noun, nom. sg. masc., "wearing a linen corselet"). The line emphasizes Odysseus's physical smallness compared to Ajax, noting specifically that he wore a linen breastplate rather than bronze armor.

lines.original: ἐγχείῃ δʼ ἐκέκαστο Πανέλληνας καὶ Ἀχαιούς·
lines.english: but with the spear he surpassed all the Panachaeans and Achaeans.
lines.gloss:
**ἐγχείῃ** (dative singular, ἐγχείη) - "in spear-work"; **δʼ** (postpositive particle) - "but/and"; **ἐκέκαστο** (3rd singular pluperfect middle-passive, ἐκκαίνυμαι) - "he excelled, surpassed"; **Πανέλληνας** (accusative plural, Πανέλληνες) - "all the Hellenes"; **Ἀχαιούς** (accusative plural, Ἀχαιοί) - "Achaeans." 

The line states that this warrior excelled all the Hellenes and Achaeans in spear-work, emphasizing his martial superiority despite limited forces.

lines.original: οἳ Κῦνόν τʼ ἐνέμοντʼ Ὀπόεντά τε Καλλίαρόν τε
lines.english: Those who held Cynus and Opous and Calliarus
lines.gloss:
**οἳ Κῦνόν τʼ ἐνέμοντʼ Ὀπόεντά τε Καλλίαρόν τε**

**οἵ** (nom. pl. masc., relative pronoun): "who"
**ἐνέμοντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid., νέμω): "inhabited, occupied" (elided to ἐνέμοντ')
**Κῦνον, Ὀπόεντα, Καλλίαρον** (acc. sg., proper nouns): "Cynus, Opous, Calliaros" (cities in Locris)

This verse continues the Catalogue of Ships, listing cities controlled by the Locrians under Ajax son of Oileus.

lines.original: Βῆσσάν τε Σκάρφην τε καὶ Αὐγειὰς ἐρατεινὰς
lines.english: Bessa and Scarphē and lovely Augeiai
lines.gloss: **Βῆσσάν** (acc. sg., proper noun): Bessa, a town in Locris. **Σκάρφην** (acc. sg., proper noun): Scarphe, a Locrian city. **Αὐγειάς** (acc. pl., proper noun): Augeiae, Locrian settlements. **ἐρατεινάς** (acc. pl. fem. adj.): lovely, desirable. This verse continues the catalogue of Locrian cities, listing Bessa, Scarphe, and the lovely Augeiae among the territories of the Locrian contingent.

lines.original: Τάρφην τε Θρόνιον τε Βοαγρίου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα·
lines.english: Tarphe and Thronion about the streams of Boagrius
lines.gloss:
**Τάρφην τε Θρόνιον τε Βοαγρίου ἀμφὶ ῥέεθρα·**

**Τάρφην** (acc. sing., fem.): "Tarphe," an accentually irregular accusative form of a Locrian place name. **Θρόνιον** (acc. sing., neut.): "Thronion," a town in the Locrian catalogue. **Βοαγρίου** (gen. sing., masc.): "of Boagrius," a river in Locris; genitive of specification with ῥέεθρα. **ἀμφί** (prep. + acc.): "around, near" the streams. **ῥέεθρα** (acc. pl., neut.): "streams, waters," from ῥέεθρον.

lines.original: τῷ δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο
lines.english: And with him forty black ships followed.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** τῷ (dat. sg. demonstrative pronoun, "with him"), τεσσαράκοντα (indeclinable numeral, "forty"), μέλαιναι (nom. pl. fem. adj., "black"), νῆες (nom. pl. fem. noun, "ships"), ἕποντο (3rd pl. imperf. mid./pass., "followed"). 

This line describes the forty black ships that accompanied Ajax the Lesser, leader of the Locrians mentioned in the next line.

lines.original: Λοκρῶν, οἳ ναίουσι πέρην ἱερῆς Εὐβοίης.
lines.english: the Locrians who dwell beyond sacred Euboea
lines.gloss: **Λοκρῶν** (gen. pl., Lokroi) "of the Locrians"; **ναίουσι** (pres. act. indic. 3rd pl., naiō) "dwell, inhabit"; **πέρην** (adv./prep. + gen.) "across from, opposite"; **ἱερῆς** (gen. sg. fem., hieros) "holy, sacred"; **Εὐβοίης** (gen. sg., Euboia) "Euboea." This line identifies the Locrians who inhabit the territory opposite sacred Euboea, introducing the Opuntian Locrians under Ajax son of Oileus in the Catalogue of Ships.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ Εὔβοιαν ἔχον μένεα πνείοντες Ἄβαντες
lines.english: And those who held Euboea, the Abantes breathing fury
lines.gloss: **Εὔβοιαν** (acc. sg. fem., "Euboea") is the object of **ἔχον** (3rd pl. imperf. act., "held/occupied"). **μένεα πνείοντες** (acc. pl. neut. + nom. pl. masc. pres. act. part., "breathing might/fury") is a formulaic phrase characterizing the **Ἄβαντες** (nom. pl. masc., "Abantes"), the inhabitants of Euboea. This line introduces the Euboean contingent, famous for their martial spirit.

lines.original: Χαλκίδα τʼ Εἰρέτριάν τε πολυστάφυλόν θʼ Ἱστίαιαν
lines.english: Chalkis and Eretria and Histiaia rich in grapes
lines.gloss:
