**Νιρεύς** (nom. sg. masc.) - Nireus, leader from Syme. **αὖ** (particle) - "again, next" (marking transition to new contingent). **Σύμηθεν** (adverb, <-θεν suffix) - "from Syme" (ablative of origin). **ἄγε** (3rd sg. impf. act., ἄγω) - "led, brought." **ἐΐσας** (acc. pl. fem., ἐΐση) - "well-benched" (epithet modifying ships).

The verse introduces Nireus leading three well-benched ships from Syme, continuing the Catalogue's formulaic pattern.

lines.original: Νιρεὺς Ἀγλαΐης υἱὸς Χαρόποιό τʼ ἄνακτος
lines.english: Nireus son of Aglaia and lord Charopus
lines.gloss: **Νιρεὺς** (nom. sg. m., proper noun): Nireus, son of Aglaia and King Charopus. **Ἀγλαΐης** (gen. sg. f., proper noun): of Aglaia, his mother. **υἱὸς** (nom. sg. m., noun): son. **Χαρόποιό** (gen. sg. m., proper noun): of Charopus. **ἄνακτος** (gen. sg. m., noun): lord, king, in apposition to Charopus. The line provides Nireus's parentage: son of Aglaia and lord Charopus.

lines.original: Νιρεύς, ὃς κάλλιστος ἀνὴρ ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθε
lines.english: Nireus, who was the most beautiful man who came to Troy
lines.gloss:
**Νιρεύς** (nom. sg. masc., proper name): Nireus, son of Aglaia and Charopus. **κάλλιστος** (nom. sg. masc., superlative adjective): most beautiful, handsomest. **ἀνήρ** (nom. sg. masc., noun): man, warrior. **ὑπό** (preposition + acc.): to, toward. **Ἴλιον** (acc. sg. neut., proper name): Ilion, Troy. **ἦλθε** (3rd sg. aor. indic., ἔρχομαι): came, went.

Nireus is identified as the most handsome man who came to Troy (among the Achaeans after Achilles, as the following line specifies).

lines.original: τῶν ἄλλων Δαναῶν μετʼ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα·
lines.english: of all the other Danaans after blameless Peleus' son
lines.gloss:
**τῶν ἄλλων Δαναῶν μετʼ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα·**

**τῶν ἄλλων** (gen. pl. masc., article + adjective) "of the other"; **Δαναῶν** (gen. pl., "Danaans/Greeks"); **μετά** (preposition + acc.) "after"; **ἀμύμονα** (acc. sg. masc., adjective) "blameless, excellent"; **Πηλεΐωνα** (acc. sg., "son of Peleus" = Achilles). Nireus was the handsomest of the other Greeks after the excellent son of Peleus (Achilles).

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἀλαπαδνὸς ἔην, παῦρος δέ οἱ εἵπετο λαός.
lines.english: But he was weak and feeble, and few people followed him.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλʼ ἀλαπαδνὸς ἔην, παῦρος δέ οἱ εἵπετο λαός.**

*ἀλαπαδνὸς* (nom. sg. masc. adj.) "weak, feeble"; *ἔην* (3rd sg. impf. of εἰμί) "he was"; *παῦρος* (nom. sg. masc. adj.) "few, small"; *εἵπετο* (3rd sg. impf. mid. of ἕπομαι) "followed." The verse describes a weak leader followed by only a small contingent of troops.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἄρα Νίσυρόν τʼ εἶχον Κράπαθόν τε Κάσον τε
lines.english: Those who held Nisyros and Krapathos and Kasos
lines.gloss:
**Target: οἳ δʼ ἄρα Νίσυρόν τʼ εἶχον Κράπαθόν τε Κάσον τε**

**οἵ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.): "who, they who" – introduces new contingent. **εἶχον** (verb, impf. act. ind., 3rd pl. < ἔχω): "held, possessed" – controls the accusative place names. **Νίσυρόν, Κράπαθόν, Κάσον** (proper nouns, acc. sing.): "Nisyros, Krapathos, Kasos" – Aegean islands held by this group of warriors.

lines.original: καὶ Κῶν Εὐρυπύλοιο πόλιν νήσους τε Καλύδνας,
lines.english: and Cos the city of Eurypylus and the Calydnian islands
lines.gloss: **Κῶν** (acc. sg. fem., "Cos"), **Εὐρυπύλοιο** (gen. sg. masc., "of Eurypylus"), **πόλιν** (acc. sg. fem., "city"), **νήσους** (acc. pl. fem., "islands"), **Καλύδνας** (acc. pl. fem., "Calydnae"). The line catalogs Cos, city of Eurypylus, and the Calydnae islands as part of the contingent's territory.

lines.original: τῶν αὖ Φείδιππός τε καὶ Ἄντιφος ἡγησάσθην
lines.english: Of these Pheidippus and Antiphus were the two leaders.
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (genitive plural, demonstrative pronoun): "of these," referring to the men from Cos and the Calydnian islands. **αὖ** (particle): "in turn," "moreover," marking the transition to the next contingent's leaders. **Φείδιππός** and **Ἄντιφος** (nominative singular, proper nouns): Pheidippus and Antiphus, co-commanders of this contingent. **ἡγησάσθην** (3rd person dual, aorist middle indicative of ἡγέομαι): "led," "were leaders of," with the dual form indicating the two joint commanders.

lines.original: Θεσσαλοῦ υἷε δύω Ἡρακλεΐδαο ἄνακτος·
lines.english: The two sons of Thessalus, the lord descended from Heracles.
lines.gloss: **Θεσσαλοῦ** (gen. sg. of Θεσσαλός): "of Thessalus," patronymic genitive depending on υἷε. **υἷε** (nom. dual of υἱός): "two sons," dual form indicating the pair Pheidippus and Antiphus. **δύω** (nom./acc. dual of δύο): "two," dual numeral in apposition to υἷε. **Ἡρακλεΐδαο** (gen. sg. of Ἡρακλείδης): "of the descendant of Heracles," i.e., Heracles' grandson through Thessalus. **ἄνακτος** (gen. sg. of ἄναξ): "lord, king," in apposition to Ἡρακλεΐδαο, emphasizing royal line

lines.original: τοῖς δὲ τριήκοντα γλαφυραὶ νέες ἐστιχόωντο.
lines.english: And with them thirty hollow ships were marshaled in their rows.
lines.gloss:
**τοῖς** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "for these/them," referring to the forces just described, governed by the verb of accompaniment.

**τριήκοντα** (numeral, indeclinable): "thirty," modifying νέες.

**γλαφυραὶ** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "hollow, curved," standard Homeric epithet for ships, agreeing with νέες.

**νέες** (noun, nominative plural feminine from ναῦς): "ships," subject of the verb.

**ἐστιχόωντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect medio-passive from στοιχέω): "were drawn up in rows, were arrayed," describing the fleet's formation in the Catalogue of Ships.

lines.original: νῦν αὖ τοὺς ὅσσοι τὸ Πελασγικὸν Ἄργος ἔναιον,
lines.english: Now again those who dwelt in Pelasgian Argos
lines.gloss:
**νῦν** (adverb) "now" — marks transition to new catalog section. **αὖ** (particle) "again, further" — continuing the enumeration. **τοὺς** (article, acc. pl. masc.) "those" — object of upcoming verb of leading/commanding. **Πελασγικὸν** (adj., acc. sg. neut.) "Pelasgian" — ethnic epithet modifying Ἄργος. **Ἄργος** (noun, acc. sg. neut.) "Argos" — here the broader Thessalian region, not the southern city. **ἔναιον** (verb, impf. 3rd pl.) "dwelt in, inhabited" — from ναίω.

The line introduces the contingent from Pelasgian Argos (Thessaly), shifting catalog focus northward.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ Ἄλον οἵ τʼ Ἀλόπην οἵ τε Τρηχῖνα νέμοντο,
lines.english: those who dwelt in Alos and Alope and those who held Trachis
lines.gloss: **Ἄλον** (acc. sg., "Alos," Thessalian city), **Ἀλόπην** (acc. sg., "Alope," another Thessalian city), **Τρηχῖνα** (acc. sg., "Trachis," city in southern Thessaly), **νέμοντο** (3rd pl. impf. mid., νέμω, "they inhabited/controlled"). This line continues the Thessalian catalog with three cities controlled by Achilles' forces, using the relative pronoun **οἵ τε** (nom. pl. masc., "those who") in anaphoric repetition to enumerate the territories.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ εἶχον Φθίην ἠδʼ Ἑλλάδα καλλιγύναικα,
lines.english: those who held Phthia and Hellas of the fair women
lines.gloss: **Φθίην** (acc. sing. fem., "Phthia," Achilles' homeland in Thessaly) and **Ἑλλάδα** (acc. sing. fem., "Hellas," a region in Thessaly, not all Greece) are direct objects of **εἶχον** (3rd pl. imperf. act. indic. of ἔχω, "they held/possessed"). **καλλιγύναικα** (acc. sing. fem. compound adj., "with beautiful women," from καλλι- + γυνή) modifies Ἑλλάδα, describing the region's notable characteristic.

lines.original: Μυρμιδόνες δὲ καλεῦντο καὶ Ἕλληνες καὶ Ἀχαιοί,
lines.english: They were called Myrmidons and Hellenes and Achaeans.
lines.gloss: **Μυρμιδόνες** (nominative plural masculine): "Myrmidons," the people of Achilles, subject of passive verb καλεῦντο. **καλεῦντο** (3rd plural imperfect medio-passive, καλέω): "they were called," indicating how these three groups were collectively named. **Ἕλληνες** (nominative plural masculine): "Hellenes," one of the three tribal names for Achilles' followers. **Ἀχαιοί** (nominative plural masculine): "Achaeans," the third name in the series connected by καί. The line lists the three designations—Myrmidons, Hellenes, and Achaeans—by which Achilles' contingent was known.

lines.original: τῶν αὖ πεντήκοντα νεῶν ἦν ἀρχὸς Ἀχιλλεύς.
lines.english: Achilles was the commander of these fifty ships.
lines.gloss:
**τῶν** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive plural masculine) "of these/them"; **πεντήκοντα** (numeral) "fifty"; **νεῶν** (noun, genitive plural from ναῦς) "of ships"; **ἦν** (verb, 3rd singular imperfect from εἰμί) "was"; **ἀρχὸς** (noun, nominative singular) "leader, commander." 

Achilles was the commander of fifty ships belonging to these men (the Myrmidons, Hellenes, and Achaeans just mentioned).

lines.original: ἀλλʼ οἵ γʼ οὐ πολέμοιο δυσηχέος ἐμνώοντο·
lines.english: But they had no mind for the din of grievous war.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλʼ οἵ γʼ οὐ πολέμοιο δυσηχέος ἐμνώοντο·**

**ἀλλά** (conjunction): "but"; **οἵ γε** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.): "they" (the Myrmidons); **πολέμοιο** (noun, gen. sg.): "of war"; **δυσηχέος** (adjective, gen. sg.): "ill-sounding, with evil din"; **ἐμνώοντο** (verb, 3rd pl. imperf. mid./pass.): "were mindful of, remembered, thought upon." The Myrmidons did not think upon war's dreadful clamor, since Achilles kept them idle by the ships.

lines.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔην ὅς τίς σφιν ἐπὶ στίχας ἡγήσαιτο·
lines.english: For there was no one who could lead them into the ranks of battle.
lines.gloss:
**οὐ γὰρ ἔην ὅς τίς σφιν ἐπὶ στίχας ἡγήσαιτο·**

Key words: **ἔην** (3rd sg. imperfect of εἰμί, "there was"); **ὅς τίς** (indefinite relative pronoun, "anyone who"); **σφιν** (3rd pl. dative pronoun, "for them"); **στίχας** (acc. pl. of στίχος, "ranks, lines"); **ἡγήσαιτο** (3rd sg. aorist optative middle of ἡγέομαι, "would lead"). The verse explains why the Myrmidons were not engaged in battle: there was no one who would lead them into the battle lines.

lines.original: κεῖτο γὰρ ἐν νήεσσι ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεὺς
lines.english: For swift-footed godlike Achilles lay among the ships.
lines.gloss:
**κεῖτο γὰρ ἐν νήεσσι ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς**

**κεῖτο** (3rd sg. impf. mid./pass. of κεῖμαι): "was lying," "remained." **νήεσσι** (dat. pl. of ναῦς): "in/among the ships." **ποδάρκης** (nom. sg. adj.): "swift-footed," traditional epithet. **δῖος** (nom. sg. adj.): "noble," "godlike." **Ἀχιλλεύς** (nom. sg.): "Achilles," subject of the verb. The line explains why there was no leader for the Myrmidons: godlike, swift-footed Achilles remained idle by the ships.

lines.original: κούρης χωόμενος Βρισηΐδος ἠϋκόμοιο,
lines.english: enraged over the fair-haired daughter Briseis
lines.gloss: κούρης (nom. sg. fem., "girl/maiden") - genitive of separation with χωόμενος. χωόμενος (pres. mid. ptc. nom. sg. masc., "being angry") - explains why Achilles lay among the ships, governing a genitive object. Βρισηΐδος (gen. sg. fem., "of Briseis") - in apposition to κούρης, specifying which girl. ἠϋκόμοιο (gen. sg. fem., "fair-haired/lovely-haired") - ornamental epithet modifying Βρισηΐδος.

lines.original: τὴν ἐκ Λυρνησσοῦ ἐξείλετο πολλὰ μογήσας
lines.english: whom he had taken from Lyrnessus after much toil
lines.gloss:
**τὴν** (fem. acc. sing. demonstrative/relative pronoun) "whom/her" — refers to Briseis. **ἐκ** (preposition + gen.) "from, out of." **Λυρνησσοῦ** (gen. sing. proper noun) "Lyrnessus" — the city whence Briseis was taken. **ἐξείλετο** (3rd sing. aor. mid. indic. of ἐξαιρέω) "he took out, carried off as booty." **μογήσας** (aor. act. participle of μογέω) "having toiled, having labored hard."

Achilles seized her as prize from Lyrnessus after great exertion in battle.

lines.original: Λυρνησσὸν διαπορθήσας καὶ τείχεα Θήβης,
lines.english: having sacked Lyrnessus and the walls of Thebes
lines.gloss: **Λυρνησσόν** (acc. sing.) "Lyrnessus" - object of διαπορθήσας. **διαπορθήσας** (aor. act. ptcp., nom. sing. masc.) "having sacked/destroyed utterly" - causal/temporal participle modifying the subject. **τείχεα** (acc. pl. neut.) "walls" - second object coordinated with Λυρνησσόν. **Θήβης** (gen. sing.) "of Thebe" - possessive genitive with τείχεα. The line describes the hero's prior destruction of both Lyrnessus and the walls of Thebe (Cilician Thebe, home of Andromache).

lines.original: κὰδ δὲ Μύνητʼ ἔβαλεν καὶ Ἐπίστροφον ἐγχεσιμώρους,
lines.english: and he struck down Mynes and Epistrophus wielders of the spear
lines.gloss:
**κὰδ δὲ Μύνητʼ ἔβαλεν καὶ Ἐπίστροφον ἐγχεσιμώρους,**

**κὰδ** (κατά + elision before δέ): preposition/adverb, "down, killed"; **Μύνητα** (acc. sg.): Mynes, a Trojan leader slain by Achilles; **ἔβαλεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of βάλλω): "he struck down, killed"; **Ἐπίστροφον** (acc. sg.): Epistrophos, brother of Mynes; **ἐγχεσιμώρους** (acc. pl. masc., ἐγχεσίμωρος): "spear

lines.original: υἱέας Εὐηνοῖο Σεληπιάδαο ἄνακτος·
lines.english: sons of Euenus the lord, son of Selepius
lines.gloss: **υἱέας** (acc. pl. masc. of υἱός) "sons"; **Εὐηνοῖο** (gen. sg. of Εὐήνος) "of Euēnus"; **Σεληπιάδαο** (gen. sg. patronymic of Σεληπιάδης) "son of Selepios"; **ἄνακτος** (gen. sg. masc. of ἄναξ) "lord, king." The line identifies Mynēs and Epistrophos as the sons of lord Euēnus, himself son of Selepios, establishing their noble lineage.

lines.original: τῆς ὅ γε κεῖτʼ ἀχέων, τάχα δʼ ἀνστήσεσθαι ἔμελλεν.
lines.english: For her he lay grieving, but soon he was destined to rise up.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.704:**

τῆς (demonstrative pronoun, genitive singular feminine) "because of her/this"; κεῖτʼ = ἔκειτο (imperfect middle/passive, 3rd singular of κεῖμαι) "he lay"; ἀχέων (present participle, nominative singular masculine of ἀχεύω) "grieving"; ἀνστήσεσθαι = ἀναστήσεσθαι (future infinitive middle of ἀνίστημι) "to rise up." He lay grieving because of her, but he was destined soon to rise up again—referring to Protesilaus mourning and his anticipated but unfulfilled return.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ εἶχον Φυλάκην καὶ Πύρασον ἀνθεμόεντα
lines.english: Those who held Phylace and flowery Pyrasus
lines.gloss: οἳ (nom. pl. masc. relative pronoun) "who, those who" introduces a new contingent. Φυλάκην (acc. sg. fem.) "Phylace," a city in Thessaly. Πύρασον (acc. sg. masc.) "Pyrasus," another Thessalian city. ἀνθεμόεντα (acc. sg. masc. adj.) "flowery, blooming," poetic epithet modifying Pyrasus. εἶχον (3rd pl. imperf. act.) "held, possessed" indicates their territorial control.

lines.original: Δήμητρος τέμενος, Ἴτωνά τε μητέρα μήλων,
lines.english: Demeter's precinct and Iton mother of flocks
lines.gloss:
**Δήμητρος** (gen. sg. fem. of Δημήτηρ): "of Demeter," goddess of grain; genitive dependent on τέμενος. **τέμενος** (acc. sg. neut.): "sacred precinct, shrine," direct object of εἶχον from previous lines. **Ἴτωνά** (acc. sg. fem. of Ἰτώνη): "Iton," a Thessalian town, also in apposition/parallel with τέμενος. **μητέρα** (acc. sg. fem.): "mother," in apposition to Ἴτωνά. **μήλων** (gen. pl. neut. of μῆλον): "of flocks, sheep," objective genitive with μητέρα.

The line lists Demeter's sacred precinct and Iton as "mother

lines.original: ἀγχίαλόν τʼ Ἀντρῶνα ἰδὲ Πτελεὸν λεχεποίην,
lines.english: Antron by the sea and Ptelon rich in meadows.
lines.gloss:
**ἀγχίαλόν τʼ Ἀντρῶνα ἰδὲ Πτελεὸν λεχεποίην**

ἀγχίαλον (adjective, accusative singular feminine): "near the sea," describing a coastal location. Ἀντρῶνα (proper noun, accusative singular): Antron, a town in Thessaly. Πτελεόν (proper noun, accusative singular): Pteleon, another Thessalian town. λεχεποίην (adjective, accusative singular feminine): "with beds of grass/verdant," an epithet describing lush, grassy terrain.

lines.original: τῶν αὖ Πρωτεσίλαος ἀρήϊος ἡγεμόνευε
lines.english: Of these warlike Protesilaus was leader.
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (gen. pl. demonstrative pronoun, "of these") refers to the troops from the previously mentioned towns; **Πρωτεσίλαος** (nom. sg. proper noun) is Protesilaus, leader of the Thessalian contingent; **ἀρήϊος** (nom. sg. adj., "warlike, martial") modifies Protesilaus; **ἡγεμόνευε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of ἡγεμονεύω, "was leading, commanded"). The imperfect tense poignantly foreshadows his death, as the next line reveals he is already held by the black earth.

lines.original: ζωὸς ἐών· τότε δʼ ἤδη ἔχεν κάτα γαῖα μέλαινα.
lines.english: while he was living, but then already the black earth held him.
lines.gloss: **ζωὸς ἐών** (nominative singular masculine present participle of εἰμί): "while (he was) living" or "when he was still alive." **κάτα** (adverbial/tmesis with ἔχεν): "down" or "beneath," suggesting complete enclosure. **γαῖα μέλαινα** (nominative singular feminine): "the black earth," a formulaic expression for the grave or underworld. The line refers to Protesilaus, already dead and held by the earth while his wife remained alive in Phylace.

lines.original: τοῦ δὲ καὶ ἀμφιδρυφὴς ἄλοχος Φυλάκῃ ἐλέλειπτο
lines.english: His wife with torn cheeks was left behind in Phylace and his house half-finished.
lines.gloss:
**τοῦ δὲ καὶ ἀμφιδρυφὴς ἄλοχος Φυλάκῃ ἐλέλειπτο**

**τοῦ** (demonstrative pronoun, gen. sing. masc.): "of him," referring to the slain warrior. **ἀμφιδρυφὴς** (adjective, nom. sing. fem.): "tearing both cheeks," describing a grieving woman. **ἄλοχος** (noun, nom. sing. fem.): "wife." **Φυλάκῃ** (proper noun, dat. sing.): "in Phylace," a city in Thessaly. **ἐλέλειπτο** (verb, pluperfect mid./pass. indic., 3rd sing.): "had been left behind." His

lines.original: καὶ δόμος ἡμιτελής· τὸν δʼ ἔκτανε Δάρδανος ἀνὴρ
lines.english: and a half-finished house; a Dardanian man killed him.
lines.gloss:
**καὶ δόμος ἡμιτελής· τὸν δʼ ἔκτανε Δάρδανος ἀνὴρ**

*δόμος* (nominative singular masculine): "house"; *ἡμιτελής* (nominative singular, compound adjective from ἡμι- + τέλος): "half-finished"; *ἔκτανε* (3rd singular aorist active indicative of κτείνω): "killed"; *Δάρδανος* (nominative singular masculine adjective): "Dardanian, Trojan"; *ἀνήρ* (nominative singular masculine): "man, warrior." The half-finished house left behind emphasizes the incompleteness of Protesilaus' life, killed by a Trojan warrior as he leapt from his ship.

lines.original: νηὸς ἀποθρῴσκοντα πολὺ πρώτιστον Ἀχαιῶν.
lines.english: leaping from his ship, by far the first of all the Achaeans.
lines.gloss:
**νηὸς** (gen. sg. fem. of ναῦς): "from the ship"; **ἀποθρῴσκοντα** (pres. act. ptc. acc. sg. masc. of ἀποθρῴσκω): "leaping down/away"; **πρώτιστον** (superl. acc. sg. masc. of πρῶτος): "very first, foremost"; **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιοί): "of the Achaeans." 

The line describes someone leaping from a ship, being by far the first/foremost of the Achaeans, when he was killed by a Dardanian warrior.

lines.original: οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδʼ οἳ ἄναρχοι ἔσαν, πόθεόν γε μὲν ἀρχόν·
lines.english: Yet they were not without a leader, though they longed for their leader.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἄναρχοι (nominative plural adjective, "without a leader"), πόθεον (3rd plural imperfect, "they longed for/missed"), ἀρχόν (accusative singular noun, "leader/commander"). 

The line asserts that the troops were not leaderless (double negative for emphasis), though they did indeed miss their fallen leader; the contrastive structure (οὐδὲ... ἔσαν vs. πόθεόν γε μέν) acknowledges their grief while confirming they maintained military order.

lines.original: ἀλλά σφεας κόσμησε Ποδάρκης ὄζος Ἄρηος
lines.english: But Podarces, scion of Ares, marshaled them into order.
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for:** ἀλλά σφεας κόσμησε Ποδάρκης ὄζος Ἄρηος

**κόσμησε** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of κοσμέω): "marshaled" or "ordered [them]"; **σφεας** (acc. pl. pronoun): "them," referring to the leaderless troops; **Ποδάρκης** (nom. sg.): "Podarces," the new leader; **ὄζος** (nom. sg.): "scion" or "branch," a poetic term for offspring; **Ἄρηος** (gen. sg.): "of Ares," the war god. Podarces, described as a scion of Ares, marshaled the previously leaderless contingent.

lines.original: Ἰφίκλου υἱὸς πολυμήλου Φυλακίδαο
lines.english: son of Iphiclus the sheep-rich Phylacid
lines.gloss:
**Ἰφίκλου** (gen. sg., "of Iphiclos") **υἱὸς** (nom. sg., "son") **πολυμήλου** (gen. sg., "rich in flocks/sheep") **Φυλακίδαο** (gen. sg., "of Phylakides/descended from Phylax").

Podarkēs is identified by patronymic: son of Iphiclos, himself descended from Phylax, with the epithet *polumēlos* emphasizing the family's pastoral wealth.

lines.original: αὐτοκασίγνητος μεγαθύμου Πρωτεσιλάου
lines.english: own brother of great-hearted Protesilaus
lines.gloss: **αὐτοκασίγνητος** (nom. sg. masc., compound adjective) "own brother, full brother" — describes Podarces' relationship to Protesilaus. **μεγαθύμου** (gen. sg. masc., adjective) "great-hearted, brave" — epithet modifying Protesilaus. **Πρωτεσιλάου** (gen. sg. masc., proper noun) "of Protesilaus" — the first Greek to die at Troy, whose brother Podarces now leads the troops. The line identifies Podarces as the full brother of the noble Protesilaus, establishing his legitimacy as a replacement commander.

lines.original: ὁπλότερος γενεῇ· ὁ δʼ ἅμα πρότερος καὶ ἀρείων
lines.english: younger by birth, but the other was both older and more valiant
lines.gloss:
**ὁπλότερος** (comparative adjective, nominative singular masculine) "younger" modifies the subject (Podarces); **γενεῇ** (noun, dative singular) "in birth/age," dative of respect; **ὁ** (demonstrative pronoun, nominative singular masculine) refers to Protesilaus; **πρότερος** (comparative adjective, nominative) "older/former"; **ἀρείων** (comparative adjective, nominative) "better, braver." 

The line contrasts the two brothers: Podarces was younger by birth, but Protesilaus was both older and superior (in martial prowess).

lines.original: ἥρως Πρωτεσίλαος ἀρήϊος· οὐδέ τι λαοὶ
lines.english: the warrior hero Protesilaus who loved battle, nor were the people
lines.gloss:
**ἥρως Πρωτεσίλαος ἀρήϊος· οὐδέ τι λαοὶ**

*ἥρως* (nom. sg. masc.): "hero," subject. *Πρωτεσίλαος* (nom. sg. masc.): proper name, "Protesilaus," in apposition. *ἀρήϊος* (nom. sg. masc.): "warlike, martial," epithet modifying Protesilaus. *οὐδέ τι*: "nor at all," negative conjunction with indefinite adverb. *λαοὶ* (nom. pl. masc.): "the people, troops," subject of the following clause. The line introduces the dead hero Protesilaus with his martial epithet; the troops are not [doing something] despite his excellence.

lines.original: δεύονθʼ ἡγεμόνος, πόθεόν γε μὲν ἐσθλὸν ἐόντα·
lines.english: The men did not lack a leader, though they longed for him who had been noble.
lines.gloss:
δεύονθʼ (δέομαι): 3rd pl. imperf. mid./pass., "they lacked" or "were in need of" (with genitive ἡγεμόνος). ἡγεμόνος (ἡγεμών): gen. sg. masc., "leader, commander." πόθεόν (ποθέω): 3rd pl. imperf. act., "they longed for, missed." ἐσθλὸν ἐόντα (ἐσθλός, εἰμί): acc. sg. masc. pres. part., "being noble/brave."

The soldiers lacked a leader and longed for him, noble though he was.

lines.original: τῷ δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.
lines.english: And with him forty black ships followed.
lines.gloss:
**τῷ δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.**

τῷ (demonstrative pronoun, dative singular masculine): "with him," referring to the leader just mentioned; ἅμα (adverb): "together with"; τεσσαράκοντα (numeral): "forty"; μέλαιναι (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "black," epithet for ships; ἕποντο (imperfect middle/passive, 3rd plural of ἕπομαι): "were following." The line states that forty black ships accompanied this commander.

lines.original: οἳ δὲ Φερὰς ἐνέμοντο παραὶ Βοιβηΐδα λίμνην
lines.english: Those who held Pherae beside the Boibeian lake
lines.gloss:
**οἳ δὲ Φερὰς ἐνέμοντο παραὶ Βοιβηΐδα λίμνην**

**οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who, those who"; **Φερὰς** (proper noun, acc. pl. fem.) "Pherae," a Thessalian city; **ἐνέμοντο** (imperfect mid./pass., 3rd pl. of νέμω) "inhabited, dwelt in"; **Βοιβηΐδα** (adj., acc. sg. fem.) "Boebeian," referring to Lake Boebeis; **λίμνην** (noun, acc. sg. fem.) "lake." Those who inhabited Pherae beside the Boebeian lake, continuing the catalogue's geographical description of Thessalian

lines.original: Βοίβην καὶ Γλαφύρας καὶ ἐϋκτιμένην Ἰαωλκόν,
lines.english: Boebe and Glaphyrae and well-built Iolcus.
lines.gloss: **Βοίβην** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Boibe, a town in Thessaly. **Γλαφύρας** (acc. pl. fem., proper noun): Glaphyrae, another Thessalian settlement. **ἐϋκτιμένην** (acc. sg. fem., perfect passive participle of ἐυκτίζω): "well-built" or "well-founded," modifying Iolcus. **Ἰαωλκόν** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Iolcus, the famous city of Jason. This line continues the catalogue of places near Lake Boibe, listing three settlements with the characteristic epithet for Iolcus.

lines.original: τῶν ἦρχʼ Ἀδμήτοιο φίλος πάϊς ἕνδεκα νηῶν
lines.english: Of these the dear son of Admetus led eleven ships.
lines.gloss:
**τῶν ἦρχʼ Ἀδμήτοιο φίλος πάϊς ἕνδεκα νηῶν**

**τῶν** (pronoun, gen. pl. masc.): "of these/them" — refers to the warriors from the cities just mentioned.
**ἦρχʼ** (verb, 3rd sg. impf. act.): "was leading/commanding" — elided form of ἦρχε.
**Ἀδμήτοιο** (proper noun, gen. sg.): "of Admetus" — patronymic genitive.
**φίλος** (adj., nom. sg. masc.): "dear, beloved."
**ἕνδεκα** (numeral): "eleven."
**νηῶν** (noun, gen. pl. fem.

lines.original: Εὔμηλος, τὸν ὑπʼ Ἀδμήτῳ τέκε δῖα γυναικῶν
lines.english: Eumelos, whom the noblest of women bore to Admetos.
lines.gloss:
**Εὔμηλος, τὸν ὑπʼ Ἀδμήτῳ τέκε δῖα γυναικῶν**

Εὔμηλος (nom. sg., proper name): Eumelus, the son of Admetus. τέκε (3rd sg. aor. indic. act., τίκτω): "bore" or "gave birth to." ὑπʼ Ἀδμήτῳ (prep. + dat. sg.): "to/for Admetus," indicating the father. δῖα γυναικῶν (nom. sg. fem., δῖος + gen. pl., γυνή): "noblest/most divine of women," a formulaic epithet.

lines.original: Ἄλκηστις Πελίαο θυγατρῶν εἶδος ἀρίστη.
lines.english: Alcestis, noblest in beauty of Pelias's daughters.
lines.gloss:
**Ἄλκηστις** (nom. sg. f., proper noun): Alcestis, subject of the verb "was best."

**Πελίαο** (gen. sg. m., proper noun): of Pelias, genitive of source/relationship.

**θυγατρῶν** (gen. pl. f., noun): of daughters, partitive genitive indicating the group from which Alcestis is singled out.

**εἶδος** (acc. sg. n., noun): in appearance/form, accusative of respect.

**ἀρίστη** (nom. sg. f., adj.): best/most excellent, predicate adjective agreeing with Ἄλκηστις.

The line identifies Alcestis as best in appearance among Pelias' daughters, completing the description of Eumelus' parentage.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἄρα Μηθώνην καὶ Θαυμακίην ἐνέμοντο
lines.english: Those who held Methone and Thaumacia
lines.gloss: **οἳ** (nom. pl. masc., relative pronoun) "who"; **ἐνέμοντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid., νέμω) "held, occupied"; **Μηθώνην** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun) "Methone" (city in Thessaly); **Θαυμακίην** (acc. sg. fem., proper noun) "Thaumacia" (city in Thessaly). This verse continues the Catalogue of Ships, listing commanders who held the Thessalian cities of Methone and Thaumacia.

lines.original: καὶ Μελίβοιαν ἔχον καὶ Ὀλιζῶνα τρηχεῖαν,
lines.english: and held Meliboea and rugged Olizon
lines.gloss:
**καὶ Μελίβοιαν ἔχον καὶ Ὀλιζῶνα τρηχεῖαν**

Μελίβοιαν (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Meliboea, a Thessalian city. ἔχον (3rd pl. impf. act., ἔχω): "they held/occupied." Ὀλιζῶνα (acc. sg. fem., proper noun): Olizon, another Thessalian town. τρηχεῖαν (acc. sg. fem., τρηχύς): "rugged, rocky." This line continues the catalogue listing territories under Philoctetes' command, with the epithet emphasizing Olizon's harsh terrain.

lines.original: τῶν δὲ Φιλοκτήτης ἦρχεν τόξων ἐῢ εἰδὼς
lines.english: Philoctetes skilled with the bow was commander of these men.
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive plural masculine) "of these/them"; **Φιλοκτήτης** (proper noun, nominative singular) "Philoctetes"; **ἦρχεν** (imperfect active indicative, 3rd singular of ἄρχω) "was leading/commanded"; **τόξων** (noun, genitive plural neuter) "in archery/the bow"; **εἰδώς** (perfect active participle, nominative singular masculine of οἶδα) "knowing/skilled." Philoctetes, skilled in archery, was commanding these men.

lines.original: ἑπτὰ νεῶν· ἐρέται δʼ ἐν ἑκάστῃ πεντήκοντα
lines.english: with seven ships, and in each one fifty oarsmen
lines.gloss:
**ἑπτὰ** (numeral, indeclinable): "seven," modifying νεῶν. **νεῶν** (noun, genitive plural of ναῦς): "of ships," governed by ἑπτά. **ἐρέται** (noun, nominative plural of ἐρέτης): "rowers, oarsmen," subject of the understood verb. **ἑκάστῃ** (adjective, dative singular of ἕκαστος): "in each (ship)," modifying the understood νηί. **πεντήκοντα** (numeral, indeclinable): "fifty," specifying the number of rowers per ship.

Philoctetes commanded seven ships, with fifty rowers in each, skilled with the bow for fighting.

lines.original: ἐμβέβασαν τόξων εὖ εἰδότες ἶφι μάχεσθαι.
lines.english: had embarked skilled in archery and strong in battle with the bow.
lines.gloss:
**ἐμβέβασαν** (ἐμβιβάζω): pluperfect 3rd plural, "had embarked/put aboard" — the crews had been placed in the ships.

**τόξων** (τόξον): genitive plural neuter, "of bows" — modifies εἰδότες, indicating expertise with archery.

**εὖ εἰδότες** (εἰδέναι): perfect participle nominative plural masculine, "knowing well" — describes the skill of the embarked warriors.

**ἶφι** (ἶφι): adverb, "mightily/strongly" — modifies μάχεσθαι, indicating fierce combat capability.

**μάχεσθαι** (μάχομαι): present middle/passive infinitive, "to fight" — completes the sense with ἶφι.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὃ μὲν ἐν νήσῳ κεῖτο κρατέρʼ ἄλγεα πάσχων
lines.english: But he lay on an island suffering strong pains.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλʼ ὃ μὲν ἐν νήσῳ κεῖτο κρατέρʼ ἄλγεα πάσχων**

Key words: **ὃ** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. sg. masc., "he"); **κεῖτο** (3rd sg. impf. mid. of κεῖμαι, "was lying"); **κρατέρʼ** (acc. pl. neut. of κρατερός, "severe, strong"); **ἄλγεα** (acc. pl. neut. of ἄλγος, "pains, sufferings"); **πάσχων** (pres. act. participle nom. sg. masc. of πάσχω, "suffering, enduring"). The line describes someone (Philoctetes) lying on

lines.original: Λήμνῳ ἐν ἠγαθέῃ, ὅθι μιν λίπον υἷες Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: in sacred Lemnos, where the sons of the Achaeans had left him
lines.gloss: **Λήμνῳ** (dat. sing., "at Lemnos"): dative of place where, referring to the island where Philoctetes was abandoned. **ἐν ἠγαθέῃ** (prep. + dat. sing. fem., "in sacred/noble"): the epithet *ἠγαθέη* (from *ἀγαθός*) describes Lemnos. **λίπον** (3rd pl. aor. act. indic. of *λείπω*, "they left/abandoned"): main verb indicating the Greeks' action. **υἷες Ἀχαιῶν** (nom. pl. + gen. pl., "sons of the Achaeans"): standard epic formula for the Greek warriors who abandoned him there.

lines.original: ἕλκεϊ μοχθίζοντα κακῷ ὀλοόφρονος ὕδρου·
lines.english: laboring with a painful wound from the deadly-minded serpent
lines.gloss:
Key words: **ἕλκεϊ** (dat. sg. neut. of ἕλκος) "with a wound"; **μοχθίζοντα** (pres. act. ptcp. acc. sg. masc. of μοχθίζω) "suffering, in pain"; **κακῷ** (dat. sg. neut. of κακός) "evil, grievous"; **ὀλοόφρονος** (gen. sg. fem. of ὀλοόφρων) "destructive-minded, deadly"; **ὕδρου** (gen. sg. fem. of ὕδρος) "of a water-snake." 

Philoctetes suffers from the grievous wound inflicted by the bite of a deadly water-snake.

lines.original: ἔνθʼ ὅ γε κεῖτʼ ἀχέων· τάχα δὲ μνήσεσθαι ἔμελλον
lines.english: There he lay in anguish, but soon the Argives were to remember him.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** 
- **κεῖτʼ** (imperfect middle/passive, 3rd sg. of κεῖμαι): "he lay"
- **ἀχέων** (present participle, nominative sg. masculine of ἄχομαι): "grieving, suffering"
- **μνήσεσθαι** (future middle/passive infinitive of μιμνήσκομαι): "to remember, be mindful of"
- **ἔμελλον** (imperfect, 3rd pl. of μέλλω): "they were about to, were destined to"

"There he lay suffering; but soon the Argives were destined to remember him." The line describes Philoctetes' abandonment and foreshadows his eventual recall.

lines.original: Ἀργεῖοι παρὰ νηυσὶ Φιλοκτήταο ἄνακτος.
lines.english: The Argives by the ships would soon remember their lord Philoctetes.
lines.gloss: **Ἀργεῖοι** (nom. pl. masc., "Argives"): the Greeks/Achaeans. **παρὰ νηυσί** (prep. + dat. pl., "beside the ships"): locative phrase indicating position. **Φιλοκτήταο** (gen. sg. masc., "of Philoctetes"): possessive genitive modifying ἄνακτος. **ἄνακτος** (gen. sg. masc., "of the lord/chieftain"): genitive of possession dependent on νηυσί. The Argives are stationed at the ships belonging to lord Philoctetes (who lies suffering, as the previous line indicates).

lines.original: οὐδὲ μὲν οὐδʼ οἳ ἄναρχοι ἔσαν, πόθεόν γε μὲν ἀρχόν·
lines.english: Yet they were not without a leader, though they longed for their true commander.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἄναρχοι (nominative plural masculine, "without a leader," from ἀν-αρχος), πόθεον (3rd plural imperfect active, "they missed/longed for," from ποθέω), ἀρχόν (accusative singular masculine, "leader/commander," from ἀρχός).

The men were not leaderless (in the strict sense), though they indeed longed for their proper leader; the negative construction with μέν...γε μέν emphasizes the contrast between their technical organization and their yearning for Philoctetes.

lines.original: ἀλλὰ Μέδων κόσμησεν Ὀϊλῆος νόθος υἱός,
lines.english: but Medon marshaled them, the bastard son of Oileus.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλὰ Μέδων κόσμησεν Ὀϊλῆος νόθος υἱός,**

**κόσμησεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of κοσμέω): "marshaled, ordered"; **Μέδων** (nom. sg.): proper name, "Medon"; **νόθος** (nom. sg. adj.): "bastard, illegitimate"; **υἱός** (nom. sg.): "son"; **Ὀϊλῆος** (gen. sg.): "of Oileus." Medon, the bastard son of Oileus, marshaled the troops in the absence of their regular leaders.

lines.original: τόν ῥʼ ἔτεκεν Ῥήνη ὑπʼ Ὀϊλῆϊ πτολιπόρθῳ.
lines.english: whom Rhene bore to Oileus sacker of cities.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** τόν (masculine accusative singular demonstrative pronoun, "him/whom"), ἔτεκεν (3rd singular aorist indicative active of τίκτω, "bore/gave birth to"), Ῥήνη (nominative singular proper noun, "Rhene"), ὑπʼ (preposition + dative, "by/under"), πτολιπόρθῳ (dative singular adjective, "city-sacking"). 

Rhene bore him (Medon) to city-sacking Oileus, explaining the parentage of the bastard son mentioned in the previous line.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ εἶχον Τρίκκην καὶ Ἰθώμην κλωμακόεσσαν,
lines.english: Those who held Trikke and craggy Ithome,
lines.gloss:
οἳ δʼ (οἵ + δέ, nominative plural masculine relative/demonstrative pronoun): "and those who" or "and they who"

εἶχον (imperfect active 3rd plural of ἔχω): "held" or "possessed"

Τρίκκην (accusative singular feminine proper noun): "Trikke," a city in Thessaly

Ἰθώμην (accusative singular feminine proper noun): "Ithome," another Thessalian city

κλωμακόεσσαν (accusative singular feminine adjective): "rugged with hills" or "mountainous," modifying Ithome

This line introduces the contingent from Trikke and mountainous Ithome, continuing the Catalogue of Ships' geographic survey.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ ἔχον Οἰχαλίην πόλιν Εὐρύτου Οἰχαλιῆος,
lines.english: and those who held Oechalia, city of Eurytus the Oechalian
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for οἵ τʼ ἔχον Οἰχαλίην πόλιν Εὐρύτου Οἰχαλιῆος:**

**οἵ τε** (relative pronoun + particle, nom. pl. masc.) "and who/those who"; **ἔχον** (imperfect, 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held, possessed"; **Οἰχαλίην** (acc. sing. fem.) "Oechalia" (city name); **Εὐρύτου** (gen. sing. masc.) "of Eurytus"; **Οἰχαλιῆος** (gen. sing. masc., epithet) "the Oechalian." This line completes the catalogue entry for those who held Oechalia, the city of Eurytus the

lines.original: τῶν αὖθʼ ἡγείσθην Ἀσκληπιοῦ δύο παῖδε
lines.english: Of these in turn the two sons of Asclepius were leaders
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (demonstrative pronoun, genitive plural masculine) "of these/them" — refers to the forces from Oichalia. **ἡγείσθην** (verb, 3rd person dual imperfect middle-passive, from ἡγέομαι) "were leading" — dual form indicating two leaders. **Ἀσκληπιοῦ** (proper noun, genitive singular) "of Asclepius" — the healing god. **δύο παῖδε** (numeral + noun, nominative dual) "two sons" — dual form παῖδε of παῖς. The two sons of Asclepius were leading these contingents.

lines.original: ἰητῆρʼ ἀγαθὼ Ποδαλείριος ἠδὲ Μαχάων·
lines.english: The two good healers Podaleirius and Machaon led them.
lines.gloss:
**ἰητῆρʼ ἀγαθὼ Ποδαλείριος ἠδὲ Μαχάων·**

*ἰητῆρε* (nom. dual, "healers") with *ἀγαθώ* (nom. dual masc. of ἀγαθός, "skilled/good") describes the two sons of Asclepius as skilled physicians. *Ποδαλείριος* and *Μαχάων* (both nom. sg.) are the proper names of these legendary healers. *ἠδέ* is the epic conjunction "and."

lines.original: τοῖς δὲ τριήκοντα γλαφυραὶ νέες ἐστιχόωντο.
lines.english: And with them thirty hollow ships were ranged in order.
lines.gloss:
**τοῖς** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "for these [men]," referring to the leaders just mentioned (Podalirius and Machaon).

**τριήκοντα** (numeral, indeclinable): "thirty," the number of ships.

**γλαφυραί** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "hollow, curved," epithet describing ships.

**νέες** (noun, nominative plural feminine): "ships," subject of the verb.

**ἐστιχόωντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect medio-passive): "were arrayed, were marshaled in rows."

The line states that thirty hollow ships were arrayed in formation under the command of these leaders.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἔχον Ὀρμένιον, οἵ τε κρήνην Ὑπέρειαν,
lines.english: Those who held Ormenion and the spring Hypereia
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.734:**

**ἔχον** (imperf. act. ind., 3rd pl. of ἔχω): "held" or "occupied," governing the geographic locations that follow. **Ὀρμένιον** (acc. sg., proper noun): Ormenion, a Thessalian town. **κρήνην** (acc. sg. fem. of κρήνη): "spring" or "fountain," here the proper name of a location. **Ὑπέρειαν** (acc. sg. fem., proper adj.): Hypereia, modifying κρήνην as another Thessalian place name. This line continues the catalog's enumeration of the territories controlled by Eurypylos's contingent.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ ἔχον Ἀστέριον Τιτάνοιό τε λευκὰ κάρηνα,
lines.english: and those who held Asterion and the white headlands of Titanos
lines.gloss:
**οἵ τʼ ἔχον Ἀστέριον Τιτάνοιό τε λευκὰ κάρηνα**

οἵ (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who"; ἔχον (imperfect 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held, occupied"; Ἀστέριον (acc. sg. proper noun) "Asterion," a city in Thessaly; Τιτάνοιο (gen. sg. proper noun) "of Titanos," another place; λευκὰ (acc. pl. neut. adj.) "white, bright"; κάρηνα (acc. pl. neut. noun) "peaks, headlands." The verse catalogs those who held Asterion and the white peaks of Titanos.

lines.original: τῶν ἦρχʼ Εὐρύπυλος Εὐαίμονος ἀγλαὸς υἱός·
lines.english: Eurypylus the splendid son of Euaemon was their leader.
lines.gloss:
**τῶν ἦρχʼ Εὐρύπυλος Εὐαίμονος ἀγλαὸς υἱός·**

*τῶν* (pronoun, gen. pl. masc.): "of them"; *ἦρχʼ* (impf. 3rd sg. from ἄρχω): "was leading, commanded"; *Εὐαίμονος* (proper noun, gen. sg.): "of Euaimon" (patronymic); *ἀγλαὸς* (adj. nom. sg. masc.): "splendid, glorious"; *υἱός* (noun, nom. sg.): "son." Eurpylos, the splendid son of Euaimon, commanded these contingents.

lines.original: τῷ δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.
lines.english: And with him forty black ships followed.
lines.gloss:
**τῷ δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.**

**τῷ** (pronoun, dative singular masculine): "with him" (referring to Eurypylos). **ἅμα** (adverb): "together with, along with." **τεσσαράκοντα** (numeral, indeclinable): "forty." **μέλαιναι** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "black, dark" (epithet for ships). **ἕποντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle): "were following, accompanied."

lines.original: οἳ δʼ Ἄργισσαν ἔχον καὶ Γυρτώνην ἐνέμοντο,
lines.english: Those who held Argissa and dwelt in Gyrtone
lines.gloss: **οἳ** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "those who/they"; **Ἄργισσαν** (proper noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Argissa," a city in Thessaly; **ἔχον** (imperfect act. indic. 3rd pl. of ἔχω) "held/possessed"; **Γυρτώνην** (proper noun, acc. sg. fem.) "Gyrtone," another Thessalian city; **ἐνέμοντο** (imperfect mid. indic. 3rd pl. of νέμω) "inhabited/occupied." This line introduces a new contingent who held the cities of Argissa and inhabited Gyrtone, both located in Thessaly.

lines.original: Ὄρθην Ἠλώνην τε πόλιν τʼ Ὀλοοσσόνα λευκήν,
lines.english: Orthe and Elone and the city of white Oloösson
lines.gloss:
**Ὄρθην Ἠλώνην τε πόλιν τʼ Ὀλοοσσόνα λευκήν**

Ὄρθην (accusative singular feminine): the city Orthe; Ἠλώνην (accusative singular feminine): Elone; πόλιν (accusative singular feminine, noun): "city," in apposition to Oloossona; Ὀλοοσσόνα (accusative singular feminine): Oloossona; λευκήν (accusative singular feminine, adjective): "white," "gleaming." The line continues the catalog listing three more Thessalian cities controlled by the leaders mentioned in the surrounding context, with "white Oloossona" receiving the epithet λευκήν.

lines.original: τῶν αὖθʼ ἡγεμόνευε μενεπτόλεμος Πολυποίτης
lines.english: Of these in turn war-steadfast Polypoetes was leader.
lines.gloss: **τῶν** (gen. pl. demonstrative pronoun) - "of these/them," refers to the aforementioned warriors or cities; **αὖθ(α)** (adverb) - "again, in turn"; **ἡγεμόνευε** (3rd sg. impf. act. indic. of ἡγεμονεύω) - "was leading, commanded"; **μενεπτόλεμος** (nom. sg. masc. adj.) - "steadfast in battle," compound epithet; **Πολυποίτης** (nom. sg.) - "Polypoetes," proper name. Polypoetes, steadfast in battle, was commanding these troops in turn.

lines.original: υἱὸς Πειριθόοιο τὸν ἀθάνατος τέκετο Ζεύς·
lines.english: son of Peirithous whom immortal Zeus begot
lines.gloss: **υἱὸς** (noun, nom. sg.) "son"; **Πειριθόοιο** (proper noun, gen. sg.) "of Peirithous"; **ἀθάνατος** (adjective, nom. sg.) "immortal"; **τέκετο** (verb, 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of τίκτω) "begot, fathered"; **Ζεύς** (proper noun, nom. sg.) "Zeus." The line identifies Polypoetes as the son of Peirithous, whom immortal Zeus himself begot, establishing the hero's divine ancestry through his grandfather.

lines.original: τόν ῥʼ ὑπὸ Πειριθόῳ τέκετο κλυτὸς Ἱπποδάμεια
lines.english: whom glorious Hippodameia bore to Peirithous
lines.gloss: **τόν** (demonstrative pronoun, accusative singular masculine) "him" – refers back to Polypoetes, object of τέκετο. **ὑπὸ** (preposition + dative) "by" – indicating agent with passive sense. **Πειριθόῳ** (proper noun, dative singular) "by Peirithous" – agent/father. **τέκετο** (verb, 3rd singular aorist middle indicative of τίκτω) "bore, gave birth to." **κλυτὸς** (adjective, nominative singular feminine) "glorious, renowned" – modifying Ἱπποδάμεια. **Ἱπποδάμεια** (proper noun, nominative singular) "Hippodameia" – the famous mother, subject of the verb.

lines.original: ἤματι τῷ ὅτε Φῆρας ἐτίσατο λαχνήεντας,
lines.english: on the day when he punished the shaggy Centaurs
lines.gloss:
**ἤματι** (dat. sg. n. of ἦμαρ): "on the day," temporal dative. **τῷ ὅτε**: "on which when," relative-temporal construction (demonstrative + relative adverb). **Φῆρας** (acc. pl. m. of Φήρ): "the Centaurs," wild beast-men. **ἐτίσατο** (3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of τίνω): "he punished/made pay." **λαχνήεντας** (acc. pl. m. adj.): "shaggy, hairy." 

The line refers to the day Peirithous punished the shaggy Centaurs, alluding to the famous battle at his wedding.

lines.original: τοὺς δʼ ἐκ Πηλίου ὦσε καὶ Αἰθίκεσσι πέλασσεν·
lines.english: He drove them from Pelion and brought them near to the Aethices.
lines.gloss:
**τοὺς δʼ ἐκ Πηλίου ὦσε καὶ Αἰθίκεσσι πέλασσεν·**

*τοὺς* (demonstrative pronoun, acc. pl. masc.): "them" (the Centaurs). *Πηλίου* (proper noun, gen. sg. neut.): "from Pelion" (the mountain). *ὦσε* (verb, 3rd sg. aor. indic. act. of ὠθέω): "drove" or "thrust." *Αἰθίκεσσι* (proper noun, dat. pl. masc.): "to/toward the Aethices" (a Thessalian tribe). *πέλασσεν* (verb, 3rd sg. aor. indic. act. of π

lines.original: οὐκ οἶος, ἅμα τῷ γε Λεοντεὺς ὄζος Ἄρηος
lines.english: Not alone, but with him Leonteus the scion of Ares
lines.gloss: **οὐκ οἶος** (not alone): οὐκ negates οἶος (nom. sg. masc. of οἶος "alone, sole"). **ἅμα** (together with, along with): adverb/preposition governing the dative. **τῷ** (him): dative sg. masc. demonstrative pronoun, referring to the previously mentioned hero. **Λεοντεὺς** (Leonteus): nom. sg. proper name, subject of an implied verb. **ὄζος** (branch, scion): nom. sg. masc., metaphorical epithet meaning "offspring." **Ἄρηος** (of Ares): gen. sg. of Ἄρης, indicating divine lineage or martial prowess.

lines.original: υἱὸς ὑπερθύμοιο Κορώνου Καινεΐδαο·
lines.english: son of greathearted Koronos, son of Kaineus
lines.gloss:
**υἱὸς ὑπερθύμοιο Κορώνου Καινεΐδαο·**

*υἱὸς* (nom. sg. masc., "son") is the subject identifying Leonteus; *ὑπερθύμοιο* (gen. sg. masc., "high-spirited, exceedingly bold") modifies *Κορώνου*; *Κορώνου* (gen. sg. masc., "of Coronus") is the father's name in patronymic construction; *Καινεΐδαο* (gen. sg. masc., "of Caeneus," epic form) marks Coronus as son of Caeneus, establishing three-generation genealogy. The line identifies Leonteus as son of the high-spirited Coronus, grandson of Caeneus.

lines.original: τοῖς δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.
lines.english: And with them forty black ships followed.
lines.gloss:
**τοῖς** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural masculine): "with/for them" (referring to the previously mentioned leader and forces).
**τεσσαράκοντα** (numeral, indeclinable): "forty."
**μέλαιναι** (adjective, nominative plural feminine): "black," modifying νῆες.
**νῆες** (noun, nominative plural feminine from ναῦς): "ships," subject of ἕποντο.
**ἕποντο** (verb, 3rd plural imperfect middle-passive of ἕπομαι): "were following/accompanied."

Forty black ships accompanied them (the contingent under the son of Coronus).

lines.original: Γουνεὺς δʼ ἐκ Κύφου ἦγε δύω καὶ εἴκοσι νῆας·
lines.english: Gouneus led twenty-two ships from Cyphus.
lines.gloss:
**Γουνεύς** (nom. sg. masc.) "Gouneus" - subject, leader from Cyphus. **ἐκ Κύφου** "from Cyphus" - prepositional phrase indicating origin (Κύφου gen. sg.). **ἦγε** (3rd sg. impf. act.) "was leading" - main verb from ἄγω. **δύω καὶ εἴκοσι** "two and twenty" (twenty-two) - cardinal numbers modifying νῆας. **νῆας** (acc. pl. fem.) "ships" - direct object of ἦγε.

Gouneus leads a contingent of twenty-two ships from Cyphus, continuing the Catalogue of Ships with another Greek leader and his forces.

lines.original: τῷ δʼ Ἐνιῆνες ἕποντο μενεπτόλεμοί τε Περαιβοὶ
lines.english: With him followed the Enienes and the battle-staunch Peraebi.
lines.gloss: **τῷ** (dat. sg. masc. of ὁ): dative of accompaniment, "with him" (i.e., with Gouneus). **Ἐνιῆνες** (nom. pl. masc.): the Enienes, a Thessalian tribe. **ἕποντο** (3rd pl. imperf. mid. of ἕπομαι): "followed" or "accompanied." **μενεπτόλεμοι** (nom. pl. masc. adj.): "steadfast in battle," compound adjective modifying Περαιβοί. **Περαιβοί** (nom. pl. masc.): the Peraeboi, another Thessalian people. The Enienes and war-steadfast Peraeboi followed him as contingents in his command.

lines.original: οἳ περὶ Δωδώνην δυσχείμερον οἰκίʼ ἔθεντο,
lines.english: who settled their homes around wintry Dodona
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.750:**

Key words: **Δωδώνην** (acc. sg. fem., proper name) "Dodona," the famous oracular site; **δυσχείμερον** (acc. sg. fem. adj.) "wintry, storm-swept," modifying Dodona; **οἰκίʼ** (acc. pl. neut. noun, crasis for οἰκία) "dwellings, homes"; **ἔθεντο** (3rd pl. aor. mid. indic. of τίθημι) "established, made." The line describes those who established their homes around wintry Dodona.

lines.original: οἵ τʼ ἀμφʼ ἱμερτὸν Τιταρησσὸν ἔργα νέμοντο
lines.english: and those who tended their fields around lovely Titaressus
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἀμφί (prep. + acc.) "around, about"; ἱμερτόν (adj. acc. masc. sing.) "lovely, desirable"; Τιταρησσόν (proper noun, acc.) the Titaressos river, tributary of the Peneios; ἔργα (noun acc. neut. pl.) "lands, fields"; νέμοντο (imperf. mid. 3rd pl. of νέμω) "dwelt, inhabited, pastured."

The line describes those who dwelt around the lovely Titaressos river, working or inhabiting the lands near this tributary of the Peneios in Thessaly.

lines.original: ὅς ῥʼ ἐς Πηνειὸν προΐει καλλίρροον ὕδωρ,
lines.english: which pours its beautiful-flowing water into Peneius
lines.gloss: **ὅς** (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) "which" refers to the Titaressos river from the previous line. **προΐει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of προΐημι) "sends forth, pours forth." **καλλίρροον** (adj., acc. sg. neut.) "beautifully-flowing, fair-flowing" modifies ὕδωρ. **ὕδωρ** (noun, acc. sg. neut.) "water," direct object of προΐει. The line describes how the Titaressos sends its beautiful waters into the Peneios river.

lines.original: οὐδʼ ὅ γε Πηνειῷ συμμίσγεται ἀργυροδίνῃ,
lines.english: nor does it mingle with the silver-eddying Peneios
lines.gloss:
**οὐδʼ ὅ γε Πηνειῷ συμμίσγεται ἀργυροδίνῃ**

*οὐδέ* (conjunction): "nor, and not"; *συμμίσγεται* (3rd sg. pres. mid. indic. of συμμίσγω): "mixes with, mingles with" (+ dative); *Πηνειῷ* (dat. sg. of Πηνειός): "with the Peneius" (river name); *ἀργυροδίνῃ* (dat. sg. epithet, ἀργυρο- + δίνη): "silver-swirling, with silvery eddies," modifying Peneius. The river does not mingle with the silver-eddied Peneius but flows atop

lines.original: ἀλλά τέ μιν καθύπερθεν ἐπιρρέει ἠΰτʼ ἔλαιον·
lines.english: but flows over it from above like oil
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλά** (conjunction): "but" — marks strong contrast with the previous statement about not mingling.

**καθύπερθεν** (adverb): "from above, over the top" — describes the spatial relationship of how the Styx flows.

**ἐπιρρέει** (verb, 3rd sing. pres. ind.): "flows upon/over" — from ἐπιρρέω, describing the surface flow.

**ἠΰτε** (adverb/particle): "just like, as" — introduces the simile.

**ἔλαιον** (noun, acc. sing. neuter): "oil" — the comparandum, illustrating how oil floats without mixing.

The Styx flows over the Peneus from above like oil, remaining separate and unmixed due to its sacred oath-nature.

lines.original: ὅρκου γὰρ δεινοῦ Στυγὸς ὕδατός ἐστιν ἀπορρώξ.
lines.english: For it is a branch flowing from the terrible oath-water of the Styx.
lines.gloss:
**ὅρκου γὰρ δεινοῦ Στυγὸς ὕδατός ἐστιν ἀπορρώξ.**

Key words: **ὅρκου** (gen. sg. of ὅρκος) "of an oath"; **δεινοῦ** (gen. sg. adj.) "terrible, dread"; **Στυγὸς** (gen. sg. of Στύξ) "of the Styx"; **ὕδατος** (gen. sg. of ὕδωρ) "of water"; **ἀπορρώξ** (nom. sg. fem.) "effluence, outflow." The Styx water serves as the gods' most terrible oath by which they swear.

lines.original: Μαγνήτων δʼ ἦρχε Πρόθοος Τενθρηδόνος υἱός,
lines.english: Prothoös son of Tenthredon led the Magnetes.
lines.gloss: **Μαγνήτων** (genitive plural, Μάγνης): "of the Magnetes," genitive of the people governed by Prothoos. **ἦρχε** (3rd singular imperfect, ἄρχω): "was leading/commanding," from ἄρχω, governing the genitive Μαγνήτων. **Πρόθοος** (nominative singular): "Prothoos," the Magnesian leader. **Τενθρηδόνος** (genitive singular): "of Tenthredon," patronymic identifying Prothoos's father. **υἱός** (nominative singular, υἱός): "son," in apposition to Πρόθοος.

lines.original: οἳ περὶ Πηνειὸν καὶ Πήλιον εἰνοσίφυλλον
lines.english: those who dwelt around Peneus and leafy Pelion
lines.gloss: **οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who" — refers to the Magnetes. **περὶ Πηνειόν** (preposition + acc.) "around the Peneios" — the river of Thessaly. **Πήλιον** (acc. sing. neut.) "Pelion" — the famous mountain. **εἰνοσίφυλλον** (acc. sing. neut., compound adjective) "leaf-shaking" or "with trembling leaves" — epithet modifying Pelion. The line describes the Magnetes dwelling around the river Peneios and wooded Mount Pelion.

lines.original: ναίεσκον· τῶν μὲν Πρόθοος θοὸς ἡγεμόνευε,
lines.english: These men Prothous the swift commanded.
lines.gloss: **ναίεσκον** (imperfect of ναίω): "they dwelt" - iterative/habitual imperfect describing the Magnesians' dwelling around Peneus and Pelion. **τῶν** (genitive plural of ὁ): "of these" - partitive genitive referring to the previously mentioned people. **Πρόθοος** (nominative singular): Prothous, son of Tenthredon, leader of the Magnesian contingent. **θοός** (nominative singular adjective): "swift" or "nimble" - epithet modifying Prothous. **ἡγεμόνευε** (imperfect of ἡγεμονεύω): "was leading" - indicates his command over this group.

lines.original: τῷ δʼ ἅμα τεσσαράκοντα μέλαιναι νῆες ἕποντο.
lines.english: And with him forty black ships followed.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** τῷ (dative singular masculine demonstrative pronoun, "with him"), τεσσαράκοντα (indeclinable numeral, "forty"), μέλαιναι (nominative plural feminine adjective, "black"), νῆες (nominative plural feminine noun, "ships"), ἕποντο (3rd plural imperfect middle/passive indicative of ἕπομαι, "followed"). 

The line describes how forty black ships followed with this leader, a formulaic verse used throughout the Catalogue to enumerate each contingent's naval strength.

lines.original: οὗτοι ἄρʼ ἡγεμόνες Δαναῶν καὶ κοίρανοι ἦσαν·
lines.english: These then were the leaders and commanders of the Danaans.
lines.gloss: **οὗτοι** (demonstrative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "these"; **ἡγεμόνες** (noun, nom. pl. masc.) "leaders"; **Δαναῶν** (noun, gen. pl.) "of the Danaans/Greeks"; **κοίρανοι** (noun, nom. pl. masc.) "commanders, chiefs"; **ἦσαν** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. act. indic. of εἰμί) "were." This verse concludes the Catalogue of Ships by summarizing that these men were the leaders and commanders of the Greek forces.

lines.original: τίς τὰρ τῶν ὄχʼ ἄριστος ἔην σύ μοι ἔννεπε Μοῦσα
lines.english: Tell me then Muse who was by far the best of them all
lines.gloss: **τίς** (interrogative pronoun, nom. sg.) "who"; **ὄχʼ** = **ὄχα** (superlative adverb) "by far"; **ἄριστος** (superlative adj., nom. sg. masc.) "best"; **ἔην** (3rd sg. impf. of εἰμί) "was"; **ἔννεπε** (2nd sg. aor. imperat. of ἐνέπω) "tell!"; **Μοῦσα** (voc. sg.) "O Muse." The poet invokes the Muse to reveal who was by far the best of the Danaans and their horses who followed with the Atreidae.

lines.original: αὐτῶν ἠδʼ ἵππων, οἳ ἅμʼ Ἀτρεΐδῃσιν ἕποντο.
lines.english: of the men themselves and of the horses who followed with the sons of Atreus.
lines.gloss: **αὐτῶν** (αὐτός, genitive plural masculine): "of the men themselves" — partitive genitive dependent on the superlative in the previous line. **ἠδέ** (conjunction): "and" — connecting the two categories being evaluated (men and horses). **ἵππων** (ἵππος, genitive plural masculine): "of horses" — parallel to αὐτῶν, completing the dual subject of inquiry. **ἕποντο** (ἕπομαι, 3rd plural imperfect middle/passive): "followed, accompanied" — describing the horses' attendance with the Atreids on the expedition to Troy.

lines.original: ἵπποι μὲν μέγʼ ἄρισται ἔσαν Φηρητιάδαο,
lines.english: The best horses by far were those of the son of Pheres.
lines.gloss: **ἵπποι** (nom. pl. masc., "horses") **μὲν** (particle, "indeed," marking contrast) **μέγʼ** (adv., crasis for μέγα, "by far, greatly") **ἄρισται** (nom. pl. fem., superlative of ἀγαθός, "best") **ἔσαν** (3rd pl. impf. of εἰμί, "were") **Φηρητιάδαο** (gen. sg. masc., patronymic, "of the son of Pheretius," i.e., Admetus/Eumelus). The horses of Eumelus, son of Admetus (himself son of Pheres), were by far the best in the Greek army.

lines.original: τὰς Εὔμηλος ἔλαυνε ποδώκεας ὄρνιθας ὣς
lines.english: which Eumelus drove, swift as birds in flight
lines.gloss: **τὰς** (demonstrative pronoun, acc. fem. pl.) "them" refers to the mares; **Εὔμηλος** (proper noun, nom. masc. sg.) "Eumelos," son of Admetus; **ἔλαυνε** (imperfect act. ind. 3rd sg. of ἐλαύνω) "was driving"; **ποδώκεας** (adj., acc. fem. pl.) "swift-footed"; **ὄρνιθας ὣς** "like birds" (comparative simile). Eumelos drove those swift-footed mares like birds, emphasizing their remarkable speed and synchronized movement.

lines.original: ὄτριχας οἰέτεας σταφύλῇ ἐπὶ νῶτον ἐΐσας·
lines.english: mares both female of the same age and matching in coat color along their backs
lines.gloss:
**ὄτριχας** (acc. pl. fem., ὄτριξ): "swift, fleet"; **οἰέτεας** (acc. pl. fem., οἰέτης): "of one age/birth"; **σταφύλῃ** (dat. sg. fem., σταφύλη): "bunch of grapes, cluster" (here metaphor for close-bunched formation); **νῶτον** (acc. sg. neut., νῶτον): "back"; **ἐΐσας** (acc. pl. fem., pf. pple. ἔοικα): "resembling, alike." 

The line describes Eumelos' mares as swift, of matching age, equal in height at the back as a bunch of grapes (perfectly matched in size and formation).

lines.original: τὰς ἐν Πηρείῃ θρέψʼ ἀργυρότοξος Ἀπόλλων
lines.english: These silver-bowed Apollo reared in Pereia, both of them mares, bearing the terror of Ares.
lines.gloss: **τὰς** (fem. acc. pl., demonstrative/relative pronoun) "these/which"; **Πηρείῃ** (fem. dat. sg., proper noun) "in Pereie"; **θρέψʼ** (aor. act. ind. 3rd sg., τρέφω) "reared/nurtured"; **ἀργυρότοξος** (masc. nom. sg., epithet) "silver-bowed"; **Ἀπόλλων** (masc. nom. sg., proper noun) "Apollo." The silver-bowed Apollo nurtured these (mares) in Pereie, linking the divine rearing of Eumelos's exceptional horses.

lines.original: ἄμφω θηλείας, φόβον Ἄρηος φορεούσας.
lines.english: both females, bearing the terror of Ares.
lines.gloss: **ἄμφω** (adj., nom. dual fem.) "both" - referring to the two mares; **θηλείας** (adj., acc. pl. fem.) "female" - describing the mares' sex; **φόβον** (noun, acc. sg. masc.) "fear, rout" - object of the participle; **Ἄρηος** (noun, gen. sg. masc.) "of Ares" - genitive with φόβον; **φορεούσας** (participle, acc. pl. fem. pres. act.) "carrying, bearing" - describing the mares' warlike nature. Both female horses bearing the terror of Ares into battle.

lines.original: ἀνδρῶν αὖ μέγʼ ἄριστος ἔην Τελαμώνιος Αἴας
lines.english: The best of the men by far was Telamonian Ajax.
lines.gloss:
**ἀνδρῶν** (gen. pl. of ἀνήρ, "man"): partitive genitive, "of men."
**αὖ** (particle): "in turn," "on the other hand," marking a transition.
**μέγʼ** (adverb, crasis for μέγα): "greatly," "by far," modifying ἄριστος.
**ἄριστος** (superlative adj., nom. sg. masc.): "best," "most excellent."
**Τελαμώνιος Αἴας** (nom. sg.): "Telamonian Ajax," son of Telamon, distinguished from the lesser Ajax.

The line identifies Ajax son of Telamon as by far the best of the warriors while Achilles was withdrawing from battle in his wrath.

lines.original: ὄφρʼ Ἀχιλεὺς μήνιεν· ὃ γὰρ πολὺ φέρτατος ἦεν,
lines.english: while Achilles remained angry, for he was by far the mightiest.
lines.gloss: **ὄφρʼ** (ὄφρα): temporal conjunction, "while, as long as." **Ἀχιλεὺς**: nominative singular subject, "Achilles." **μήνιεν**: 3rd sg. imperfect of μηνίω, "was wrathful, was angry." **φέρτατος**: superlative adjective, nominative, from φέρτερος, "best, strongest, most excellent." **ἦεν**: 3rd sg. imperfect of εἰμί, "was." The verse explains that Ajax was best of the Achaeans while Achilles remained angry, for Achilles himself was by far the most excellent (warrior).

lines.original: ἵπποι θʼ οἳ φορέεσκον ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα.
lines.english: and the horses that used to carry the blameless son of Peleus
lines.gloss:
**ἵπποι** (nom. pl. masc., "horses") **θʼ** = **τε** (enclitic conjunction, "and"); **φορέεσκον** (3rd pl. impf. iterative of φορέω, "were accustomed to carry"); **ἀμύμονα** (acc. sg. masc., "blameless, noble"); **Πηλεΐωνα** (acc. sg. masc., "son of Peleus," i.e., Achilles). 

The iterative imperfect **φορέεσκον** emphasizes the horses' customary action of bearing Achilles into battle, now suspended during his withdrawal from combat.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ὃ μὲν ἐν νήεσσι κορωνίσι ποντοπόροισι
lines.english: But he among the sea-faring curved ships lay.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** *νήεσσι* (dat. pl. of ναῦς, "ship"): "in/among the ships"; *κορωνίσι* (dat. pl. adj. from κορωνίς, "curved"): "curved" (describing ships with curved sterns); *ποντοπόροισι* (dat. pl. adj. from ποντόπορος, "sea-faring"): "sea-traversing, seafaring"; *μέν* (particle): establishes contrast with following *δέ*, "on the one hand."

The line describes Achilles remaining among his curved, sea-faring ships, with *μέν* anticipating the contrast that he stays idle while others fight.

lines.original: κεῖτʼ ἀπομηνίσας Ἀγαμέμνονι ποιμένι λαῶν
lines.english: he lay nursing his wrath against Agamemnon shepherd of the people
lines.gloss: **κεῖτο** (3rd sg. impf. mid. of κεῖμαι): "lay, remained," describing Achilles' inactive state in his ships. **ἀπομηνίσας** (aor. act. ptc. nom. sg. masc. of ἀπομηνίω): "having withdrawn in wrath," expressing Achilles' decisive rejection and anger. **Ἀγαμέμνονι** (dat. sg. of Ἀγαμέμνων): dative of person offended, "at/toward Agamemnon." **ποιμένι λαῶν** (dat. sg.): traditional epithet "shepherd of the people," here in apposition to Agamemnon.

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδῃ· λαοὶ δὲ παρὰ ῥηγμῖνι θαλάσσης
lines.english: the son of Atreus; and the people beside the breaking of the sea
lines.gloss:
**Ἀτρεΐδῃ· λαοὶ δὲ παρὰ ῥηγμῖνι θαλάσσης**

**Ἀτρεΐδῃ** (dat. sing., "son of Atreus"): dative after ἀπομηνίσας, specifying against whom Achilles is wrathful. **λαοὶ** (nom. pl., "the troops/people"): subject of the implied verb, contrasting with Achilles' isolation. **παρὰ** (prep. + dat., "beside, along"): governs ῥηγμῖνι, indicating location. **ῥηγμῖνι** (dat. sing., "breaking of waves, surf, shore"): place where the troops remain encamped. **θαλάσσης** (

lines.original: δίσκοισιν τέρποντο καὶ αἰγανέῃσιν ἱέντες
lines.english: They amused themselves throwing discs and casting javelins.
lines.gloss: **δίσκοισιν** (dative plural of δίσκος, "discus"): instrumental dative with τέρποντο, "with discuses." **τέρποντο** (3rd plural imperfect middle of τέρπω, "to delight, enjoy"): "they were enjoying themselves." **αἰγανέῃσιν** (dative plural of αἰγανέη, "javelin"): another instrumental dative, "with javelins." **ἱέντες** (nominative plural masculine present participle of ἵημι, "to hurl, throw"): "throwing." The Achaean troops amuse themselves by hurling discuses and javelins during the respite from battle.

lines.original: τόξοισίν θʼ· ἵπποι δὲ παρʼ ἅρμασιν οἷσιν ἕκαστος
lines.english: and with bows, and the horses each beside their chariots
lines.gloss:
**τόξοισίν** (dat. pl. of τόξον): "with bows," dative of means/instrument. **ἵπποι** (nom. pl. of ἵππος): "horses," subject. **ἅρμασιν** (dat. pl. of ἅρμα): "chariots," dative of place where. **οἷσιν** (dat. pl. of ὅς): "their own," possessive pronoun agreeing with ἅρμασιν. **ἕκαστος** (nom. sg. of ἕκαστος): "each one," referring to each horse individually.

The warriors amused themselves with bows (completing the list of athletic activities), while their horses stood idle beside their respective chariots.

lines.original: λωτὸν ἐρεπτόμενοι ἐλεόθρεπτόν τε σέλινον
lines.english: feeding on lotus and marsh-nurtured celery
lines.gloss:
**λωτὸν ἐρεπτόμενοι ἐλεόθρεπτόν τε σέλινον**

**λωτὸν** (acc. sg. masc.) – "lotus" or "clover," object of ἐρεπτόμενοι; **ἐρεπτόμενοι** (pres. mid. ptc. nom. pl. masc., ἐρέπτομαι) – "feeding on," "grazing"; **ἐλεόθρεπτον** (acc. sg. neut., ἐλεό-θρεπτος) – "marsh-nourished," compound adjective modifying σέλινον; **σέλινον** (acc. sg. neut.) – "celery" or "parsley," second object of the participle. The horses

lines.original: ἕστασαν· ἅρματα δʼ εὖ πεπυκασμένα κεῖτο ἀνάκτων
lines.english: They stood; and the well-made chariots of the lords lay idle in the huts.
lines.gloss: ἕστασαν (ἵστημι): 3rd plural pluperfect, "they stood" or "had taken their stand." ἅρματα (ἅρμα, -ατος, τό): nominative/accusative plural neuter, "chariots." πεπυκασμένα (πυκάζω): perfect passive participle, nominative/accusative plural neuter, "closely packed" or "compactly stored." κεῖτο (κεῖμαι): 3rd singular imperfect middle, "lay" or "were lying." The horses stood idle while their lords' chariots lay stored away, the warriors longing for their battle-loving leader.

lines.original: ἐν κλισίῃς· οἳ δʼ ἀρχὸν ἀρηΐφιλον ποθέοντες
lines.english: and they longing for their war-loving leader wandered here and there through the camp and did not fight
lines.gloss: **ἐν κλισίῃς**: ἐν + dative singular of κλισίη, "in the huts/shelters" (location where the chariots were stored). **οἳ δʼ**: nominative plural masculine of ὅς (relative/demonstrative pronoun), "and they/these men" (the horses). **ἀρχὸν**: accusative singular of ἄρχος, "their leader/master." **ἀρηΐφιλον**: accusative singular masculine adjective (compound: Ares + φίλος), "war-loving, dear to Ares" (modifying ἀρχόν). **ποθέοντες**: nominative plural masculine present participle of ποθέω, "longing for, missing." The horses stand idle missing their war-loving master while the chariots rest in the shelters.

lines.original: φοίτων ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα κατὰ στρατὸν οὐδὲ μάχοντο.
lines.english: They wandered here and there throughout the camp and did not fight.
lines.gloss: **φοίτων** (present participle, nominative plural masculine, from φοιτάω): "moving about, ranging"; **ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα**: "here and there, to and fro"; **στρατόν** (accusative singular masculine): "army, host"; **μάχοντο** (imperfect middle/passive, 3rd plural, from μάχομαι): "they were fighting." The Myrmidons move aimlessly throughout the camp, not engaging in battle, while longing for their war-loving leader Achilles.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἄρʼ ἴσαν ὡς εἴ τε πυρὶ χθὼν πᾶσα νέμοιτο·
lines.english: They came on as though the whole earth were being consumed by fire.
lines.gloss:
**οἳ δʼ ἄρʼ ἴσαν ὡς εἴ τε πυρὶ χθὼν πᾶσα νέμοιτο·**

**ἴσαν** (3rd pl. impf. of εἶμι): "they went/advanced"
**πυρὶ** (dat. sg. neut. of πῦρ): "with fire," dative of means
**χθὼν** (nom. sg. fem.): "earth/land," subject of νέμοιτο
**πᾶσα** (nom. sg. fem. of πᾶς): "all/entire," modifying χθὼν
**νέμοιτο** (3rd sg. pres. opt. mid. of νέμω): "were being grazed/

lines.original: γαῖα δʼ ὑπεστενάχιζε Διὶ ὣς τερπικεραύνῳ
lines.english: The earth groaned beneath them as when Zeus who delights in thunder is angry.
lines.gloss: **γαῖα** (nom. sg. fem., "earth") **ὑπεστενάχιζε** (3rd sg. impf. act., "groaned beneath"), **Διὶ** (dat. sg. masc., "for Zeus"), **τερπικεραύνῳ** (dat. sg. masc. epithet, "who delights in thunder/lightning"). The earth groaned beneath as it does for Zeus who delights in thunderbolts, continuing the cosmic simile of divine wrath.

lines.original: χωομένῳ ὅτε τʼ ἀμφὶ Τυφωέϊ γαῖαν ἱμάσσῃ
lines.english: when he is angered and lashes the earth around Typhoeus with his thunderbolts
lines.gloss: **χωομένῳ** (pres. mid./pass. participle, dat. sing. masc. of χόομαι) "being angry, in wrath" — modifies Διί from the previous line; **ὅτε** (temporal conjunction) "when"; **ἀμφί** (preposition + acc.) "around, about"; **Τυφωέϊ** (dat. sing. of Τυφωεύς) "Typhoeus" (the monstrous enemy of Zeus); **ἱμάσσῃ** (pres. subj. 3rd sing. of ἱμάσσω) "he lashes, scourges" (Zeus whipping the earth around Typhoeus with thunderbolts). The line describes Zeus in his wrath lashing the earth around Typhoeus with lightning.

lines.original: εἰν Ἀρίμοις, ὅθι φασὶ Τυφωέος ἔμμεναι εὐνάς·
lines.english: in the land of the Arimoi, where men say is the bed of Typhoeus
lines.gloss:
**εἰν Ἀρίμοις, ὅθι φασὶ Τυφωέος ἔμμεναι εὐνάς·**

*Ἀρίμοις* (dat. pl., "Arimoi"): locative dative indicating the place in Cilicia associated with Typhoeus. *ὅθι* (relative adverb, "where"): introduces relative clause of place. *φασὶ* (3rd pl. pres. act. indic., φημί, "they say"): marks hearsay/tradition. *Τυφωέος* (gen. sg., "of Typhoeus"): the monstrous Titan Zeus defeated. *εὐνάς* (acc. pl., "resting-place, lair"): where the vanquished monster lies buried.

lines.original: ὣς ἄρα τῶν ὑπὸ ποσσὶ μέγα στεναχίζετο γαῖα
lines.english: So beneath their feet the earth groaned mightily as they went.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ἄρα τῶν ὑπὸ ποσσὶ μέγα στεναχίζετο γαῖα**

**ὑπὸ ποσσί** (prep. + dat. pl. of πούς): "beneath their feet"; **στεναχίζετο** (3rd sg. impf. mid./pass. of στεναχίζω): "groaned, resounded"; **γαῖα** (nom. sg.): "earth, ground." The earth groans mightily beneath the feet of the advancing warriors, emphasizing the massive scale of their movement.

lines.original: ἐρχομένων· μάλα δʼ ὦκα διέπρησσον πεδίοιο.
lines.english: as they marched, and very swiftly they crossed over the plain.
lines.gloss: **ἐρχομένων**: present middle/passive participle, genitive plural of ἔρχομαι ("going," "marching"); genotes the advancing troops under whose feet the earth groaned. **μάλα**: adverb, "very," "exceedingly," intensifying the following adverb. **ὦκα**: adverb, "swiftly," "quickly," describing the speed of their movement. **διέπρησσον**: imperfect active, 3rd plural of διαπράσσω/διαπρήθω ("they traversed," "they crossed"); the army rapidly covered the plain.

lines.original: Τρωσὶν δʼ ἄγγελος ἦλθε ποδήνεμος ὠκέα Ἶρις
lines.english: To the Trojans came swift-footed Iris, fleet as the wind, as messenger.
lines.gloss: **Τρωσὶν** (dat. pl. of Τρῶες) "to/for the Trojans"; **ἄγγελος** (nom. sg. f.) "messenger"; **ποδήνεμος** (nom. sg. f., compound adj.) "wind-footed, swift as the wind"; **ὠκέα** (nom. sg. f., adj.) "swift"; **Ἶρις** (nom. sg. f.) "Iris" (goddess). Storm-footed Iris came as a swift messenger to the Trojans, with the epithet emphasizing her divine speed.

lines.original: πὰρ Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο σὺν ἀγγελίῃ ἀλεγεινῇ·
lines.english: from aegis-bearing Zeus with a grievous message
lines.gloss:
**πὰρ** (prep. + gen.) "from": indicates source or origin, here "from the side of" Zeus.

**Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο** (gen. sg., epithet) "of aegis-bearing Zeus": compound epithet (αἰγί- + ἔχω) modifying Zeus, the divine sender.

**σὺν ἀγγελίῃ** (prep. + dat. sg.) "with a message": ἀγγελίῃ is the noun expressing Iris's mission purpose.

**ἀλεγεινῇ** (adj., dat. sg. fem.) "grievous, painful": modifies ἀγγελίῃ, indicating the message's distressing nature for the Trojans.

lines.original: οἳ δʼ ἀγορὰς ἀγόρευον ἐπὶ Πριάμοιο θύρῃσι
lines.english: and they held assembly at the gates of Priam
lines.gloss:
**οἳ δʼ ἀγορὰς ἀγόρευον ἐπὶ Πριάμοιο θύρῃσι**

**οἳ** (relative pronoun, nom. pl. masc.) "who, they"; **ἀγορὰς** (noun, acc. pl. fem.) "assemblies, speeches"; **ἀγόρευον** (verb, 3rd pl. impf. act.) "were holding, were speaking"; **ἐπὶ** (preposition + dat.) "at, by"; **θύρῃσι** (noun, dat. pl. fem.) "doors, gates." The Trojan elders were holding assemblies at the gates of Priam's palace, a traditional place for council meetings in Homer.

lines.original: πάντες ὁμηγερέες ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες·
lines.english: all assembled together both young men and old
lines.gloss:
**πάντες** (πᾶς): nominative plural masculine adjective, "all" — modifies the assembled Trojans.

**ὁμηγερέες** (ὁμηγερής): nominative plural masculine adjective, "gathered together, assembled" — describes the collective assembly.

**ἠμὲν ... ἠδὲ**: correlative conjunctions, "both ... and" — linking the two age groups.

**νέοι** (νέος): nominative plural masculine adjective, "young men."

**γέροντες** (γέρων): nominative plural masculine noun, "old men, elders." 

The line emphasizes the universality of the gathering at Priam's doors, encompassing all Trojans regardless of age.

lines.original: ἀγχοῦ δʼ ἱσταμένη προσέφη πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις·
lines.english: Swift-footed Iris stood near them and spoke.
lines.gloss:
**ἀγχοῦ** (adv.): "near, close by" — indicating Iris's proximity to the assembly.

**ἱσταμένη** (pres. mid. participle, nom. sg. fem. from ἵστημι): "standing" or "having taken her stand" — modifying Iris.

**προσέφη** (3rd sg. aor. indic. act. from προσφημί): "addressed, spoke to" — the main verb.

**πόδας ὠκέα** (acc. sg. fem. phrase): "swift-footed" — traditional epithet modifying **Ἶρις** (nom. sg. fem.), the messenger goddess who is the subject of the sentence.

Iris, standing nearby, addressed the assembly in swift-footed manner (or: swift-footed Iris addressed them).

lines.original: εἴσατο δὲ φθογγὴν υἷϊ Πριάμοιο Πολίτῃ,
lines.english: She likened her voice to that of Priam's son Polites.
lines.gloss: **εἴσατο** (verb, 3rd sg. aorist middle indicative of *εἴδομαι*) "made herself like" or "took the form of"; **φθογγὴν** (noun, accusative singular feminine) "voice, speech"; **υἷϊ** (noun, dative singular masculine) "to the son"; **Πριάμοιο** (proper noun, genitive singular) "of Priam"; **Πολίτῃ** (proper noun, dative singular) "to Polites." Iris assumes the voice of Polites, son of Priam, as part of her disguise.

lines.original: ὃς Τρώων σκοπὸς ἷζε ποδωκείῃσι πεποιθὼς
lines.english: who sat as a Trojan lookout trusting in his swift feet
lines.gloss:
**Gloss for Iliad 2.793:**

ὃς (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.) "who"; σκοπὸς (noun, nom. sg.) "lookout, watchman"; ἷζε (imperfect, 3rd sg. of ἵζω) "was sitting"; ποδωκείῃσι (noun, dat. pl. from ποδωκείη) "in/by swiftness of foot"; πεποιθὼς (perfect participle, nom. sg. masc. of πείθω) "trusting, relying on." Polites served as the Trojans' sentinel, stationed on the tomb, confident in his speed as a runner.

lines.original: τύμβῳ ἐπʼ ἀκροτάτῳ Αἰσυήταο γέροντος,
lines.english: on the topmost mound of ancient Aesyetes
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** τύμβῳ (dat. sg. masc. noun) "on the burial mound"; ἀκροτάτῳ (superlative adj. dat. sg.) "topmost, highest"; Αἰσυήταο (gen. sg. proper name) "of Aesyetes"; γέροντος (gen. sg. masc. noun/adj.) "old man, elder."

Polites sits as lookout on the topmost part of the tomb-mound of old Aesyetes, a conspicuous landmark overlooking the Greek ships.

lines.original: δέγμενος ὁππότε ναῦφιν ἀφορμηθεῖεν Ἀχαιοί·
lines.english: watching for when the Achaeans would set forth with their ships
lines.gloss: **δέγμενος** (δέχομαι, present middle participle, nominative singular masculine) "waiting" or "watching for"; **ὁππότε** (conjunction) "for when" or "until"; **ναῦφιν** (ναῦς, dative plural, Aeolic form) "from the ships"; **ἀφορμηθεῖεν** (ἀφορμάω, aorist optative, 3rd plural) "would set forth" or "would rush out"; **Ἀχαιοί** (nominative plural) "the Achaeans." The line describes someone positioned as a lookout, watching to see when the Achaeans would launch an attack from their ships.

lines.original: τῷ μιν ἐεισαμένη προσέφη πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις·
lines.english: Looking like him swift-footed Iris addressed him.
lines.gloss:
**Iliad** - Target line gloss:

**τῷ** (demonstrative pronoun, dative singular masculine) "to him/in that form"; **ἐεισαμένη** (aorist middle participle, nominative singular feminine, from *εἴδομαι*) "having likened herself, disguising herself as"; **προσέφη** (3rd singular aorist middle indicative, from *προσφημί*) "addressed, spoke to"; **πόδας ὠκέα** (accusative of respect with epithet) "swift-footed"; **Ἶρις** (nominative singular) "Iris." Iris, disguising herself as him (Polites), addressed Hector with the epithet "swift-footed."

lines.original: ὣς ἔφαθʼ, Ἕκτωρ δʼ οὔ τι θεᾶς ἔπος ἠγνοίησεν,
lines.english: Thus she spoke, and Hector in no way failed to recognize the goddess's word.
lines.gloss:
**ὣς ἔφαθʼ, Ἕκτωρ δʼ οὔ τι θεᾶς ἔπος ἠγνοίησεν**

Key words: **ἔφαθʼ** (ἔφατο, 3rd sg. aor. mid. indic. of φημί, "spoke"); **Ἕκτωρ** (nom. sg., "Hector"); **ἠγνοίησεν** (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of ἀγνοέω, "failed to recognize/disregard"); **θεᾶς** (gen. sg. of θεά, "of the goddess"); **ἔπος** (acc. sg., "word/speech"). Thus she spoke, and Hector did not at all disregard

lines.original: αἶψα δʼ ἔλυσʼ ἀγορήν· ἐπὶ τεύχεα δʼ ἐσσεύοντο·
lines.english: He swiftly dismissed the assembly and they rushed to their arms.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** αἶψα (adverb) "swiftly, immediately"; ἔλυσε(ν) (3rd sg. aor. act. indic. of λύω) "he dissolved, dismissed"; ἀγορήν (acc. sg. fem. noun) "assembly"; τεύχεα (acc. pl. neut. noun) "armor, arms"; ἐσσεύοντο (3rd pl. impf. mid. indic. of σεύω) "they rushed toward."

Hector immediately dismissed the assembly, and the warriors rushed to their arms.

lines.original: πᾶσαι δʼ ὠΐγνυντο πύλαι, ἐκ δʼ ἔσσυτο λαὸς
lines.english: All the gates were opened wide, and the host poured out.
lines.gloss: **πᾶσαι** (πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν): nom. fem. pl., "all" - the gates collectively opened. **ὠΐγνυντο** (οἴγνυμι): 3rd pl. impf. mid.-pass., "were being opened." **πύλαι** (πύλη, -ης, ἡ): nom. fem. pl., "gates." **ἔσσυτο** (σεύω): 3rd sg. aor. mid., "rushed out." **λαὸς** (λαός, -οῦ, ὁ): nom. masc. sg., "the people/army." The gates all swung open and the host poured forth, with the singular collective λαὸς taking a singular verb despite the mass movement.

lines.original: πεζοί θʼ ἱππῆές τε· πολὺς δʼ ὀρυμαγδὸς ὀρώρει.
lines.english: Foot soldiers and horsemen, and a great tumult arose.
lines.gloss:
**πεζοί θʼ ἱππῆές τε· πολὺς δʼ ὀρυμαγδὸς ὀρώρει.**

*πεζοί* (nom. pl. masc., πεζός): "footmen," infantry; *ἱππῆές* (nom. pl. masc., ἱππεύς): "horsemen," cavalry; *πολὺς* (nom. sg. masc., πολύς): "great," "loud"; *ὀρυμαγδός* (nom. sg. masc.): "din," "tumult," "clamor"; *ὀρώρει* (3rd sg. plupf. act., ὄρνυμι): "had arisen," "rose up." The Trojan army pours forth, both foot-soldiers and cavalry,

lines.original: ἔστι δέ τις προπάροιθε πόλιος αἰπεῖα κολώνη
lines.english: There is a steep hill before the city
lines.gloss:
**ἔστι** (3rd sg. pres. indic. of εἰμί) "there is"; **προπάροιθε** (adv./prep. + gen.) "before, in front of"; **πόλιος** (gen. sg. of πόλις) "of the city"; **αἰπεῖα** (nom. sg. fem. adj.) "steep, sheer"; **κολώνη** (nom. sg. fem.) "hill, mound."

There is a certain steep hill in front of the city, describing a strategic topographical feature in the plain.

lines.original: ἐν πεδίῳ ἀπάνευθε περίδρομος ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα,
lines.english: in the plain apart, with room to run around on this side and that
lines.gloss:
**ἐν πεδίῳ ἀπάνευθε περίδρομος ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα**

**ἐν** (prep. + dat.): "in" or "on"
**πεδίῳ** (noun, dat. sg. neut.): "the plain"
**ἀπάνευθε** (adv.): "apart," "away from" (the city)
**περίδρομος** (adj., nom. sg. fem.): "accessible all around," "with running-space around it"
**ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα** (adv. phrase): "on this side and that," "on both sides"

This line describes a hill standing isolated on the plain, accessible or with clear space all around it on every side.

lines.original: τὴν ἤτοι ἄνδρες Βατίειαν κικλήσκουσιν,
lines.english: This men call Batieia, but the immortals call it the barrow of bounding Myrine.
lines.gloss:
**τὴν ἤτοι ἄνδρες Βατίειαν κικλήσκουσιν**

**τήν** (demonstrative pronoun, acc. fem. sing.) "this [mound]" — refers back to the hill mentioned previously; **ἤτοι** (particle) "indeed, truly" — emphatic marker; **ἄνδρες** (noun, nom. masc. pl.) "men" — mortals in contrast to gods; **Βατίειαν** (proper noun, acc. fem. sing.) "Batieia" — the mortal name for the mound; **κικλήσκουσιν** (verb, 3rd pl. pres. act. indic.) "they call" — iterative/customary present. Men call this mound "Batieia," contrasting mortal nomenclature with the divine name in the

lines.original: ἀθάνατοι δέ τε σῆμα πολυσκάρθμοιο Μυρίνης·
lines.english: but the immortals call it the barrow of bounding Myrine
lines.gloss: **ἀθάνατοι** (nom. pl. masc., "immortals"/"gods") contrasts with **ἄνδρες** in the previous line. **σῆμα** (acc. sg. neut., "tomb"/"grave marker") identifies what the gods call it. **πολυσκάρθμοιο** (gen. sg. fem., "much-leaping"/"dancing") and **Μυρίνης** (gen. sg. fem., "Myrina") specify whose tomb: the Amazon warrior Myrina. The line presents the divine versus mortal nomenclature for the landmark.

lines.original: ἔνθα τότε Τρῶές τε διέκριθεν ἠδʼ ἐπίκουροι.
lines.english: There the Trojans and their allies were marshaled in their divisions.
lines.gloss:
**ἔνθα** (adverb): "there," referring to the location previously described (the hill/tomb of Myrine).

**διέκριθεν** (3rd pl. aorist passive indicative of διακρίνω): "they were divided" or "they separated themselves," describing the marshaling of troops into contingents.

**ἠδέ** (conjunction): "and," connecting Τρῶές and ἐπίκουροι.

**ἐπίκουροι** (nominative plural masculine): "allies" or "auxiliaries," the non-Trojan allied forces.
