**τοσσαῦτα** (demonstrative adjective, neuter accusative plural): "so many" - modifying ἔτεα, correlating with the nine years just mentioned.

**ἔτεα** (noun, neuter accusative plural): "years" - direct object indicating duration.

**πτολεμίξομεν** (verb, 1st plural future indicative): "we shall wage war" - from πτολεμίζω, indicating future military action.

The line means: "Thus we shall wage war here for so many years," connecting the prophecy of nine years' duration to the siege of Troy.

lines.original: τῷ δεκάτῳ δὲ πόλιν αἱρήσομεν εὐρυάγυιαν.
lines.english: and in the tenth year we shall take the wide-wayed city.
lines.gloss: **τῷ δεκάτῳ** (δέκατος, -η, -ον): dative singular masculine/neuter adjective, "in the tenth (year)," agreeing with an understood ἔτει. **πόλιν** (πόλις, -εως, ἡ): accusative singular feminine noun, "the city," direct object of αἱρήσομεν. **αἱρήσομεν** (αἱρέω): first person plural future active indicative, "we will take/capture." **εὐρυάγυιαν** (εὐρυάγυια, -ης, ἡ): accusative singular feminine adjective, "broad-streeted/with wide streets," modifying πόλιν.

lines.original: ὦ πόποι ἦ δὴ παισὶν ἐοικότες ἀγοράασθε
lines.english: Good heavens, you are holding council like children.
lines.gloss: **ὦ πόποι** (interjection): exclamation of dismay or reproach, "alas" or "oh my." **ἦ** (particle): "truly" or "indeed," emphasizing the statement. **παισὶν** (noun, dative plural of παῖς): "children" or "boys," dative of comparison with ἐοικότες. **ἐοικότες** (perfect active participle, nominative plural of ἔοικα): "being like" or "resembling." **ἀγοράασθε** (verb, 2nd person plural present middle indicative of ἀγοράομαι): "you gather" or "you hold assembly." The line reproaches the assembled men for conducting their debate like children.

lines.original: νηπιάχοις οἷς οὔ τι μέλει πολεμήϊα ἔργα.
lines.english: like foolish children who have no concern for the works of war
lines.gloss:
**νηπιάχοις** (dat. pl. masc., νηπίαχος): "childish ones, infants" – dative of comparison or reference, emphasizing immaturity.

**οἷς** (dat. pl. relative pronoun): "to whom" – introduces relative clause.

**μέλει** (3rd sg. pres., μέλω): "it is a care, it matters" – impersonal verb governing genitive (πολεμήϊα ἔργα).

**πολεμήϊα ἔργα** (nom./acc. pl. neut., πολεμήϊος + ἔργον): "warlike deeds, martial works" – subject of μέλει in the sense "for whom warlike deeds are no concern."

The line condemns the Greeks as childish, to whom war matters not at all.

lines.original: πῇ δὴ συνθεσίαι τε καὶ ὅρκια βήσεται ἥμιν;
lines.english: Where then shall our compacts and oaths go for us?
lines.gloss: **πῇ** (interrogative adverb) "where? whither?"; **συνθεσίαι** (nominative plural, feminine noun from σύνθεσις) "compacts, covenants"; **ὅρκια** (nominative plural, neuter noun from ὅρκιον) "oaths, sworn pledges"; **βήσεται** (3rd singular future middle, from βαίνω) "will go, will come to pass"; **ἥμιν** (dative 1st person plural pronoun) "for us, to us." The speaker questions where their covenants and sworn oaths will end up, implying their dissolution or nullification.

lines.original: ἐν πυρὶ δὴ βουλαί τε γενοίατο μήδεά τʼ ἀνδρῶν
lines.english: Let our plans and counsels of men go up in fire then.
lines.gloss: **ἐν πυρὶ** (prep. + dat.): "in fire" — idiomatic for destruction or futility. **βουλαί** (nom. pl., βουλή): "counsels, plans." **γενοίατο** (3rd pl. aor. opt. mid., γίγνομαι): "may they come to be, may they end up" — optative expressing a wish or potential consequence. **μήδεά** (nom. pl., μῆδος): "plans, designs." The line laments that all plans and counsels of men may come to nothing (literally "end up in fire") if oaths are broken.

lines.original: σπονδαί τʼ ἄκρητοι καὶ δεξιαί, ᾗς ἐπέπιθμεν·
lines.english: Let our libations unmixed and our pledges in which we trusted perish in the fire.
lines.gloss:
**σπονδαί** (nom. pl. fem. of σπονδή): "libations, treaty-oaths"; **ἄκρητοι** (nom. pl. fem. of ἄκρητος, -ον): "unmixed (with water), pure"; **δεξιαί** (nom. pl. fem. of δεξιά): "right hands, pledges"; **ἐπέπιθμεν** (1st pl. plpf. mid. of πείθω): "we trusted in, relied upon." 

The line lists what would be destroyed in fire: the libations of unmixed wine and the clasping of right hands in which the Greeks had placed their trust when making their treaty with the Trojans.

lines.original: αὔτως γὰρ ἐπέεσσʼ ἐριδαίνομεν, οὐδέ τι μῆχος
lines.english: For thus we wrangle with words, nor can we find any device.
lines.gloss:
**αὔτως** (adverb): "in vain, fruitlessly, to no purpose" — modifies the manner of their quarreling.

**ἐπέεσσ(ι)** (noun, dative plural of ἔπος): "with words, in words" — dative of means, indicating the instrument of their dispute.

**ἐριδαίνομεν** (verb, 1st plural present indicative of ἐριδαίνω): "we quarrel, we wrangle" — the main verb describing their ongoing contentious debate.

**μῆχος** (noun, nominative/accusative singular neuter of μῆχος): "means, remedy, device" — the object they fail to find, with **οὐδέ τι** ("not any") negating it.

The line conveys their futile quarreling in words without finding any solution or means forward

lines.original: εὑρέμεναι δυνάμεσθα, πολὺν χρόνον ἐνθάδʼ ἐόντες.
lines.english: We cannot find any solution, though we have been here a long time.
lines.gloss: **εὑρέμεναι** (aorist infinitive, active, from εὑρίσκω) "to find"; **δυνάμεσθα** (1st plural present middle/passive indicative from δύναμαι) "we are able"; **πολὺν χρόνον** (accusative of duration of time) "for a long time"; **ἐνθάδʼ** (adverb) "here"; **ἐόντες** (nominative plural masculine present participle from εἰμί) "being." The line expresses their inability to find any solution despite being here for a long time.

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδη σὺ δʼ ἔθʼ ὡς πρὶν ἔχων ἀστεμφέα βουλὴν
lines.english: Son of Atreus, do you still hold fast to your unshaken purpose as before
lines.gloss: **Ἀτρεΐδη** (vocative singular, "son of Atreus") addresses Agamemnon directly. **σὺ δʼ** (nominative singular pronoun + particle, "and you") emphasizes the subject. **ἔχων** (present active participle, nominative masculine singular, "holding/keeping") governs **ἀστεμφέα βουλήν** (accusative singular, "unwavering counsel/purpose"). **ὡς πρίν** ("as before") indicates continuity of steadfast leadership.

lines.original: ἄρχευʼ Ἀργείοισι κατὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας,
lines.english: Lead the Argives through the mighty battles.
lines.gloss:
**ἄρχευʼ** (ἄρχευε, 2nd sg. pres. impv. act. of ἀρχεύω): "be leader, command" (with dative)
**Ἀργείοισι** (dat. pl. masc. of Ἀργεῖος): "to/for the Argives"
**κατὰ** (prep. + acc.): "throughout, in"
**κρατερὰς** (acc. pl. fem. of κρατερός): "mighty, violent"
**ὑσμίνας** (acc. pl. fem. of ὑσμίνη): "battles, combats"

The verse commands Agamemnon to continue leading the Argives through mighty battles.

lines.original: τούσδε δʼ ἔα φθινύθειν ἕνα καὶ δύο, τοί κεν Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: Let these one or two of the Achaeans waste away who would
lines.gloss: **τούσδε** (pronoun, acc. pl. masc. of ὅδε): "these (men)," i.e., the quarreling Greek leaders. **φθινύθειν** (verb, pres. inf. of φθινύθω): "waste away, perish." **ἕνα καὶ δύο** (numerals, acc.): "one and two," i.e., "both" or "the pair." **τοί** (particle): "who (indeed)," relative/demonstrative introducing a characterizing clause. Zeus tells Athena to let these two (Agamemnon and Achilles) waste away, who among the Achaeans [are causing strife].

lines.original: νόσφιν βουλεύωσʼ· ἄνυσις δʼ οὐκ ἔσσεται αὐτῶν·
lines.english: Let them plan apart, but there will be no accomplishment for them.
lines.gloss: **νόσφιν** (adverb): "apart, separately" — governs the participle, indicating isolated action. **βουλεύωσι** (3rd pl. pres. subj. act. of βουλεύω): "they deliberate, make plans" — jussive subjunctive in indirect discourse. **ἄνυσις** (nom. sg. fem. noun): "accomplishment, fulfillment" — subject of ἔσσεται. **ἔσσεται** (3rd sg. fut. mid. of εἰμί): "will be" — predicting the outcome. The line warns that whatever few Achaeans plot apart will achieve no fulfillment.

lines.original: πρὶν Ἄργος δʼ ἰέναι πρὶν καὶ Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο
lines.english: before going to Argos and before knowing Zeus the aegis-bearer's will
lines.gloss: **πρὶν** (adverb): "before" (governing the following infinitives). **Ἄργος** (noun, accusative singular neuter): "Argos" (object of *ἰέναι*). **ἰέναι** (verb, present infinitive): "to go." **Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο** (noun phrase, genitive singular masculine): "of aegis-bearing Zeus" (epithet modifying Zeus). The line states they should not return to Argos before determining whether Zeus's promise is false or true.

lines.original: γνώμεναι εἴ τε ψεῦδος ὑπόσχεσις εἴ τε καὶ οὐκί.
lines.english: learning whether his promise is false or true.
lines.gloss: **γνώμεναι** (aorist infinitive, from γιγνώσκω) "to know, ascertain"; **ψεῦδος** (nominative neuter singular noun) "falsehood, lie"; **ὑπόσχεσις** (nominative feminine singular noun) "promise, undertaking"; **εἴ τε ... εἴ τε** (correlative conjunctions) "whether ... or"; **οὐκί** (negative particle) "not." The line presents an indirect question to determine whether the promise is false or not.

lines.original: φημὶ γὰρ οὖν κατανεῦσαι ὑπερμενέα Κρονίωνα
lines.english: For I say that the mighty son of Kronos nodded his assent.
lines.gloss:
**φημί** (1st sg. pres. act. indic.) "I declare/assert"; **κατανεῦσαι** (aor. act. infin. of κατανεύω) "to nod assent"; **ὑπερμενέα** (acc. sg. masc. of ὑπερμενής) "exceedingly mighty"; **Κρονίωνα** (acc. sg. of Κρονίων) "son of Kronos" (Zeus). 

Thetis asserts that Zeus nodded in assent to her petition, employing the verb **φημί** with infinitive construction to emphasize the certainty of the divine promise.

lines.original: ἤματι τῷ ὅτε νηυσὶν ἐν ὠκυπόροισιν ἔβαινον
lines.english: on the day when the Argives embarked in their swift-faring ships
lines.gloss: **ἤματι** (dat. sg. neut. of ἦμαρ) "on the day"; **τῷ** (dat. sg. neut. of ὁ, demonstrative/relative) "that" or "on which"; **ὅτε** (temporal conjunction) "when"; **νηυσὶν** (dat. pl. of ναῦς) "the ships"; **ὠκυπόροισιν** (dat. pl. fem./masc. of ὠκύπορος) "swift-faring"; **ἔβαινον** (3rd pl. impf. of βαίνω) "they embarked/went." The line refers to the day when the Achaeans boarded their swift ships, setting the temporal context for Zeus's prophesied nod.

lines.original: Ἀργεῖοι Τρώεσσι φόνον καὶ κῆρα φέροντες
lines.english: The Argives bringing slaughter and death to the Trojans
lines.gloss:
**Ἀργεῖοι Τρώεσσι φόνον καὶ κῆρα φέροντες**

**Ἀργεῖοι** (nom. pl. masc., "Argives"): the Greeks. **Τρώεσσι** (dat. pl. masc., "for/to the Trojans"): dative of disadvantage. **φόνον** (acc. sg. masc., "slaughter") and **κῆρα** (acc. sg. fem., "death/doom"): objects of φέροντες. **φέροντες** (nom. pl. masc. pres. part., "bringing/bearing"): the Argives bring slaughter and death to the Trojans.

lines.original: ἀστράπτων ἐπιδέξιʼ ἐναίσιμα σήματα φαίνων.
lines.english: Lightning on the right and showing favorable signs.
lines.gloss: **ἀστράπτων** (pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. masc., ἀστράπτω) "flashing lightning"; **ἐπιδέξιʼ** (adv., ἐπιδέξια) "on the right" (with elision); **ἐναίσιμα** (adj. acc. pl. neut., ἐναίσιμος) "favorable, propitious"; **σήματα** (noun acc. pl. neut., σῆμα) "signs, portents"; **φαίνων** (pres. act. ptcp. nom. sg. masc., φαίνω) "showing, displaying." Zeus sends lightning on the right, displaying favorable omens to encourage the Argives against the Trojans.

lines.original: τὼ μή τις πρὶν ἐπειγέσθω οἶκον δὲ νέεσθαι
lines.english: Let no one be eager to return home yet
lines.gloss:
**τὼ** (adverb): "therefore," "for that reason" – inferential particle drawing conclusion from Zeus's favorable sign.

**πρίν** (adverb/conjunction): "before," "until" – temporal marker indicating the condition that must be met first.

**ἐπειγέσθω** (verb): 3rd person singular present middle/passive imperative of ἐπείγω, "let him hasten" – jussive imperative forbidding premature departure.

**οἶκον δὲ νέεσθαι** (noun + particle + infinitive): "to return homeward" – οἶκον (accusative of direction) with νέεσθαι (present middle infinitive of νέομαι), completing the prohibition against going home before fulfilling the condition stated in the next line.

lines.original: πρίν τινα πὰρ Τρώων ἀλόχῳ κατακοιμηθῆναι,
lines.english: before each man has lain with a Trojan's wife
lines.gloss: **πρίν** (adv.) "before"; **τινα** (indef. pron., acc. sg. masc.) "some (man)," object of κατακοιμηθῆναι; **Τρώων** (noun, gen. pl.) "of the Trojans," partitive genitive; **ἀλόχῳ** (noun, dat. sg. fem.) "with the wife," dative of accompaniment; **κατακοιμηθῆναι** (aor. inf. pass.) "to sleep with," complementing the prohibition. The line forbids Greeks from hastening home before sleeping with some Trojan's wife, part of Agamemnon's exhortation for vengeance.

lines.original: τίσασθαι δʼ Ἑλένης ὁρμήματά τε στοναχάς τε.
lines.english: and to avenge the strivings and groans of Helen.
lines.gloss: **τίσασθαι** (aorist middle infinitive of τίνω) "to exact vengeance for" governs **Ἑλένης** (genitive of Ἑλένη) "Helen's" (objective genitive). **ὁρμήματά** (neuter accusative plural of ὅρμημα) "impulses, provocations" and **στοναχάς** (accusative plural of στοναχή) "groanings, lamentations" are coordinated objects connected by **τε...τε** "both...and." The infinitive continues the purpose clause: the Greeks must avenge both Helen's abduction and the sufferings it caused before anyone returns home.

lines.original: εἰ δέ τις ἐκπάγλως ἐθέλει οἶκον δὲ νέεσθαι
lines.english: But if anyone is exceedingly eager to return home
lines.gloss: **εἰ δέ τις** (if anyone): conditional particle with indefinite pronoun nominative singular. **ἐκπάγλως** (exceedingly, excessively): adverb intensifying the desire. **ἐθέλει** (wishes): 3rd singular present active indicative of ἐθέλω. **οἶκον δὲ νέεσθαι** (to return homeward): accusative of goal with present middle infinitive of νέομαι (return). The line introduces a conditional warning about anyone who desires too eagerly to go home.

lines.original: ἁπτέσθω ἧς νηὸς ἐϋσσέλμοιο μελαίνης,
lines.english: Let him lay hands on his well-benched black ship
lines.gloss:
**ἁπτέσθω** (3rd sg. pres. mid. impv. of ἅπτω): "let him lay hold of, touch" — a command construction. **ἧς** (fem. gen. sg. of ὅς): possessive pronoun "his own." **νηὸς** (gen. sg. of ναῦς): "ship," governed by ἁπτέσθω. **ἐϋσσέλμοιο** (gen. sg. of ἐΰσσελμος): compound epithet "well-benched." **μελαίνης** (fem. gen. sg. of μέλας): "black," standard Homeric ship epithet. 

Agamemnon warns that whoever excessively desires to return home should grasp his own well-benched black ship, so that he may meet death and doom before the others

lines.original: ὄφρα πρόσθʼ ἄλλων θάνατον καὶ πότμον ἐπίσπῃ.
lines.english: so that before the others he may draw death and destruction upon himself.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ὄφρα (conjunction) "so that, in order that"; πρόσθʼ (adverb, elided πρόσθεν) "before, ahead of"; θάνατον (acc. sg. masculine noun) "death"; πότμον (acc. sg. masculine noun) "fate, doom"; ἐπίσπῃ (2nd sg. aorist subjunctive middle, ἐφέπω) "you may draw upon yourself, incur."

The line expresses a purpose clause: "so that you may draw death and doom upon yourself before the others," warning of the peril of seizing the ship first.

lines.original: ἀλλὰ ἄναξ αὐτός τʼ εὖ μήδεο πείθεό τʼ ἄλλῳ·
lines.english: But lord, take good counsel yourself and listen to another.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλά** (ἀλλά, conjunction): "but" — strong adversative introducing a contrasting exhortation.

**αὐτός** (αὐτός, intensive pronoun, nominative singular masculine): "yourself" — emphasizing the subject's personal responsibility.

**μήδεο** (μήδομαι, present middle imperative, 2nd singular): "devise, plan well" — the verb governs strategic thought, here with adverb **εὖ** ("well").

**πείθεο** (πείθομαι, present middle imperative, 2nd singular): "obey, be persuaded by" — governing the dative **ἄλλῳ** ("another").

The speaker urges the addressee both to plan wisely himself and to heed others' counsel.

lines.original: οὔ τοι ἀπόβλητον ἔπος ἔσσεται ὅττί κεν εἴπω·
lines.english: The word I speak to you will not be cast aside.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἀπόβλητον (adjective, nominative neuter singular) "thrown away, fruitless, in vain"; ἔπος (noun, nominative neuter singular) "word, speech"; ἔσσεται (future middle indicative, 3rd singular of εἰμί) "will be"; ὅττί κεν εἴπω (relative clause with modal particle) "whatever I may say."

The line means "the word will not be fruitless/in vain, whatever I may say"—a solemn assurance that the speaker's advice will prove valuable.

lines.original: κρῖνʼ ἄνδρας κατὰ φῦλα κατὰ φρήτρας Ἀγάμεμνον,
lines.english: Divide the men by tribes and by clans, Agamemnon.
lines.gloss: **κρῖνον** (κρίνω): 2nd sg. aorist imperative active, "marshal, separate, organize." **φῦλα** (φῦλον): acc. pl. neuter, "tribes" (administrative divisions). **φρήτρας** (φρήτρη/φρήτρα): acc. pl. feminine, "phratries, clans" (kinship groups within tribes). Agamemnon is urged to organize his troops by tribal and clan divisions so that units of kinsmen will fight together and support one another.

lines.original: ὡς φρήτρη φρήτρηφιν ἀρήγῃ, φῦλα δὲ φύλοις.
lines.english: So that clan may help clan and tribe help tribe.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** φρήτρη (nom. sg. fem.) "phratry/clan"; ἀρήγῃ (3rd sg. pres. subj. act. of ἀρήγω) "may aid, help"; φῦλα (nom. pl. neut.) "tribes"; φύλοις (dat. pl. neut.) "to/for tribes."

Nestor advises organizing troops by kinship groups so that "phratry may aid phratry, and tribes [aid] tribes," with the datives φρήτρηφιν and φύλοις expressing mutual support among these social divisions.

lines.original: εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἕρξῃς καί τοι πείθωνται Ἀχαιοί,
lines.english: If you do this and the Achaeans obey you
lines.gloss:
**εἰ δέ κεν ὣς ἕρξῃς καί τοι πείθωνται Ἀχαιοί**

**εἰ** (conjunction): if, introducing a future-more-vivid condition. **κεν** (particle): modal particle (= ἄν) with subjunctive in protasis. **ἕρξῃς** (2nd sg. aor. subj. act. of ῥέζω/ἔρδω): "you should do/act," referring to Agamemnon organizing troops by tribes and clans. **πείθωνται** (3rd pl. pres. subj. mid. of πείθω): "they obey," the Achaeans submitting to his command. **Ἀχαιοί** (nom. pl. masc.): "the Achaeans

lines.original: γνώσῃ ἔπειθʼ ὅς θʼ ἡγεμόνων κακὸς ὅς τέ νυ λαῶν
lines.english: Then you will know which of the leaders is cowardly and which of the men.
lines.gloss:
**γνώσῃ** (verb, 2nd sg. future middle indicative of γιγνώσκω): "you will know/recognize." **ἡγεμόνων** (noun, genitive plural of ἡγεμών): "of the leaders/commanders." **κακός** (adjective, nominative singular masculine): "cowardly/base/bad." **λαῶν** (noun, genitive plural of λαός): "of the people/troops."

"Then you will recognize which of the leaders is cowardly and which of the troops," establishing the purpose of the proposed test to distinguish brave from cowardly fighters at all ranks.

lines.original: ἠδʼ ὅς κʼ ἐσθλὸς ἔῃσι· κατὰ σφέας γὰρ μαχέονται.
lines.english: and who is brave, for they will fight according to their ranks.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** ἠδέ (conj.) "and, or"; ἐσθλός (adj. nom. sg. masc.) "good, brave"; ἔῃσι (pres. subj. 3rd sg. of εἰμί) "may be"; κατὰ σφέας (prep. + acc. pronoun) "according to themselves, each for himself"; μαχέονται (pres. mid./pass. 3rd pl. of μάχομαι) "they fight."

Agamemnon continues that he will recognize who among the leaders and men is brave, since they will fight "according to themselves" (i.e., individually or each man showing his true mettle in battle).

lines.original: γνώσεαι δʼ εἰ καὶ θεσπεσίῃ πόλιν οὐκ ἀλαπάξεις,
lines.english: You will know whether it is by divine fate that you fail to sack the city.
lines.gloss: **γνώσεαι** (γιγνώσκω): 2nd sg. future middle indicative, "you will know/learn." **θεσπεσίῃ** (θεσπέσιος): dat. sg. fem., "by divine ordinance/god-sent fate." **πόλιν** (πόλις): acc. sg., "city," object of ἀλαπάξεις. **ἀλαπάξεις** (ἀλαπάζω): 2nd sg. future active indicative, "you will sack/destroy." Agamemnon tells the seer he will learn whether it is by divine will that the Greeks cannot sack the city, or by human failings in war.

lines.original: ἦ ἀνδρῶν κακότητι καὶ ἀφραδίῃ πολέμοιο.
lines.english: or through the cowardice of men and their ignorance in war.
lines.gloss: **ἦ** (particle): "or" introducing an alternative question. **ἀνδρῶν** (noun, gen. pl. of ἀνήρ): "of men," genitive of source/cause. **κακότητι** (noun, dat. sg. of κακότης): "because of cowardice/badness," dative of cause. **ἀφραδίῃ** (noun, dat. sg. of ἀφραδίη): "because of folly/thoughtlessness," paired with κακότητι. **πολέμοιο** (noun, gen. sg. of πόλεμος): "of war," objective genitive with ἀφραδίῃ. The line asks whether failure to sack Troy results from the troops' cowardice and tactical foolishness in battle rather than divine protection.

lines.original: ἦ μὰν αὖτʼ ἀγορῇ νικᾷς γέρον υἷας Ἀχαιῶν.
lines.english: Indeed old man, you prevail over the sons of the Achaeans in assembly.
lines.gloss: **ἦ** (particle): asseverative, "truly, indeed"; **μάν** (particle): strengthening/affirmative, "certainly"; **ἀγορῇ** (noun, dative singular from ἀγορή): "in assembly/speech-making"; **νικᾷς** (verb, 2nd singular present indicative from νικάω): "you conquer, surpass"; **γέρον** (noun, vocative singular from γέρων): "old man." The speaker concedes that the old man surpasses the sons of the Achaeans in assembly/oratory, with emphatic particles (ἦ μάν, αὖτε) reinforcing the acknowledgment.

lines.original: αἲ γὰρ Ζεῦ τε πάτερ καὶ Ἀθηναίη καὶ Ἄπολλον
lines.english: O Father Zeus and Athena and Apollo
lines.gloss: **αἲ γάρ** (particle + particle): "would that, if only" — expressive wish construction. **Ζεῦ** (nom. masc. sg., voc.): vocative of Zeus, "O Zeus." **πάτερ** (nom. masc. sg., voc.): "father," in apposition to Zeus. **Ἀθηναίη** (nom. fem. sg., voc.): vocative of Athena. **Ἄπολλον** (nom. masc. sg., voc.): vocative of Apollo. The speaker calls upon the three principal gods in a wish formula, introducing a prayer for assistance.

lines.original: τοιοῦτοι δέκα μοι συμφράδμονες εἶεν Ἀχαιῶν·
lines.english: If only ten such counselors among the Achaeans were mine.
lines.gloss:
**τοιοῦτοι** (toioûtoi): demonstrative adjective, nominative plural masculine, "such (men), of such a kind"

**δέκα** (déka): indeclinable numeral, "ten"

**συμφράδμονες** (sumphádmones): noun, nominative plural masculine, "counselors, advisers" (from συμ- "together" + φράδμων "one who plans")

**εἶεν** (eîen): optative, 3rd plural of εἰμί, "might be, would be" (expressing a wish)

Agamemnon wishes that ten such counselors among the Achaeans might be his, continuing his praise of Nestor's strategic wisdom.

lines.original: τώ κε τάχʼ ἠμύσειε πόλις Πριάμοιο ἄνακτος
lines.english: Then would the city of lord Priam soon be taken.
lines.gloss: **τώ** (adverb, "then," "therefore") introduces the apodosis. **κε** (modal particle) with **ἠμύσειε** (3rd sing. aorist optative middle of ἀμύω, "would be sacked/taken") forms a potential optative construction. **πόλις** (nominative singular, "city") is the subject. **Πριάμοιο ἄνακτος** (genitive singular, "of lord Priam") modifies πόλις. The line expresses a hypothetical consequence: "then would the city of lord Priam be taken."

lines.original: χερσὶν ὑφʼ ἡμετέρῃσιν ἁλοῦσά τε περθομένη τε.
lines.english: captured and sacked by our hands.
lines.gloss: **χερσίν** (dative plural of χείρ): "by the hands" – dative of agent with passive participles. **ὑφ'** (preposition + dative): "under, by" – reinforces instrumental sense. **ἡμετέρῃσιν** (dative plural feminine of ἡμέτερος): "our" – possessive adjective modifying χερσίν. **ἁλοῦσα** (aorist passive participle, feminine nominative singular of ἁλίσκομαι): "having been captured/taken." **περθομένη** (present passive participle, feminine nominative singular of πέρθω): "being sacked/destroyed" – both participles modify πόλις from the previous line, describing Troy's capture and destruction at Achaean hands.

lines.original: ἀλλά μοι αἰγίοχος Κρονίδης Ζεὺς ἄλγεʼ ἔδωκεν,
lines.english: But aegis-bearing Zeus the son of Kronos has given me sorrows.
lines.gloss:
**ἀλλά** (ἀλλά, conjunction): "but" – strong adversative marking a contrast with the previous thought.

**αἰγίοχος** (αἰγίοχος, -ον, nominative singular masculine adjective): "aegis-bearing" – standard Homeric epithet for Zeus.

**Κρονίδης** (Κρονίδης, -ου, nominative singular masculine): "son of Kronos" – patronymic identifying Zeus.

**ἄλγεʼ** (ἄλγος, -εος, accusative plural neuter): "griefs, pains" – object of ἔδωκεν.

**ἔδωκεν** (δίδωμι, 3rd singular aorist active indicative): "gave, has given" – main verb expressing Zeus's bestowal of suffering.

lines.original: ὅς με μετʼ ἀπρήκτους ἔριδας καὶ νείκεα βάλλει.
lines.english: who casts me into futile quarrels and strife
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** 
- **ὅς** (relative pronoun, nom. sg. masc.): "who" — refers back to Zeus
- **μετά** (preposition + acc.): "into" — direction into which something is cast
- **ἀπρήκτους** (adjective, acc. pl. fem.): "fruitless, profitless" — modifies ἔριδας
- **ἔριδας** (noun, acc. pl. fem.): "quarrels, disputes"
- **βάλλει** (verb, 3rd sg. pres. act. indic.): "casts, throws"

Zeus repeatedly casts the speaker into pointless quarrels and strife, emphasizing divine responsibility for human conflict.

lines.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼν Ἀχιλεύς τε μαχεσσάμεθʼ εἵνεκα κούρης
lines.english: For Achilles and I once quarreled over a girl.
lines.gloss:
**καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼν Ἀχιλεύς τε μαχεσσάμεθʼ εἵνεκα κούρης**

*ἐγών* (1st sg. nom. pronoun) "I"; *Ἀχιλεύς* (nom. sg.) "Achilles"; *μαχεσσάμεθα* (1st pl. aor. mid. indic. < μάχομαι) "we fought, quarreled"; *εἵνεκα* (prep. + gen.) "on account of, because of"; *κούρης* (gen. sg. < κούρη) "girl, maiden." The speaker recalls how he and Achilles quarreled over a girl (Briseis), establishing a precedent for the current dispute.

lines.original: ἀντιβίοις ἐπέεσσιν, ἐγὼ δʼ ἦρχον χαλεπαίνων·
lines.english: with opposing words, and I was the first to grow angry.
lines.gloss:
**ἀντιβίοις** (adj. dat. pl. masc./neut.): "hostile, opposing" - modifies ἐπέεσσιν. **ἐπέεσσιν** (noun dat. pl.): "with words, speeches" - dative of means. **ἦρχον** (verb 1st sg. imperf.): "I began, I was the first" - from ἄρχω. **χαλεπαίνων** (participle nom. sg. masc. pres.): "being angry, raging" - from χαλεπαίνω, modifying ἐγώ. 

The line means: "with hostile words, and I was the first to be angry."

lines.original: εἰ δέ ποτʼ ἔς γε μίαν βουλεύσομεν, οὐκέτʼ ἔπειτα
lines.english: But if ever we two should plan together in one accord, no longer then will there be delay of evil for the Trojans, not even a little.
lines.gloss: **εἰ** (conjunction): "if" — introducing a future condition. **μίαν** (fem. acc. sg. of εἷς, μία, ἕν): "one," modifying βουλήν (understood). **βουλεύσομεν** (1st pl. fut. indic. of βουλεύω): "we shall deliberate/plan together." **οὐκέτι** (adverb): "no longer," negating future action. **ἔπειτα** (adverb): "thereafter/afterwards." The line expresses a conditional hope: "But if ever we shall plan together as one, then no longer afterwards..." (implying Trojan plans will be thwarted).

lines.original: Τρωσὶν ἀνάβλησις κακοῦ ἔσσεται οὐδʼ ἠβαιόν.
lines.english: Then there will be no postponement of doom for the Trojans, not even a little.
lines.gloss: **Τρωσὶν** (dat. pl. of Τρῶες): "for the Trojans" — dative of disadvantage. **ἀνάβλησις** (nom. sg. fem.): "postponement, delay" — subject of the sentence. **κακοῦ** (gen. sg. neut. of κακός): "of evil" — objective genitive with ἀνάβλησις. **ἔσσεται** (3rd sg. fut. mid. of εἰμί): "will be." **ἠβαιόν** (adv.): "even a little bit, at all" — with the negative "not even slightly." The line means once the Greeks unite in counsel, there will be no postponement of disaster for the Trojans, not even a little.

lines.original: νῦν δʼ ἔρχεσθʼ ἐπὶ δεῖπνον ἵνα ξυνάγωμεν Ἄρηα.
lines.english: Now go to your meal so that we may join together in battle.
lines.gloss: **νῦν** (adverb): "now." **ἔρχεσθʼ(ε)** (2nd pl. pres. impv. mid., ἔρχομαι): "go, come!" **δεῖπνον** (acc. sg. neut. noun): "dinner, meal." **ξυνάγωμεν** (1st pl. aor. subj. act., ξυνάγω): "let us join, bring together" (purpose clause with ἵνα). **Ἄρηα** (acc. sg. masc., Ἄρης): "Ares," here metonymy for "battle, war." Agamemnon urges the Greeks to take their meal so they may join battle, with Ares representing the coming combat.

lines.original: εὖ μέν τις δόρυ θηξάσθω, εὖ δʼ ἀσπίδα θέσθω,
lines.english: Let each man sharpen well his spear and set well his shield.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** *θηξάσθω* (aorist middle imperative, 3rd sg. of θήγω) "let him sharpen"; *δόρυ* (nom./acc. neut. sg.) "spear"; *ἀσπίδα* (acc. fem. sg.) "shield"; *θέσθω* (aorist middle imperative, 3rd sg. of τίθημι) "let him set/prepare."

The anaphoric *εὖ* ("well") emphasizes thorough preparation: each warrior should sharpen his spear well and ready his shield well before the coming battle.

lines.original: εὖ δέ τις ἵπποισιν δεῖπνον δότω ὠκυπόδεσσιν,
lines.english: Let each man give fodder well to his swift-footed horses.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** εὖ (adverb) "well"; ἵπποισιν (dative plural of ἵππος) "to the horses"; δεῖπνον (accusative singular neuter noun) "meal, dinner"; δότω (3rd singular aorist imperative active of δίδωμι) "let him give"; ὠκυπόδεσσιν (dative plural adjective modifying ἵπποισιν) "swift-footed."

The line continues Agamemnon's exhortations for battle preparation, commanding that each warrior properly feed his swift horses before engaging in combat.

lines.original: εὖ δέ τις ἅρματος ἀμφὶς ἰδὼν πολέμοιο μεδέσθω,
lines.english: And let each man look well to his chariot and think of war.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** εὖ (adverb) "well, carefully"; ἅρματος (noun, genitive singular, neuter) "of chariot," from ἅρμα; ἀμφίς (adverb) "on both sides, around"; ἰδών (participle, aorist active nominative singular masculine) "having looked to," from ὁράω; μεδέσθω (verb, imperative present middle 3rd singular) "let him attend to, take thought for," from μέδομαι. 

Each man should look carefully around his chariot and attend to the business of war.

lines.original: ὥς κε πανημέριοι στυγερῷ κρινώμεθʼ Ἄρηϊ.
lines.english: So that all day long we may contend in hateful battle.
lines.gloss:
**ὥς** (adverb): "thus, in this way" – marks purpose/result of the previous exhortation.

**πανημέριοι** (adjective, nominative plural masculine): "all day long, for the whole day" – from πᾶν + ἡμέρα, describing the duration of battle.

**στυγερῷ** (adjective, dative singular masculine/neuter): "hateful, dreadful" – modifies Ἄρηϊ, emphasizing the grim nature of warfare.

**κρινώμεθʼ** (verb, 1st plural present middle subjunctive): "we may be separated/decided" – from κρίνω, here meaning "engage in battle," with Ἄρηϊ as dative of means.

**Ἄρηϊ** (noun, dative singular): "by

lines.original: οὐ γὰρ παυσωλή γε μετέσσεται οὐδʼ ἠβαιὸν
lines.english: For there will be no respite at all, not even a little.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** παυσωλή (noun, nom. sg. fem.) "respite, pause"; μετέσσεται (verb, 3rd sg. fut. mid.) "will come between, intervene"; οὐδʼ ἠβαιόν (adv.) "not even a little, not at all." 

The line asserts that there will be no respite or pause, not even briefly, in the coming battle—emphasizing the relentless nature of the combat until nightfall intervenes.

lines.original: εἰ μὴ νὺξ ἐλθοῦσα διακρινέει μένος ἀνδρῶν.
lines.english: unless night coming on shall part the fury of the warriors.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** νύξ (nom. sg. fem.) "night"; ἐλθοῦσα (aor. act. ptcp. nom. sg. fem. from ἔρχομαι) "coming, having come"; διακρινέει (fut. act. 3rd sg. from διακρίνω) "will separate, will decide"; μένος (acc. sg. neut.) "fury, fighting spirit." 

The line means "unless night coming separates the fury of men"—a conditional clause indicating that only nightfall will halt the relentless battle.

lines.original: ἱδρώσει μέν τευ τελαμὼν ἀμφὶ στήθεσφιν
lines.english: The shield strap will sweat around the chest of many a man.
lines.gloss:
**ἱδρώσει** (fut. act. indic. 3rd sg. of ἱδρόω, "to sweat") "will become sweaty"; **τευ** (enclitic indef. pronoun gen. sg., "of someone") "of someone"; **τελαμών** (nom. sg., "shoulder-strap, baldric") "the shield-strap"; **ἀμφί** (prep. + dat., "around") "around"; **στήθεσφιν** (dat. pl. of στῆθος, "chest, breast") "the chest." 

The shield-strap of someone will become sweaty around his chest (from the exertion of battle).

lines.original: ἀσπίδος ἀμφιβρότης, περὶ δʼ ἔγχεϊ χεῖρα καμεῖται·
lines.english: The shield-strap around both shoulders, and the hand will weary around the spear.
lines.gloss:
**ἀσπίδος ἀμφιβρότης, περὶ δʼ ἔγχεϊ χεῖρα καμεῖται·**

*ἀσπίδος* (gen. sg. of ἀσπίς): "of the shield," dependent on ἀμφιβρότης. *ἀμφιβρότης* (nom. sg. adj.): "covering both sides," or "worn around," epithet describing the shield-strap. *ἔγχεϊ* (dat. sg. of ἔγχος): "with the spear," instrumental dative. *χεῖρα* (acc. sg. of χείρ): "hand," subject accusative. *καμεῖται* (3rd sg. fut. mid. of κάμνω): "will grow

lines.original: ἱδρώσει δέ τευ ἵππος ἐΰξοον ἅρμα τιταίνων.
lines.english: His horse will sweat straining to pull the well-built chariot.
lines.gloss: **ἱδρώσει** (future, 3rd sing. of ἱδρόω): "will sweat" — the horse laboring in battle. **τευ** (enclitic genitive, σύ): "of someone/anyone" — indefinite possessive. **ἐΰξοον** (adjective, acc. sing. neut.): "well-polished" — modifying ἅρμα. **ἅρμα** (noun, acc. sing. neut.): "chariot" — object being pulled. **τιταίνων** (present participle, nom. sing. masc. of τιταίνω): "straining/pulling" — the horse's exertion. The verse describes a warrior's horse sweating as it strains to pull the polished chariot.

lines.original: ὃν δέ κʼ ἐγὼν ἀπάνευθε μάχης ἐθέλοντα νοήσω
lines.english: But whomever I notice willingly holding back from the battle
lines.gloss:
**ὃν δέ κʼ ἐγὼν ἀπάνευθε μάχης ἐθέλοντα νοήσω**

**ὃν** (relative pronoun, acc. sing. masc.) "whom"; **κε** (particle) modal "κέ" (= ἄν); **ἀπάνευθε** (adverb/preposition + gen.) "far from, away from"; **ἐθέλοντα** (present participle, acc. sing. masc. from ἐθέλω) "willing, wishing"; **νοήσω** (1st sing. aor. subjunctive from νοέω) "I perceive, notice." "But whomever I perceive wishing (to remain) away from battle..."

lines.original: μιμνάζειν παρὰ νηυσὶ κορωνίσιν, οὔ οἱ ἔπειτα
lines.english: lingering by the beaked ships, for him there shall not then
lines.gloss: **μιμνάζειν** (pres. inf., μίμνω): "to remain, linger"; **παρὰ νηυσὶ κορωνίσιν** (prep. + dat. pl.): "beside the curved ships" (*κορωνίς* = curved, beaked); **οὔ οἱ** (neg. adv. + dat. sg. pronoun): "not for him"; **ἔπειτα** (adv.): "thereafter, then." Agamemnon threatens that whoever he finds lingering by the ships will find no escape from dogs and vultures (anticipating the next line).

lines.original: ἄρκιον ἐσσεῖται φυγέειν κύνας ἠδʼ οἰωνούς.
lines.english: It will not be enough for him to escape the dogs and birds of prey.
lines.gloss:
**ἄρκιον** (neuter nominative singular, adjective): "sufficient," "enough" – serving as predicate with ἐσσεῖται. **ἐσσεῖται** (3rd singular future of εἰμί): "will be" – future indicative forming impersonal construction. **φυγέειν** (aorist active infinitive of φεύγω): "to escape," "to flee" – complementing ἄρκιον in an infinitive construction. **κύνας** (masculine accusative plural): "dogs" – direct object of φυγέειν. **οἰωνούς** (masculine accusative plural): "birds," "vultures" – second object coordinated with κύνας.

The line states "it will be sufficient to escape the dogs and birds (of prey)," expressing the hope of avoiding becoming carrion.

lines.original: Ζεῦ κύδιστε μέγιστε κελαινεφὲς αἰθέρι ναίων
lines.english: Zeus most glorious and greatest, dweller in the dark clouds of heaven
lines.gloss: **Ζεῦ** (vocative of Ζεύς) "Zeus"; **κύδιστε** (vocative superlative adjective) "most glorious"; **μέγιστε** (vocative superlative adjective) "greatest"; **κελαινεφές** (vocative compound adjective, κελαιν- "dark" + νεφ- "cloud") "dark-clouded"; **ναίων** (present active participle, nominative masculine singular of ναίω) "dwelling." An invocation to Zeus with accumulated epithets: the greatest and most glorious god who dwells in the dark-clouded upper air.

lines.original: μὴ πρὶν ἐπʼ ἠέλιον δῦναι καὶ ἐπὶ κνέφας ἐλθεῖν
lines.english: Let not the sun set and darkness come on before
lines.gloss: Key words: **πρίν** (adverb) "before"; **ἠέλιον** (accusative singular of ἠέλιος) "sun," object of ἐπί; **δῦναι** (aorist infinitive of δύω) "to set, go down"; **κνέφας** (accusative singular neuter) "darkness," object of ἐπί; **ἐλθεῖν** (aorist infinitive of ἔρχομαι) "to come." The line means "let not the sun set and darkness come before [I accomplish my goal]," with the doubled ἐπί governing both infinitive clauses.

lines.original: πρίν με κατὰ πρηνὲς βαλέειν Πριάμοιο μέλαθρον
lines.english: before I cast down headlong the palace of Priam
lines.gloss: **πρίν** (adv.) "before" governs the infinitives; **κατὰ πρηνὲς** (adv. phrase, neut. acc.) "headlong/forward, prostrate" modifies **βαλέειν** (aor. act. inf. of βάλλω) "to cast down, hurl"; **Πριάμοιο μέλαθρον** (gen. + acc.) "Priam's hall/palace." The speaker vows not to stop before casting Priam's palace headlong (i.e., destroying it completely).

lines.original: αἰθαλόεν, πρῆσαι δὲ πυρὸς δηΐοιο θύρετρα,
lines.english: to burn it black with smoke and consume its gates with ravaging fire
lines.gloss: **αἰθαλόεν** (acc. sing. masc. participle, *αἰθαλόω*) "blackened with soot, smoke-begrimed" — modifies μέλαθρον from the previous line, describing Priam's palace. **πρῆσαι** (aor. inf., *πίμπρημι*) "to burn, set ablaze" — dependent on an implied verb of necessity or desire. **πυρός** (gen. sing., *πῦρ*) "of fire" — genitive of material. **δηΐοιο** (gen. sing., *δήϊος*) "hostile, destructive" — modifies πυρός. **θύρετρα** (acc. pl. neut., *θύρετρον*) "doorways, gates" — direct object of πρῆσαι.

lines.original: Ἑκτόρεον δὲ χιτῶνα περὶ στήθεσσι δαΐξαι
lines.english: and to rend Hector's tunic about his chest with bronze.
lines.gloss: **Ἑκτόρεον** (adjective, masculine accusative singular) "of Hector, Hector's"; **χιτῶνα** (noun, masculine accusative singular) "tunic, corselet"; **στήθεσσι** (noun, neuter dative plural) "upon the chest/breast"; **δαΐξαι** (verb, aorist active infinitive of *δαΐζω*) "to tear, rend, rip apart." The infinitive continues the dependent construction from the previous lines, expressing the speaker's desire to rend Hector's tunic upon his chest.

lines.original: χαλκῷ ῥωγαλέον· πολέες δʼ ἀμφʼ αὐτὸν ἑταῖροι
lines.english: with bronze jagged-edged, and many comrades around him fell forward in the dust biting the earth.
lines.gloss: **χαλκῷ** (dative singular, "with bronze"): instrumental dative indicating the weapon. **ῥωγαλέον** (accusative singular adjective, "jagged, torn"): describes the tunic rent by bronze. **πολέες** (nominative plural, "many"): subject describing numerous companions. **ἑταῖροι** (nominative plural, "companions"): Hector's comrades who surround and protect him. The line depicts Hector's torn tunic and the protective circle of his many comrades around him.

lines.original: πρηνέες ἐν κονίῃσιν ὀδὰξ λαζοίατο γαῖαν.
lines.english: falling headlong in the dust they might bite the earth with their teeth
lines.gloss: **πρηνέες** (adj. nom. pl. masc.): "face-forward, headlong," describing the fallen companions. **κονίῃσιν** (noun dat. pl. fem.): "in the dust," from κονίη. **ὀδάξ** (adv.): "with the teeth, biting," intensifying the image of death. **λαζοίατο** (verb 3rd pl. aor. mid. opt.): "might seize, bite," from λάζομαι. **γαῖαν** (noun acc. sg. fem.): "the earth, ground." The companions lie headlong in the dust, biting the earth in death—a vivid Homeric formula for violent death in battle.

lines.original: Ἀτρεΐδη κύδιστε ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγάμεμνον,
lines.english: Son of Atreus most glorious Agamemnon lord of men
lines.gloss: **Ἀτρεΐδη** (vocative singular, "son of Atreus"), **κύδιστε** (vocative singular superlative adjective, "most glorious"), **ἄναξ** (vocative singular noun, "lord, king"), **ἀνδρῶν** (genitive plural, "of men"), **Ἀγάμεμνον** (vocative, "Agamemnon"). This is a formal address to Agamemnon using traditional epic epithets: "Son of Atreus, most glorious lord of men, Agamemnon."

lines.original: μηκέτι νῦν δήθʼ αὖθι λεγώμεθα, μηδʼ ἔτι δηρὸν
lines.english: Let us no longer linger here nor delay any further.
lines.gloss:
**μηκέτι** (adverb): "no longer," negating further delay. **νῦν** (adverb): "now," emphasizing immediate action. **δήθ(α)** (adverb): "for a long time," reinforcing the prohibition of lingering. **λεγώμεθα** (1st pl. pres. middle subjunctive, λέγω): "let us gather/converse," hortatory subjunctive negated to mean "let us not delay in gathering/talking." **δηρόν** (adverb, accusative of duration): "for a long time," further emphasizing avoidance of protracted delay.

The speaker urges immediate action, rejecting any further postponement through deliberation or assembly.

lines.original: ἀμβαλλώμεθα ἔργον ὃ δὴ θεὸς ἐγγυαλίζει.
lines.english: Let us delay the task which the god now places in our hands.
lines.gloss: **ἀμβαλλώμεθα** (1st pl. pres. mid. subj. of ἀναβάλλω) "let us postpone"; **ἔργον** (acc. sg. neut. noun) "the task, work"; **θεός** (nom. sg. masc. noun) "god, the god"; **ἐγγυαλίζει** (3rd sg. pres. act. indic. of ἐγγυαλίζω) "entrusts, puts into (our) hands." Hector urges the Trojans not to delay the task/battle that god now places before them, creating urgency for immediate action rather than continued deliberation.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ ἄγε κήρυκες μὲν Ἀχαιῶν χαλκοχιτώνων
lines.english: But come, let the heralds of the bronze-clad Achaeans
lines.gloss: **ἀλλʼ ἄγε** (ἀλλά + ἄγε): "but come!" - standard exhortation introducing a command. **κήρυκες** (nom. pl. of κῆρυξ): "heralds" - subject of implied verb. **Ἀχαιῶν** (gen. pl. of Ἀχαιός): "of the Achaeans" - possessive genitive modifying heralds. **χαλκοχιτώνων** (gen. pl. adj. from χαλκοχίτων): "bronze-clad" - compound epithet (χαλκός + χιτών) modifying Achaeans, describing their bronze armor.

lines.original: λαὸν κηρύσσοντες ἀγειρόντων κατὰ νῆας,
lines.english: Let the heralds gather the people throughout the ships by their proclamations.
lines.gloss:
**λαὸν** (acc. sing. masc., "people/host") — the object of the heralds' gathering activity. **κηρύσσοντες** (pres. part. nom. pl. masc., "proclaiming/making proclamation") — describes the heralds' activity as they gather the troops. **ἀγειρόντων** (3rd pl. pres. impv., "let them gather") — imperative directing the heralds to assemble the army. **νῆας** (acc. pl. fem., "ships") — locative destination, where the gathering occurs.

The line commands that the heralds gather the host by making proclamation throughout the camp near the ships.

lines.original: ἡμεῖς δʼ ἀθρόοι ὧδε κατὰ στρατὸν εὐρὺν Ἀχαιῶν
lines.english: Meanwhile we here throughout the wide host of the Achaeans gathered together
lines.gloss:
**ἡμεῖς** (pronoun, nom. pl.) "we" – subject emphasizing the leaders' collective action in contrast to the heralds. **ἀθρόοι** (adj., nom. pl. masc.) "gathered together, in a body" – predicative, describing their unified movement. **κατὰ στρατόν** (prep. + acc.) "throughout the army" – indicating distribution across the camp. **εὐρύν** (adj., acc. sg. masc.) "wide, broad" – modifying στρατόν, emphasizing the army's extent. 

The leaders will move collectively throughout the broad Achaean army while the heralds summon the troops.

lines.original: ἴομεν ὄφρα κε θᾶσσον ἐγείρομεν ὀξὺν Ἄρηα.
lines.english: Let us go so that we may more swiftly rouse sharp Ares.
lines.gloss:
**ἴομεν** (1st pl. pres. subj. of εἶμι) "let us go"; **ὄφρα** (conj.) "so that, in order that"; **θᾶσσον** (comparative adv. from ταχύς) "more quickly, swiftly"; **ἐγείρομεν** (1st pl. pres. subj. of ἐγείρω) "we may rouse, stir up"; **ὀξὺν Ἄρηα** (acc. sg., "sharp/keen Ares") metonymy for battle or war. 

The speaker urges the assembled Achaean army to proceed together in order to more swiftly kindle fierce battle.

lines.original: ὦ γέρον αἰεί τοι μῦθοι φίλοι ἄκριτοί εἰσιν,
lines.english: Old man, your words are always rash and undiscerning.
lines.gloss:
**ὦ γέρον αἰεί τοι μῦθοι φίλοι ἄκριτοί εἰσιν**

**γέρον** (vocative singular, γέρων) "old man"; **αἰεί** (adverb) "always"; **μῦθοι** (nominative plural, μῦθος) "words, speeches"; **ἄκριτοί** (nominative plural masculine, ἄκριτος) "ill-considered, injudicious"; **εἰσιν** (3rd plural present, εἰμί) "are." A rebuke: "Old man, your words are always dear (to you) but ill-considered."

lines.original: ὥς ποτʼ ἐπʼ εἰρήνης· πόλεμος δʼ ἀλίαστος ὄρωρεν.
lines.english: as once in time of peace, but unceasing war has arisen.
lines.gloss:
**ὥς** (adverb): "thus, so" - introduces the comparison with a former state of peace.

**ἐπʼ εἰρήνης** (preposition + genitive noun, feminine singular): "in time of peace" - ἐπί with genitive indicates temporal setting; εἰρήνης from εἰρήνη.

**πόλεμος** (noun, nominative singular masculine): "war" - subject of the clause contrasting with peace.

**ἀλίαστος** (adjective, nominative singular masculine): "unceasing, incessant" - modifies πόλεμος, from ἀ-privative + λίαστος.

**ὄρωρεν** (verb, perfect active indicative 3rd singular): "has arisen, has broken out" - from ὄρνυμι; the perfect emphas

lines.original: ἤδη μὲν μάλα πολλὰ μάχας εἰσήλυθον ἀνδρῶν,
lines.english: I have entered very many battles of men already,
lines.gloss: **ἤδη** (adverb): "already, by now"; **μάλα πολλὰ** (adverb + neuter plural accusative of πολύς): "very many" (adverbial accusative of extent); **μάχας** (accusative plural of μάχη): "battles"; **εἰσήλυθον** (1st singular aorist indicative of εἰσέρχομαι): "I have entered, I have gone into"; **ἀνδρῶν** (genitive plural of ἀνήρ): "of men." The speaker declares that he has already entered very many battles of men.

lines.original: ἀλλʼ οὔ πω τοιόνδε τοσόνδέ τε λαὸν ὄπωπα·
lines.english: but never yet have I seen such a great host as this.
lines.gloss:
**Iliad 2.799** (Nestor speaking of the assembled Greek host)

**ἀλλʼ** (ἀλλά): conjunction, "but"
**οὔ πω**: negative adverb with enclitic particle, "not yet, never yet"
**τοιόνδε**: demonstrative adjective, accusative singular masculine (modifying λαόν), "such (as this)"
**τοσόνδέ**: demonstrative adjective, accusative singular masculine (modifying λαόν), "so great, so large"
**λαόν**: accusative singular of λαός, "host, army, people"
**ὄπωπα**: perfect active indicative, 1st singular of ὁράω, "I have seen"

Nestor declares that despite entering many battles, he has never yet seen such a vast host as this Greek army.

lines.original: λίην γὰρ φύλλοισιν ἐοικότες ἢ ψαμάθοισιν
lines.english: For they are truly like leaves or grains of sand.
lines.gloss:
**λίην** (adv.): "very much," "exceedingly" — intensifies the comparison that follows.

**φύλλοισιν** (dat. pl. neut., from φύλλον): "leaves" — dative of comparison with ἐοικότες.

**ἐοικότες** (perf. act. ptcp. nom. pl. masc., from ἔοικα): "resembling," "like" — governs dative of comparison.

**ψαμάθοισιν** (dat. pl. fem., from ψάμαθος): "grains of sand" — second term of comparison, paired with φύλλοισιν.

The speaker describes the Trojan forces as exceedingly numerous, comparing them to leaves or grains of sand in a traditional epic simile for vast multitudes.

lines.original: ἔρχονται πεδίοιο μαχησόμενοι προτὶ ἄστυ.
lines.english: They come across the plain to fight before the city.
lines.gloss: **ἔρχονται** (ἔρχομαι, 3rd pl. pres. mid./pass. indic.) "they come, they advance"; **πεδίοιο** (πεδίον, gen. sg. neut.) "of the plain"; **μαχησόμενοι** (μάχομαι, nom. pl. masc. fut. mid. participle) "about to fight, intending to fight"; **προτί** (preposition + acc.) "toward"; **ἄστυ** (ἄστυ, acc. sg. neut.) "the city." The warriors advance across the plain intending to fight toward the city.

lines.original: Ἕκτορ σοὶ δὲ μάλιστʼ ἐπιτέλλομαι, ὧδε δὲ ῥέξαι·
lines.english: Hector, to you above all I give charge, and do as follows:
lines.gloss: **Ἕκτορ** (Hektor): vocative, direct address to Hektor. **σοί** (soi): dative singular pronoun "to you," emphasizing personal responsibility. **μάλιστα** (malista): adverb "especially, most of all," intensifying the command. **ἐπιτέλλομαι** (epitellomai): first singular middle present indicative of ἐπιτέλλω, "I enjoin, command." **ῥέξαι** (rhexai): aorist active infinitive of ῥέζω, "to do, accomplish," completing the imperatival instruction.

lines.original: πολλοὶ γὰρ κατὰ ἄστυ μέγα Πριάμου ἐπίκουροι,
lines.english: For many allies of great Priam are throughout the city.
lines.gloss: **πολλοὶ** (adj. nom. masc. pl., "many") **κατὰ** (prep. + acc., "throughout") **ἄστυ** (noun acc. neut. sg., "city") **μέγα** (adj. acc. neut. sg., "great") **Πριάμου** (proper name gen. sg., "of Priam") **ἐπίκουροι** (noun nom. masc. pl., "allies, auxiliaries"). The line explains that many allies of Priam are distributed throughout his great city, setting up the observation about their diverse languages in the following verse.

lines.original: ἄλλη δʼ ἄλλων γλῶσσα πολυσπερέων ἀνθρώπων·
lines.english: The allies had different tongues, for they were gathered from many lands.
lines.gloss: **γλῶσσα** (nom. sg. fem. noun): "tongue, language" – subject of the clause. **ἄλλη δʼ ἄλλων** (nom. sg. fem. adj. + gen. pl. masc. adj.): "different (tongue) of different (men)" – expressing linguistic diversity through anaphora. **πολυσπερέων** (gen. pl. masc. pres. part. of πολυσπείρω): "scattered far and wide, dispersed" – modifying ἀνθρώπων, describing the geographical distribution of Priam's allies. This line emphasizes the multilingual nature of Troy's coalition forces, explaining why each commander must address his own contingent.

lines.original: τοῖσιν ἕκαστος ἀνὴρ σημαινέτω οἷσί περ ἄρχει,
lines.english: Let each man give orders to those over whom he rules.
lines.gloss: **τοῖσιν** (demonstrative pronoun, dative plural): "to these," referring to the various ethnic groups. **ἕκαστος** (adjective, nominative singular masculine): "each," emphasizing individual leaders. **ἀνὴρ** (noun, nominative singular): "man" or "leader." **σημαινέτω** (verb, 3rd singular present imperative active): "let him give signals/orders," from σημαίνω. **ἄρχει** (verb, 3rd singular present active indicative): "he rules/commands," from ἄρχω. The line instructs that each leader should give commands to those troops over whom he has authority, addressing the multilingual nature of Agamemnon's coalition army.

lines.original: τῶν δʼ ἐξηγείσθω κοσμησάμενος πολιήτας.
lines.english: and let him lead them after marshaling his townsmen.
lines.gloss:
**Key words:** τῶν (demonstrative genitive plural, "of these/them"), ἐξηγείσθω (present middle imperative 3rd singular of ἐξηγέομαι, "let him lead"), κοσμησάμενος (aorist middle participle masculine nominative singular of κοσμέω, "having arranged/marshaled"), πολιήτας (accusative plural of πολιήτης, "citizens/townsmen"). 

The line commands: "And let each man lead forth his townsmen, having arranged them in order," continuing instructions for commanders to organize their contingents for battle or assembly.

english_paragraphs: Now the other gods and the armed warriors on the plain slept soundly, but Zeus was wakeful, for he was thinking how to do honor to Achilles, and destroy many people at the ships of the Achaeans.
In the end he deemed it would be best to send a lying dream to King Agamemnon; so he called one to him and said to it, "Lying Dream, go to the ships of the Achaeans,

Troy into the tent of Agamemnon, and say to him word to word as I now bid you. Tell him to get the Achaeans instantly under arms, for he shall take. There are no longer divided counsels among the gods;

Hera has brought them to her own mind, and woe betides the Trojans." The dream went when it had heard its message, and soon reached the ships of the Achaeans. It sought Agamemnon son of Atreus and found him in his tent, wrapped in a profound slumber.
It hovered over his head in the likeness of Nestor, son of Neleus, whom Agamemnon honored above all his councilors, and said: - "You are sleeping, son of Atreus;

one who has the welfare of his host and so much other care upon his shoulders should dock his sleep. Hear me at once, for I come as a messenger from Zeus, who, though he be not near, yet takes thought for you and pities you. He bids you get the Achaeans instantly under arms, for you shall take

Troy. There are no longer divided counsels among the gods; Hera has brought them over to her own mind, and woe betides the Trojans at the hands of Zeus. Remember this, and when you wake see that it does not escape you."

The dream then left him, and he thought of things that were, surely not to be accomplished. He thought that on that same day he was to take the city of Priam, but he little knew what was in the mind of Zeus, who had many another

hard-fought fight in store alike for Danaans and Trojans. Then presently he woke, with the divine message still ringing in his ears; so he sat upright, and put on his soft shirt so fair and new, and over this his heavy cloak. He bound his sandals on to his comely feet,

Olympus and slung his silver-studded sword about his shoulders; then he took the imperishable staff of his father, and sallied forth to the ships of the Achaeans. The goddess Dawn now wended her way to vastthat she might herald day to Zeus and to the other immortals,

Pylos and Agamemnon sent the criers round to call the people in assembly; so they called them and the people gathered thereon. But first he summoned a meeting of the elders at the ship of Nestor king of,

and when they were assembled he laid a cunning counsel before them. "My friends," said he, "I have had a dream from heaven in the dead of night, and its face and figure resembled none but Nestor's. It hovered over my head and said,

‘You are sleeping, son of Atreus; one who has the welfare of his host and so much other care upon his shoulders should dock his sleep. Hear me at once, for I am a messenger from Zeus, who, though he be not near, yet takes thought for you and pities you.

Troy He bids you get the Achaeans instantly under arms, for you shall take. There are no longer divided counsels among the gods; Hera has brought them over to her own mind, and woe betides the Trojans

themis at the hands of Zeus. Remember this.’ The dream then vanished and I awoke. Let us now, therefore, arm the sons of the Achaeans. But it will be the right thing [] that I should first sound them, and to this end I will tell them to flee with their ships;

Pylos but do you others go about among the host and prevent their doing so." He then sat down, and Nestor the king ofwith all sincerity and goodwill addressed them thus: "My friends," said he, "princes and councilors of the Argives,

if any other man of the Achaeans had told us of this dream we should have declared it false, and would have had nothing to do with it. But he who has seen it is the foremost man among us; we must therefore set about getting the people under arms." With this he led the way from the assembly,

and the other sceptered kings rose with him in obedience to the word of Agamemnon; but the people pressed forward to hear. They swarmed like bees that sally from some hollow cave and flit in countless throng among the spring flowers,

bunched in knots and clusters; even so did the mighty multitude pour from ships and tents to the assembly, and range themselves upon the wide-watered shore, while among them ran Wildfire Rumor, messenger of Zeus, urging them ever to the fore.

Thus they gathered in a pell-mell of mad confusion, and the earth groaned under the tramp of men as the people sought their places. Nine heralds went crying about among them to stay their tumult and bid them listen to the kings, till at last they were got into their several places and ceased their clamor.

Argos Then King Agamemnon rose, holding his scepter. This was the work of Hephaistos, who gave it to Zeus the son of Kronos. Zeus gave it to Hermes, slayer of, guide and guardian. King Hermes gave it to Pelops, the mighty charioteer, and

with those that held Asterios, and the white crests of Titanus, these were led by Eurypylos, the son of Euaemon, and with them there came forty ships. Those that held Argissa and Gyrtone, Orthe, Elone, and the white city of Oloosson,

of these brave Polypoites was leader. He was son of Peirithoos, who was son of Zeus himself, for Hippodameia bore him to Peirithoos on the day when he took his revenge on the shaggy mountain savages and drove them from Mount Pelion to the Aithikes.

But Polypoites was not sole in command, for with him was Leonteus, of the race of Ares, who was son of Koronos, the son of Kaineus. And with these there came forty ships. Guneus brought two and twenty ships from Cyphus, and he was followed by the Enienes and the valiant Peraebi,

Dodona who dwelt about wintry, and held the lands round the lovely river Titaresios, which sends its waters into the Peneus. They do not mingle with the silver eddies of the Peneus, but flow on the top of them like oil;

for the Titaresios is a branch of dread Orcus and of the river Styx. Of the Magnetes, Prothoos son of Tenthredon was commander. They were they that dwelt about the river Peneus and Mount Pelion. Prothoos, fleet of foot, was their leader, and with him there came forty ships.

Such were the chiefs and princes of the Danaans. Who, then, O Muse, was the foremost, whether man or horse, among those that followed after the sons of Atreus? Of the horses, those of the son of Pheres were by far the finest. They were driven by Eumelos, and were as fleet as birds.

They were of the same age and color, and perfectly matched in height. Apollo, of the silver bow, had bred them in Perea - both of them mares, and terrible as Ares in battle. Of the men, Ajax, son of Telamon, was much the foremost so long as Achilles' anger lasted, for Achilles excelled him greatly

and he had also better horses; but Achilles was now holding aloof at his ships by reason of his quarrel with Agamemnon, and his people passed their time upon the sea shore, throwing discs or aiming with spears at a mark,

and in archery. Their horses stood each by his own chariot, champing lotus and wild celery. The chariots were housed under cover, but their owners, for lack of leadership, wandered hither and thither about the host and went not forth to fight.

Thus marched the host like a consuming fire, and the earth groaned beneath them when the lord of thunder is angry and lashes the land about Typhoeus among the Arimi, where they say Typhoeus lies. Even so did the earth groan beneath them
as they sped over the plain. And now Iris, fleet as the wind, was sent by Zeus to tell the bad news among the Trojans. They were gathered in assembly, old and young, at Priam's gates,

and Iris came close up to Priam, speaking with the voice of Priam's son Polites, who, being fleet of foot, was stationed as watchman for the Trojans on the tomb of old Aisyetes, to look out for any sally of the Achaeans.

In his likeness Iris spoke, saying, "Old man, you talk idly, as in time of peace, while war is at hand. I have been in many a battle, but never yet saw such a host as is now advancing. They are crossing the plain to attack the city as

thick as leaves or as the sands of the sea. Hektor, I charge you above all others, do as I say. There are many allies dispersed about the city of Priam from distant places and speaking divers tongues.

Therefore, let each chief give orders to his own people, setting them severally in array and leading them forth to battle." Thus she spoke, but Hektor knew that it was the goddess, and at once broke up the assembly. The men flew to arms; all the gates were opened, and the people thronged through them,

sêma horse and foot, with the tramp as of a great multitude. Now there is a high mound before the city, rising by itself upon the plain. Men call it Batieia, but the gods know that it is the tomb [] of lithe Myrrhine.
